### 1.168 Slice A35-S2 (0.12.x): settle gate: after a listed return-home failure the ladder probes the screen, and while it still changes it holds instead of restarting (#411 A35; design `rd-1021/train-0129/a35-design.md` §2.1, §3, §4.3, §5.1 S2, §5.3; coordinator decisions of 2026-10-21, Q8 revised: the frame-change measure of §1.155)

The A35 incident: an instance was in a long activity that ends by itself, its return-home package
did not know the activity's screen and failed `contained_task_page_unknown`, and the ladder went
on to the application restart at once and closed the application in the middle of it. After a
return-home failure of a listed ladder class, the ladder now probes the screen with read-only
frames and compares consecutive frames by the Runtime's one frame-change measure (§1.155 B12,
[color-digest.md](color-digest.md), "Frame change"; no second measure, no thumbnail similarity):
a settled screen is climbed past as before, a changing one is held within a configured limit.
[emulator-control.md](emulator-control.md) ("Settle gate", "Records") is the contract,
[runtime-config.md](runtime-config.md) the keys'. **No persisted ledger shape** (design §7): the
verdicts are recorded with the existing `recovery_rung_finished` and `recovery_ladder_finished`
phases and one new code; the probe's frames are ordinary read-only captures; the frame-change
digest is memory only. Gates: host keys 156 to 161.

### 1.169 Slice A35-S4 (0.12.x): a busy end of an entry layer ends the run (#411 A35, B37 entry part; design `rd-1021/train-0129/a35-design.md` §2.2 "Entry extension", §5.1 S4, §5.3; coordinator decision Q5 of 2026-10-21)

A35 seen from a run's entry: a run that starts while its instance shows an activity that ends by
itself runs its home entry's return-home layer, or a step of its navigation recovery chain, and
that layer ends on the activity page under a `busy` mapping (§1.152 B37-1). Before, the home entry
failed `contained_task_home_recovery_terminal_non_home` (`pack_logic_mismatch`, which starts the
ladder) and the navigation located again and ran the chain's next step, which may restart the
application. Now such an end ends the run. [linear-steps.md](linear-steps.md) ("Ladder and
page-graph home entry") and [package-reference.md](package-reference.md) (the navigation's
"Recovery chain") are the contract. **No persisted ledger shape**: the existing
`EntryRecoveryCompleted`, fail-closed `EntryTargetDisposition` and terminal records carry one new
code; no configuration key, no location, no package member (S1's `busy` is read). Gates: host
keys 162, 163 (164 unused).

| B37E-2 | a home entry's return-home layer that completed on a `busy` mapping | rule (no shape change) (host 162) | A35-S4 | A35-S4 | the run ends with B37E-1 after the layer's `EntryRecoveryCompleted`, in place of `contained_task_home_recovery_terminal_non_home`: no recheck, no navigation; the mapping is the one `no_designated_effect` mapping that lists the final page (the condition a layer reaches); a `linear_steps` return-home package too; a request's own recovery package declares no `scheduling_outcome`, so only the registry's package can end so |
| B37E-3 | a navigation recovery chain step that completed on a `busy` mapping | rule (no shape change) (host 163) | A35-S4 | A35-S4 | the run ends with B37E-1 after the step's `EntryRecoveryCompleted`, the gate closed fail-closed: the run does not locate again and the chain's next step is neither admitted nor run; a hop's layer and every other layer are unchanged |

unused: the status block is built in the host crate, and the frame gives a family the row does
not list the numbers `300 + 10 × row`).

### 1.173 Slice A44 writer (0.12.x): the recognition record lists every candidate page's best score and verdict (#411 A44; coordinator 10-21 00:2x; ledger revision 4, §1.153 LR-8)

The recognition record listed the targets of one page only (the matched page, else the first
candidate page), so it could not show why the other candidate pages did not match. **Persisted
shape:** this slice is the writer of ledger revision 4 row LR-8 (§1.153), `candidate_scores` of
`task.recognition_completed`, written as registered there; no other persisted member. The paired
`recognition.completed` payload is unchanged and `ledger` stays [3, 4]. The kernel hands the
verdicts to the host in memory, on its in-process recognition trace. It reports only what the
recognition already evaluates: every candidate page is evaluated today (the page detector's batch
evaluates every listed page and a recognition needs every page's evaluation; none stops at the
first match), and inside a page a lazy target is skipped once the page is ruled out (Workflow
#396 REC-6). No code, location, key, vocabulary token, wire, package member or configuration key
is added. Gates: exec keys 171 and 172, host key 174 (exec 173 and 174 unused).

### 1.175 Slice FLK07-FIX (0.12.x): a resource-close lease the instance's queue refuses fails only the capture's work and no longer halts the Runtime (#411 A52; FLK-07's cause, board #71; coordinator 10-22 11:1x)

CI run 39708910434 ran FLK-07 (`capture_failure::readonly_failures_are_visible_and_terminal_without_fake_success`)
20 times: 4 rounds latched `lease_transfer_not_safe` (`prepare_resource_close_lease`,
`host_halted=true`). A read-only observe holds the instance's admission guard while it captures,
so a Runtime claim that arrives meanwhile waits in the instance's queue; when the capture failed,
its close asked for a dedicated resource-close lease, the waiting entry refused it (Workflow #369
§5.1) and the close path made the refusal the Runtime's fatal. In production one instance's failing
observes could stop the whole Runtime while another request waited.
[read-session-resource-close.md](read-session-resource-close.md) is the contract. **No persisted
shape**: the refusal is an existing record (`runtime.failed`) of an existing code
(`lease_transfer_not_safe`) at an existing location (`prepare_resource_close_lease`); no code,
key, vocabulary token, configuration key, location or package member. Gates: host keys 171, 172
(173 unused).

| # | Shape | Kind | Code slice | First writer | Notes |

| A52-2 | every other failure of that close | rule (unchanged) (host 172) | FLK07-FIX | — | keeps its fatality: a close attempted under an expired or otherwise invalid lease or an unresolved destructive step retains failure and owner protection, a ledger failure ends the Runtime; an unconfirmed close of the instance's own resources fences it (#403) |

### 1.176 Slice A35-S3 (0.12.x): a wait step without input, and a confirmation's wait page (#411 B36, B19; design `rd-1021/train-0129/a35-design.md` §2.3, §5.1 S3, §7; Alice's B19 decision of 2026-10-20; coordinator decisions Q9 to Q11 of 2026-10-21)

A run that starts on a page showing an activity that ends by itself could only fail or end at once
there (B19 problem 1, B36), and a confirmation waited out its whole timeout on any unexpected page
(B19 problem 2). Now a page-graph operation may be a wait step that makes no input and waits on its
page for its destinations, and a confirmation may declare a wait page that pauses its clock. One
kernel wait serves both, the confirmation's (`await_postcondition`), and keeps A43b's rule
(§1.160). [resource-declarations.md](resource-declarations.md) ("Wait steps and wait pages"),
[README.md](README.md) and [linear-steps.md](linear-steps.md) are the contract. **No persisted
ledger shape** (design §7): no code, no record, no configuration key, no location, no key; the step
writes the existing `StepStarted`/`StepFinished` without effect records, as a pass-over does. The
new members join `package` revision 6, which BT-PK6 declares; until then the Runtime admits them by
code. Gates: exec keys 175 to 179.

### 1.177 Slice PERF-B1 (0.12.x): a wait's own capture interval, the configured ceiling of a declared interval, and the back-off on unchanged frames (Workflow #407 B1; coordinator brief 10-24 `rd-1024/brief-perf-b1-capture.md`; Alice 10-24: performance first, #405)

A package that declares no interval captures every 50 ms plus the capture's own time (about every
0.6 s in production), and a package could declare at most 5 000 ms: a 25-minute wait took about
2 700 captures, each with its ledger events and its frame. Now a step's `expect_after.interval_ms`
(its confirmation, or a wait step's wait) may declare a slow interval for that one wait (R1; the
kernel already had the unit, only the bound held it at 5 000 ms), the bound is the configuration's
(R2), and a step's wait for a page lengthens its pause over unchanged frames (R3); a package that
declares nothing keeps its 50 ms (R4). [resource-declarations.md](resource-declarations.md)
("Capture cadence"), [runtime-config.md](runtime-config.md) ("The `execution` section"),
[README.md](README.md) and [linear-steps.md](linear-steps.md) are the contract. **No persisted
ledger shape**: no code, location, value key or vocabulary token; the refusal above the ceiling
reuses the codes admission gives a broken interval, and the effective intervals stay where they
were recorded (`EffectiveTaskTiming.capture_interval`, each operation's `interval`). The new
section adds one section fact of an existing family (B1-2). Gates: the `gate_407_b1` tests (a) to
(d), in rows of exec.toml and host.toml.

[scheduling/README.md](scheduling/README.md) ("Optional run-count bounds"),
[scheduling/v2/README.md](scheduling/v2/README.md) and the V2 `tasks` and `activity` schemas are
the contract; [remedies.md](remedies.md) (B8's `daily_remaining`, `last_daily_slot`) and
[runtime-config.md](runtime-config.md) (the ceiling of E) name the rest. **A persisted shape
changes** (SS3-3): the members of the budget receipt become optional. Every reader of the receipt
sees the change: the admission record of `policy.dispatch_admitted` and of
`policy.dispatch_completed`, the retry round of `policy.control_state_recorded`, and the global
ledger query's public projection `PublicPayload.policy_admission`, which reaches clients through
runtime-client. A receipt of a catalog that writes every bound is unchanged byte for byte, and so
is every existing catalog's identity; `ledger` stays [3, 4], the record type, its other members,
the tables and the schema strings are unchanged.

A receipt that leaves members out is written only after the resource side first leaves a bound
out. From then on a reader before 0.12.30 cannot decode it (no downgrade, Alice 10-11):

- **A Runtime before 0.12.30** refuses the ledger with `corrupt_ledger_record`. It does so at open
  when such a record lies among the newest `ledger_observer.open_verify_tail_records` rows it
  verifies. Otherwise it does so later, when the background recheck reaches the record; the
  recheck latches a Global failure and stops the Runtime with the same code. It also refuses a V2
  catalog that leaves `loop_budget` out.
- **Tools and the UI before 0.12.30** fail to decode a ledger event query page that carries such
  a receipt in `PublicPayload.policy_admission`.

No ledger revision is bumped now (the coordinator's decision of 10-29). The 0.12.30 release notes
and Workflow #428 say both:

- after the resource side first leaves a bound out, no rollback below 0.12.30 is possible;
- the resource side leaves bounds out only once every deployment runs 0.12.30 or later.

The bump comes with SS-9, which deletes the members.

No code, location, configuration key, wire or interface revision is added. The refusals reuse
`missing_required_field`, `type_mismatch` (an explicit `null`), `loop_budget_missing` and
`policy_budget_exhausted`. The number 1.212 is the coordinator's. Safety bounds are untouched:
`on_failure` retries and escalation, `scheduling.rerun.max_per_occurrence`, the recovery ladder,
the per-run deadline, in-pack loop caps and concurrency. The recognition maintenance daily
throttle (safety bound S4, `scheduling.fact_refresh.daily_limit`) relies on the `task_daily`
counter, which the Runtime keeps only because the fact refresh task writes `daily_limit`
(`fact_refresh_task`); SS-9 must keep that item or give the throttle a counter of its own. The
no-progress guard (SS-4), batch allowances (SS-6) and deleting the members (SS-9) are later
slices.

("Task Reserves"), [instance-fact-store.md](instance-fact-store.md) ("Run parameters") and
[selection-policy.md](selection-policy.md) (the in-task consumer) name it. The Runtime can work
out how much may be spent and how much is still missing, the package can read the unit price
and the dialog's cap on its screen; so the Runtime hands its part to the package at dispatch, on
Workflow #411 B8's `session.dispatch.schedule.*` channel (§1.150), with no opt-in. B8's
`daily_remaining` and `last_daily_slot` are unchanged; counts retire in SS-9. **No new persisted
ledger shape**: the values are new optional values of the pending entry
`policy_dispatch_parameters` in the existing dispatch reason chain of `policy.dispatch_intent`
(`PolicyReasonRecord` is `#[serde(transparent)]` over `Outcome`, whose `values` every 0.12 reader
keeps as a map without a key check), and the records `session.dispatch.schedule.<key>` are an
overlay of the run's instance fact snapshots, never stored. No catalog member, no package format
change, no configuration key, no outcome code, no wire or interface revision. One-way: the values
come from the pools' state (the reserve gate's projection, the resolved goals) and the task's own
`consumes`, `produces` and `reserves`; nothing reads a task's enablement, override, priority,
offset or run state. Game-neutral. The number 1.218 is the coordinator's. Review round 2 (the
coordinator's decisions on PR #1446): the recording is B8's typed values, the 64-record limit is
documented, a met goal and a task without a reserved consumed pool give no cap (as built); the
allowance is the reserve gate's own available amount, its step 3 included; `run_cap` is at most
1000; the goal term applies only when no produced pool carries a base weight and is the largest
need over the open gaps.

**Recorded bytes.** A selected dispatch of a task that reserves a pool it consumes (its allowance
is then always known and at least one run: the gate holds the candidate otherwise), or that
produces a pool an active v1 or v2 goal covers, now carries `policy_dispatch_parameters` in its
`policy.dispatch_intent` chain: a new reason when it carried none (no package parameter, no B8
opt-in), or the same reason with `spend_allowances`, `gaps_remaining` and `run_cap` added (its
developer detail rebuilt as the outcome's text, as B8 does). Every other dispatch, an opted-in B8
task's included, carries the bytes of before. In production no task declares `reserves` and none
produces toward a goal yet (`rd-1029/design-sch-state.md` §2.1; RS-2 of the plan writes them), so
nothing changes live until the resource side writes them.

**Rollback.** Runtime 0.12.30 reads the chains 0.12.31 writes: the reason decodes as every
`policy_dispatch_parameters` does, unknown values kept and never checked. A 0.12.30 host resuming
such a dispatch overlays only B8's keys, so a package that reads an SS-6 key meets an unknown fact
(`max_repeats` ends the run with `contained_task_designated_effect_cap_unresolved` before any
input). Rolling back below 0.12.31 is therefore possible; only the packages that read the new keys
lose them. The gate itself is unchanged: its step 3 now reads its pending consumption through the
helper the allowance shares (`resource_targets::pending_consumption`), with the same entries,
order and reasons.

### 1.220 Slice R-2 (0.12.31): performance keys hot, presets, defaults aligned to `adaptive` (Workflow #429 A.1 契约 1 and 2, its defaults and the R-2 entry of `rd-1029/429-A-runtime.md`; Alice's rulings 98, 99 and 110 of 10-29; coordinator work order `rd-1029/brief-r2.md`)

lanes", "`ConfigureSettings`", "Restore at start", "Rollback"),

("Shared Run Limits"), [runtime-interface.md](runtime-interface.md) (the `perf-preset` and
`ac_perf_preset` rows) and [component-interfaces.md](component-interfaces.md) (`actingd-config`
revision 22) are the contract. The number 1.220 is the coordinator's.

**What.** The console's top bar switches between three performance presets and sets "how many
tasks at most at once". Four keys become settable, each read again where it is used, and no run
in progress is cut; one configuration key, `performance.presets`, defines the presets; a pure
function of `runtime-config` names the current preset for the CLI, MCP and the console; the
defaults file becomes `adaptive`'s members. **No new persisted ledger shape**: an applied preset
is one `ConfigureSettings`, recorded as today (`command.*` records, one `host.config_overrides`
record of the existing row shape, the changed `config.parameters.<section>` records), and the new
key is one more row of `config.parameters.performance`. No outcome code (the refusal of `full` is
`config_value_invalid` with `out_of_range`; the CLI and MCP reuse `actingctl_usage_invalid`,
`arguments_invalid`, `config_facts_missing` and `invalid_fact_snapshot_record`), no request kind,
no wire change, no `runtime-client` revision. **`actingd-config` revision 22** (from [5, 21] to
[5, 22]): the optional member `presets` of the `performance` section.

**Why.** Ruling 98: a new install defaults to `adaptive` (`pace`), so the defaults file changes
the whole group (`mode` `pace`, `scheduling.parallel.enabled` `true`, `heavy_dispatch_limit.normal`
2, no `max_concurrent_runs`); changing only `mode` would show a new install as `custom`. Ruling
99: the top bar's number is the tasks run at once, `max_concurrent_runs`, not the emulators
running. Ruling 110: production keeps today's behaviour; the coordinator writes production's
default-dependent keys as online overrides at the deploy (a deploy step, not code), which needs
`mode` settable while the deploy hold still pauses every instance. This slice therefore changes no
production behaviour by itself once those overrides are written; a key an install holds no
override for takes the new default at the update, and an override it holds is kept.

**Rollback** (to 0.12.30). The configuration file: a file that does not name
`performance.presets` (acsetup and the installers never write it) is read by 0.12.30 unchanged; a
file that names it is refused by 0.12.30 at start and in `check-config` (an unknown member of the
section), so the operator removes that member before rolling back. 0.12.30's own defaults file
applies again (`mode` `observe`, `parallel.enabled` `false`) to every key without an override.
Online overrides: the rows of `performance.pacing.mode`, `.max_concurrent_runs` and
`.heavy_dispatch_limit.normal` / `.paused` this version writes have the existing row shape; 0.12.30
parses them, finds those keys not settable (and `max_concurrent_runs` not in its configuration
unless the file writes it) and drops each, `config_override_dropped`, listed in
`StartReport.instructions_dropped`; it never refuses the record, so its start does not fail, and
its next record of `host.config_overrides` no longer holds those rows (they are lost, not kept for
a later update). A row of `scheduling.parallel.enabled` (settable in 0.12.30 too) is kept, over
0.12.30's default `false` (`config_override_base_changed` when it was set over this release's
default `true`). The Runtime start does not fail, but the install's rollback `instructions` check
(`apps/actingctl/src/install/postcheck.rs`, #421 S2-IF) fails while `instructions_dropped` is not
empty, and it lists these rows and R-1's (§1.219); so before rolling back the operator clears those
keys (`actingctl config clear <key>`, a preset's rows included) or accepts that one check failing
(corrected in the 0.12.31 snapshot, 2026-10-30: this sentence said no override needed clearing
before a rollback, which holds for the Runtime start only). An operator who wants the dropped
values in 0.12.30 writes them into its configuration file.

### 1.221 Slice RR-1 (0.12.31): an immediate rerun the admission refuses no longer keeps winning its instance (production defect of v0.12.30 on 10-30 08:4x: after its instance was resumed, one task's immediate rerun was selected at every evaluation and refused `policy_retry_round_ended`, and the instance's three other eligible candidates never ran; coordinator work order `rd-1029/brief-retry-livelock.md`)

[policy-suspension.md](policy-suspension.md) ("Immediate rerun (R22)", the two RR-1 sentences) is
the contract. The number 1.221 is the coordinator's.

**What.** The evaluation offered a pair as `failure_retry_immediate` when it had a live retry
round (`immediate_retry_pairs`: its failure, the round's window, budgets and declared duration),
but the admission (`validate_immediate_retry`) also required the intent to keep the round's
activity profile and expected duration, which the evaluation never checked. The intent's expected
duration is the pair's E (SCH-M ED-2), recomputed at every evaluation: a new run sample of its
package changes it, and so does the package becoming known after a start (a round opened by the
first run after a start carries the declared duration, and that run's own preparation makes E
readable). From then on every evaluation selected the pair, the admission refused it, and its
instance ran nothing else. Now one predicate (`immediate_retry_admits`) serves both: the
evaluation offers a pair only when a dispatch on the terms its intent will carry
(`actingcommand_policy::dispatch_terms`, which the candidate builder uses too) is admitted, so a
pair whose terms drifted waits for its own trigger and cooldown. And an immediate rerun the
admission still refuses with `policy_retry_round_ended` (the window ended between the evaluation
and the admission) ends its round at once, in memory, in the pair's value record written with the
refusal, and in every replay of the recorded refusal. **No new persisted shape, no outcome code,
no configuration key, no interface revision**; no reason code is added (a withdrawn pair carries no
reason of its own: it is not offered, and its ordinary reasons, `task_cooldown_active` for one,
say why it waits).

**Why.** The contract already said a different profile or expected duration cannot use the
round's immediate permission and that window expiry ends it; the evaluation did not apply the
same rule, so it proposed a dispatch the admission was bound to refuse, at every round.

**Unchanged.** Success clears the round; budgets, backoff, suspensions, pauses, refunds and the
owed reruns of SR-2b; the one-way rule; game neutrality. A pair whose terms still match is
offered and admitted as before.

**Restart.** The withdrawal is in the pair's `policy.control_state_recorded` value record (its
`retry_round` absent), which LN-4's start loads; a start that rebuilds the decision memory from
the dispatch history withdraws the round again from the recorded refusal (`rejection.outcome`
`policy_retry_round_ended`), so the loaded and the replayed decision memory stay equal. A ledger
with such a refusal written by 0.12.30 replays to a memory without that round, where 0.12.30's
replay kept it: the only difference, and the defect's own state.

**Rollback** (to 0.12.30). Nothing to undo in the ledger or the configuration: a value record
without `retry_round` is a shape 0.12.30 writes and reads. 0.12.30's evaluation brings the defect
back for a pair whose expected duration changes while its round is open.

| # | Shape | Kind | Code slice | First writer | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RR1-1 | the evaluation's immediate reruns are those `PolicyControlState::immediate_retry_admits` admits on the terms `actingcommand_policy::evaluated_dispatch_terms` gives their intents (profile, expected duration); `validate_immediate_retry` is the same predicate on the intent's terms | behaviour (evaluation) | RR-1 | — | `dispatch_terms` (pure, policy crate) also fills the candidate's `expected_duration_ms` and `activity_profile_id`, so the evaluation and the intent cannot differ |
| RR1-2 | a `policy.dispatch_rejected` whose `rejection.outcome` is `policy_retry_round_ended` ends the retry rounds of the pair's accounting group on its instance, live (`apply_admission_events`) and in replay (`apply_dispatch_event`) | behaviour (decision memory) | RR-1 | the admission | failure streak, backoff and counts unchanged; the pair's next legal normal trigger opens a new round |

### 1.222 Slice SS-2 (0.12.32): two priority tiers, chain inheritance, the constrained-first tie-break and declared order (Alice's ruling 104, relisted on 10-29 22:16 and approved on 10-30 21:3x, Workflow #386 comment 6523113979, points 1, 2, 4 and 5; point 3, net benefit within a tier, is not built and waits for the research channel's check against ruling 100; design `rd-1029/design-sch-state.md` §4 and the SS-2 entry; coordinator work order `rd-1029/brief-ss2.md`)

[scheduling/README.md](scheduling/README.md) ("Ties and chain heads"; "Dispatch Decision Record"
items 1 and 3), [scheduling/v2/README.md](scheduling/v2/README.md) and
[standard-pack-schedule.md](standard-pack-schedule.md) ("Two priority tiers") are the contract. The
number 1.222 is the coordinator's.

**What.** (1) A game whose composed rules use more than two distinct priority values gets one
`standard_pack_priority_tiers_exceeded` warning from the composer; the root is never refused
(RS-8 collapses each game to two values). (2) A candidate whose trigger requires another task's
success (a `dependency_completed` accepting `succeeded`, reached from the root only through `all`)
ranks, while it continues that task's latest successful run (it has not served it, the
`since_own_run` test), with the `priority` and `strategic_weight_milli` of its chain head, the
task reached by walking such links up through runs that came one after the other. (3) Of
candidates equal in `promoted`, `total` and `affinity`, the one closer to losing its eligibility
goes first: fewer chances (the fewer of the runs its required thresholds and reserves still allow
by its own declared consumption and the runs that can still start before a required window or
missed-slot grace closes), then less time left, then fewer runs left; a candidate without a bound,
or whose bound meets an unknown input, has none and comes after; then more required conditions;
then (4) the earlier position in the catalog's task list. The seeded `tie_breaker` hash only orders
one task's candidates on different instances after that.

**Why.** Ruling 104: maintenance high, business normal, chain successors follow the chain head,
a tie goes to the task that would become impossible later, declared order last. The hash made a
tie depend on the evaluation's seed.

**Unchanged.** The rank value (`total`) and every term of it but the inherited priority and weight;
the score stage, the resource terms and pool weights (the one-way rule: nothing in the resource
layer reads a chain); every gate, B41's handover, the reserve gate (its allocation order takes the
same tie-break); game neutrality. **No new persisted shape, no configuration key, no catalog
member, no interface revision.** One outcome code, `standard_pack_priority_tiers_exceeded`
(warning, `declaration_error`; `game`, `count`, `limit_count`), because no code says "a game's
rules use more tiers than ruling 104 allows": `standard_pack_package_unclassified` names one
package that is not scheduled, and `standard_pack_root_invalid` refuses. Only the composer emits
it and only the resource tools list it; the Runtime's workbench records only the unclassified
warning, as before. Without a chain window and without a tie, every evaluation is byte for byte the
one of 0.12.31.

**What changes live.** In the two production `schedule.json` checked (two games, as of 10-28/29)
every rule has nearly its own priority (78 distinct values per game), so each game gets the
warning in the tools until RS-8. Their chain links (48 and 35) all have a predecessor of higher
priority than the successor, so a successor in its window ranks a little higher, never lower. A required
`dependency_completed` accepting `succeeded` or `failed` (a few) is a link too; one under an `any`
(the ordering dependencies of the slot sequences) is not.

**Rollback** (to 0.12.31). Nothing to undo: no ledger, state, catalog or configuration shape is
new, the tie-break and chain fields are developer text of in-memory decisions, and the warning is
never recorded. 0.12.31 ranks chain successors with their own priority again and breaks ties by
the seeded hash.

### 1.223 Slice SS-5 (0.12.32): a package's own unknown fact lets its task run once per unknown period (the coordinator's rule of 10-28, memory 「自读事实不能当本包的门」: a self-read fact must not gate its own package forever; Alice's ruling 100, #386 comment 6490879952: dispatch follows live account state; design `rd-1029/design-sch-state.md` §4.6 and the SS-5 entry of §5, `rd-1029/plan-state-driven.md` SS-5; coordinator work order `rd-1029/brief-ss5-lnoff1.md` SS-5)

[scheduling/README.md](scheduling/README.md) ("Self-read fact probe"; "Why A Candidate Does Not
Run"), [scheduling/v2/README.md](scheduling/v2/README.md),
[standard-pack-schedule.md](standard-pack-schedule.md) ("Self-read fact probes") and
[actingd-check-config.md](actingd-check-config.md) are the contract. The number 1.223 is the
coordinator's.

**What.** A `fact` predicate may carry `on_unknown: "probe"` (V2 only). It names a fact only the
task's own package reads (a reading mark of that package: a clear count, an activity level, a slot
count). While the fact is unknown the predicate is true once per unknown period, with `fact_probe`,
so the task runs and its run reads the fact; no fact refresh is asked for the key. The period
begins at the later of the latest occurrence of a timeline reset that clears the key and the end of
an expired reading's freshness; a successful run of the task dispatched after that serves it, and
the predicate is then false (`fact_probe` with `served_by_dispatch_unix_ms`, no wake) until a
reading, the next reset or an expiry. A failed or cancelled run serves nothing (S1's retry, backoff
and limits bound it, as for every failure). A non-probe unknown fact keeps its trigger Unknown and
asks the maintenance package for its key, as before.

**Guards.** The compiler refuses a probe no run of the task can read or whose truth would not admit
the task, each `predicate_uncomputable` at `on_unknown`: a scope other than an instance, a key that
is no reading-mark key (`resource.`, `inventory.`), a place below `not` or in the `feedback_stop`;
a V1 document is refused `unknown_field` at the member. The compiler sees no package, so the key
against the rule's own package is checked where the rule meets its package: `actinglab
standard-pack check` and `package bundle --schedule` read the package's marks with the Runtime's
metadata reader and refuse a key the package does not mark (a key only another package reads, or
none), `standard_pack_root_invalid` / `schedule_invalid` at `on_unknown` (the UPD-1 store-update
cooldown rule is checked at the same place). A `schedule.json` that writes the member requires
the subsystem `fact_unknown_probe`.

**Why.** Missing or expired, such a fact made its gate Unknown, the maintenance package cannot read
it, and only a run of the task would: a first-run deadlock; the resource side worked around it with
result keys.

**Unchanged.** Every predicate without the member, the fact refresh (its demand, keys and gates),
the ranking and every gate, placement and admission; game neutrality; the one-way rule (nothing in
the resource layer reads it). **No new configuration key, no persisted ledger or state shape, no
wire or interface revision.** One outcome code, `fact_probe` (info; `fact_key`, `unknown_reason`;
optional `served_by_dispatch_unix_ms`, whose key description now names the probe too), because no
code says "an unknown fact admits its task" or "the probe of this period was served":
`fact_time_served` belongs to `fact_time_reached` and requires its key, and the `fact_refresh_*`
codes speak of the maintenance package. One code with an optional value covers both verdicts
(#420 S4). A catalog without the member evaluates, serializes and hashes exactly as before.

**What changes live.** Nothing until the resource side writes the member (RS-5): no deployed
`schedule.json` can hold it, since 0.12.31 and every Runtime before refuse it.

**Rollback** (to 0.12.31). Before the resource side writes the member: nothing to undo, no ledger,
state, configuration or catalog shape is new and `fact_probe` is a reason of in-memory decisions
and of the existing dispatch decision records. After it: 0.12.31 does not name the subsystem
`fact_unknown_probe`, so its composer refuses that `schedule.json` (`schedule_requires_missing`),
records `standard_pack_root_invalid` and keeps the game's last good rules; roll the resource side
back with it, or drop the member first. A dispatch decision record of 0.12.32 that holds
`fact_probe` reads back on 0.12.31 as `outcome_relay_unregistered` with the spelling as
`raw_code`, as every code an older build does not list.

**Rollback correction** (release 0.12.32). An `on_unknown` member reaches the composed generation,
so 0.12.31's start compiles it wherever its decision memory names that generation; SS-2b's
rollback correction (§1.225) applies to it as well.

| SS5-1 | `fact.on_unknown` (optional, `"probe"`; `PredicateSpec::Fact`, `FactUnknownRule`, `contracts/scheduling/v2/common.schema.json`) | catalog format addition (no ledger shape) | SS-5 | the resource side (RS-5) | V2 only; instance scope, a `resource.`/`inventory.` key, in the trigger outside every `not`; absent serializes as nothing |
| SS5-2 | `fact_probe` (info / `none`; `fact_key`, `unknown_reason` required, `served_by_dispatch_unix_ms` optional) | new outcome code (`PolicyCode`, block `SS-5`) | SS-5 | the policy evaluator | layer `policy`, review `pending`; without the optional value the predicate is true, with it false and `trigger_false` follows when it decides the trigger |
| SS5-3 | `config.subsystems` row `fact_unknown_probe` (always on, `config_subsystem_always_on`) | new row value of an existing fact (no shape) | SS-5 | actingd | the composer requires it of a `schedule.json` whose rule writes the member (`FACT_UNKNOWN_PROBE_SUBSYSTEM`); named apart from the reason code `fact_probe` (SS5-2), since a subsystem name must not equal a registered outcome name (outcome guard G5) |
| SS5-4 | the cross-check of a probe's key against the reading marks of the rule's own package (`probe_keys_marked`, `standard_pack_fact_probes`) | resource-tool check (no shape) | SS-5 | `actinglab standard-pack check`, `package bundle --schedule` | `standard_pack_root_invalid`, `schedule_invalid` at `/rules/<i>/…/on_unknown`; each package read once, metadata only |

### 1.224 Slice LN-OFF-1 (0.12.32): the bounded offline opening of an SQLite ledger (Workflow #422 comments 6503130154 and 6508064467: the UI's offline face reached 12 GB in 60 s on the 8.1 GB production ledger; design `rd-1029/design-ln-off.md`, option A, §4.2 to §4.6; pending decision 115, recommendation A, with Alice's addition of 10-30 23:3x: 「我们直接限定UI每次可以读多少就行」; coordinator work order `rd-1029/brief-ss5-lnoff1.md`)

[ledger-store.md](ledger-store.md) ("Recovery, artifacts and forensic consumers"),
[global-ledger-query.md](global-ledger-query.md) ("Offline view entry") and
[runtime-database.md](runtime-database.md) (`open_existing_unchecked`) are the contract. The number
1.224 is the coordinator's.

**What.** `GlobalLedger::open_metadata` keeps its signature and `GlobalLedgerMetadata` its public
methods; on an SQLite root its implementation is replaced. (1) The database opens without the
whole-file `quick_check` and the snapshot holds a read-only connection of its own. (2) The opening
is two short read transactions: the Runtime writer open's checks (`verify_tail`, shared with
`verify_open_tail`: format and views, the keyed meta row, marker `ready`, `MAX(sequence)` at the
head, the newest `ledger_observer.open_verify_tail_records` records authenticated and chained to the
head hash) plus contiguity (`COUNT`, `MIN`, `MAX` equal to head, 1, head); then the eviction intent
and outcome records by type, each authenticated, as the proof set (`RetentionIndex::offline_proofs`);
then it pins the point. (3) A page is the reader pool's page at that point (`ViewReader`, as
`view_page_at_point`), one short read transaction, its scope source `offline`; a page returns at
most its request's limit (`MAX_RUNTIME_EVENT_QUERY_EVENTS`, 256) and
`MAX_RUNTIME_EVENT_QUERY_RESPONSE_BYTES` (768 KiB) with a cursor to the rest, as every Runtime page
does. (4) A material fetch is one authenticated point read with its proof from the pinned set.
(5) Every read has a deadline: the opening the supplied one, else `open_timeout_ms`'s factory value
(600 s) from its start; each later read `writer_reply_timeout_ms`'s factory value (10 s) from its own
start, no later than a deadline the caller set or passed; inside a statement too
(`read_check_vm_steps`). A page whose deadline passes is refused whole; with
`sqlite_page_read_budget` (the UI's interactive use, `read_budget_ms`) it answers incomplete with its
cursor. (6) The whole-snapshot re-verification of every page (`SqliteViewSnapshot::verify_view_full`)
and its CTE selection (`views::select_sequences`) are removed. **No outcome code** (a refusal is
`ledger_read_budget_exceeded` with `phase=open|proofs|page|resolve` in its detail), **no
configuration key** (the defaults are the factory values of existing `ledger_observer` keys; the
page bound is the existing contract constants), **no persisted shape, no interface revision.** No
caller changes code.

**Why.** The opening read and authenticated the whole ledger into memory after an unbudgeted
whole-file `quick_check(1)`, and every page did so again; the UI's 1 GiB / 300 000 / 60 s budget made
the production root unopenable, and its absolute 60 s deadline refused every page a minute after the
opening.

**Integrity.** Not weaker than the writer open's (design §4.5): the meta row, the head, the tail and
the extent at the opening (contiguity is more than the writer checks); every other record is
authenticated when a read reads it. The opening no longer finds damage in records older than its
tail, nor checks the migrated prefix: those move to the explicit whole-ledger mode of LN-OFF-3 and to
`ledger-maintenance verify`, which reads every record.

**Live root** (pending decision 115, A): read, not refused. Each read is a short transaction at the
pinned head under WAL, so the writer commits meanwhile and the checkpoint catches up after it. A
later B or C adds a refusal on top (`read_writer_metadata` is still read at the opening).

**Unchanged.** The writer open (`verify_open_tail` reads exactly as before), the reader pool, the
writer's pages, `open_evidence` (whole, LN-OFF-3), `open_selected`, `open_range`, Segment roots, game
neutrality.

**Rollback** (to 0.12.31). Nothing to undo: no ledger, state, configuration or wire shape is new. A
0.12.31 offline reader again reads the whole ledger into memory at the opening and at every page.

| OFF1-2 | `GlobalLedgerMetadata::project_view_page` on SQLite | reader behaviour | LN-OFF-1 | — | the reader pool's page (`ViewReader`, `source` `offline`, `time_index` false on a root without the derived views); default: refused whole at its deadline (`ReadWork::was_spent`); optional work budget answers `read_budget` |

### 1.225 Slice SS-2b (0.12.32): business candidates ranked by net benefit within a tier; unknown value is not dispatched (Alice's ruling 104 point 3, approved with 104 on 10-30 21:3x and checked by the research channel, Workflow #386 comment 6523148251; ruling 116 of 10-30 23:2x–23:3x, which overrides that check's "unknown is dispatched as today"; design `rd-1029/design-sch-state.md` §4.1 steps 3 and 5, §4.6, §4.10; coordinator work order `rd-1029/brief-116-112-114.md` SS-2b)

[scheduling/README.md](scheduling/README.md) ("Net benefit within a tier"; "Pool Valuation" and
"Expected production (v2)" for the markers; "Task Reserves" item 4; "Dispatch Decision Record"
item 1), [scheduling/v2/README.md](scheduling/v2/README.md) and the V2 `tasks`, `pools` and
`common` schemas, [standard-pack-schedule.md](standard-pack-schedule.md) ("Judged rules", "Two
priority tiers", "Tools", "The store update rule") and
[resource-targets.md](resource-targets.md) ("Net benefit") are the contract. The number 1.225 is
the coordinator's.

**What.** (1) A V2 task may carry `benefit_judged: true`; the standard-pack composer writes it on
every rule whose package is not maintenance-role (and refuses a rule that writes it). (2) A judged
candidate (a marked task's, neither in a chain head's run window nor a manual request, a trigger
that requires a `session.` instruction through `all`) has the net benefit `B = Σ produce·W/Q −
Σ consume·P/Q` in milli, the resource layer's own `r`, `W` and `Q`, `P = W` discounted for a
regenerating pool linearly between the task's reserve line and the capacity. An unknown input
(no effect, a pending entry, a pending or missing valuation, an unknown or expired reading `P`
needs) defers it with `benefit_unknown` and never adds up the known part; a known `B ≤ 0` defers
it with `policy_benefit_nonpositive`. (3) In a catalog with a mark the round ranks `promoted`, then
the tier (unmarked, the maintenance tier, before marked, the business tier), then within a tier
the unjudged in the order of before and the judged by `B ÷ E`, then the SS-2 tie-break; the
reserve gate takes candidates in that order. (4) The explicit marker `"pending"` may stand for a
pool's `valuation` and an effect's `amount` (V2 only); it changes nothing but a judged
candidate's `B`. (5) `actinglab standard-pack check` and `package bundle --schedule` answer each
game's judged rules as complete, pending and undeclared, and warn once per undeclared rule
(`standard_pack_benefit_undeclared`). (6) The idle plan counts a decision the gate holds neither
due nor as a wake of its own.

**Why.** Ruling 104 point 3: within a tier, net benefit from high to low; not positive is not
dispatched. Ruling 116: write harmless placeholders or empty values now, so the scheduler may in
effect stop, and business values go straight into the task packages once they exist; until then
the business side is maintained by hand through the Lab. The research check (6523148251) asked
that unknown never be 0 and that partial knowledge be unknown; 116 overrides its "unknown is
dispatched as today". The tier is the task's §1.222 tier, read from the mark, not the raw
`priority` value: production rules still carry about 78 priorities per game until RS-8, and the
handwritten priority must not order the judged candidates of one tier (the work order's test 1).
**No switch**: no configuration key and no per-instance mode (104 has no benefit-first switch).

**Unchanged.** A catalog without `benefit_judged` and without a marker keeps its hash and decides
byte for byte as before (no candidate is judged, the order is the one of before). The resource
layer, every pool weight and `R` (one-way rule: nothing here writes a weight), the score stage's
thresholds, the reserve gate's steps, every closure position, B41's handover, the shared run
limits, the spend values (a pending `amount` reads as no declared quantity there, as in the
reserve gate and the tie-break), game neutrality. Unjudged candidates (maintenance-role tasks, a
chain successor in its head's window, a manual request, the Runtime's own reading) rank in the
order of before within their tier.

**New codes and keys.** `benefit_unknown` (info; `benefit_gap` required; `pool_id`, `fact_key`,
`unknown_reason` optional) and `policy_benefit_nonpositive` (info; `benefit_milli`,
`expected_duration_ms`), policy codes, because no code says "a judged candidate's value is unknown
or not positive" (`score_deferred` is a selection document's threshold, `resource_reserve_insufficient`
a reserve line); the domain `benefit_` for the policy crate; `standard_pack_benefit_undeclared`
(warning / `declaration_error`; `game`, `task_id`; `pool_id` optional), a contract code beside
SS-2's tiers warning, because `standard_pack_package_unclassified` names a package nothing
schedules; the keys `benefit_gap` (vocabulary `benefit_gap`: `no_effects`, `entry_pending`,
`valuation_pending`, `valuation_missing`, `reading_unknown`), `benefit_milli` (integer) and
`expected_duration_ms` (duration); `rank_breakdown` gains `benefit_milli` and
`expected_duration_ms` as optional values. **No new ledger record kind, no configuration key, no
interface revision.**

**What changes live.** Every production rule's package is a business package except the
maintenance-role ones, and no rule declares `produces` or `consumes` and no pool a valuation
(`rd-1029/design-sch-state.md` §2.1), so once deployed every business candidate is
`benefit_unknown` (`no_effects`) and is not dispatched (ruling 116); maintenance-role rules and the
Runtime's own reading run as before. The scheduler is stopped by Alice's order meanwhile
(`alice-116-scheduler-stop`), and the gate lifts, bypasses or works around no pause. The store
update rule's package is not maintenance-role by the root files, so it is judged too: an instance
that meets the client update dialog stays held until the resource side gives that rule values, or
a later slice classifies a `store_update` package as maintenance (the bundle's `maintenance[]`
has no use for it). The first workbench check after the deploy composes a new generation (every
business rule gains the mark, so the rules digest changes) and activates it.

**Rollback** (to 0.12.31). The configuration needs nothing. The ledger: the new values and the
new `why` codes ride in existing reason chains (`PolicyReasonRecord` is `#[serde(transparent)]`
over `Outcome`, whose values every 0.12 reader keeps as a map without a key check). The catalog:
a 0.12.31 build refuses `benefit_judged` and the pending markers (`unknown_field`,
`type_mismatch`), and its start compiles the active generation and every generation an unsettled
dispatch pins (`policy_host.rs`, `load_catalog_generation`), failing with
`catalog_generation_invalid` on a marked one. So before rolling back, let 0.12.32 activate a
generation without marks (take `schedule.json` out of the game roots, which composes the valid
empty catalog, or leave only maintenance-role rules) with no policy dispatch unsettled (the
scheduler is stopped); 0.12.31 then starts on it and composes its own generation, unmarked, at
its first check.

**Rollback correction** (release 0.12.32, from 0.12.31's code). 0.12.31's start also compiles the
generation of each (task, instance) pair's latest completed policy dispatch that its decision
memory names, settled or not (`load_dispatch_journal`, `seen_intent_of`, `load_generation`).
Every generation 0.12.32 composes carries the marks (`benefit_judged`, and `"pending"` or
`on_unknown` wherever a `schedule.json` writes them). So the steps above suffice only while
0.12.32 has dispatched no scheduled run, which is the case while the scheduler is stopped on every
instance. After one has run, each such pair must first complete a dispatch under an unmarked
generation; a pair whose rule is gone cannot, and 0.12.31 then cannot start on that state root.

**Narrowed** (release 0.12.33, §1.229). The chain exemption of (2) ("neither in a chain head's
run window") and of "Unchanged" ("a chain successor in its head's window") holds only while the
successor continues a business chain: a link walked from it up to its chain head, the head
included, is marked. A marked candidate whose walked links are all unmarked (a business task
after a maintenance task, such as a return home) is judged as in no window. Rollback to 0.12.32:
§1.229.

### 1.226 Slice WATCH-P (0.12.32): the emulator watch neither restarts nor recognizes an instance its own scheduling pause holds (Alice's ruling 112 of 10-30, 23:2x 「可以，按推荐，没问题」 and 23:3x 「没错」, on the recommendation 「暂停中的实例，监视只看状态、不重启、不识别绑定，和「玩家持有」一样；恢复时照常检查」; production 10-29 21:35 and 21:38: the watch restarted an instance twice while it was paused for a person's own check, and `emulator_control.watch_enabled` was then set false; coordinator work order `rd-1029/brief-116-112-114.md` WATCH-P)

[emulator-control.md](emulator-control.md) ("Emulator watch", "Pauses (WATCH-P)") and
[scheduling-pause.md](scheduling-pause.md) are the contract. For the watch, ruling 112 replaces
ruling 35's "a scheduling pause holds only dispatches". The number 1.226 is the coordinator's.

**What.** A poll still reads every discovery-bound instance and records its reading (R2). For an
instance that its own scheduling pause holds, in any stage (`draining`, `paused`, `released`, a
restored pause included), it then requests no R3 restart and no EMU-BIND recognition, on either
recognition path (endpoint pending or bound to another port; bound to the reported port but
unprepared). Where it would have requested one it records `emulator_autostart_skipped` (info;
`alias`, `watch_kind`, the new value `skip_reason` `instance_paused`; a `device_state_observed`
record under the instance and its report line) once per pause revision and `watch_kind`, not
once per poll. A skip takes no claim, counts against neither bound and records no
`emulator_watch_restart_exhausted`. The resume adds nothing: its reconnect and self-check run as
before, and the first poll after the pause is gone applies R3 and EMU-BIND as for any instance.
The player hold of #429 R-7 is not an instance pause but the instance's own state (corrected by
§1.233, R-7a): R-7b adds it at `automatic_start_hold`, the place every automatic start asks
(§1.230), with `skip_reason` `player_held`, first before the pause.

**Why.** The watch's restart and recognition ran "paused or not"; only the fix-1 recognition path
excluded the stage `released`. A person who pauses an instance to use it must not have its
emulator started or its endpoint rebound under them.

**Unchanged.** The global pause holds neither (it is no pause of the instance). The daemon start's
configured emulator start, IDLE-1's wake and a watch claim requested before the pause began are
autostart claims that no pause holds, as before. Blackouts, the bound, the idle hold and the
watch's keys are unchanged; an instance no pause of its own holds is watched byte for byte as in
0.12.31. **No new code, no configuration key, no persisted state shape, no interface revision.**
One new outcome key with its vocabulary, because no existing key says why a claim was not
requested: `pause_reason` names the operator's reason, not the watch's. The watch's memory of the
skips is one entry per instance (a revision and two flags), never persisted.

**What changes live.** Production holds all five instances under `alice-116-scheduler-stop`. With
the watch on, each of them that is a configured instance found stopped, or a running one in need of
a recognition, gets one skip record per pause revision and kind instead of a restart or a
recognition, so `watch_enabled = false` is no longer needed to keep the watch off paused
instances; its polls and their readings go on.

**Rollback** (to 0.12.31). Nothing to undo: 0.12.31 reads the new records (the code exists, and an
outcome's `values` are kept as a map without a key check), and the skip memory is not persisted.
0.12.31's watch restarts and recognizes paused instances again, so set
`emulator_control.watch_enabled` false before rolling back while instances are paused.

### 1.227 Slice SS-2c (0.12.32): a `schedule.json` rule may declare itself maintenance, so the net-benefit gate does not judge it (Alice's ruling 104 point 1: maintenance is startup, return home, recovery, readings maintenance and store update, everything else business; the approved design does not judge maintenance tasks by net benefit, `rd-1029/design-sch-state.md` §4.10 and the research check, Workflow #386 comment 6523148251; coordinator work order `rd-1029/brief-ss2c.md`)

[standard-pack-schedule.md](standard-pack-schedule.md) ("The file", "Judged rules" and "The
maintenance declaration", "Composition" step 3, "Two priority tiers", "Tools", "The store update
rule"), [scheduling/README.md](scheduling/README.md) ("Net benefit within a tier") and
[scheduling/v2/README.md](scheduling/v2/README.md) are the contract. The number 1.227 is the
coordinator's.

**What.** (1) A `schedule.json` rule may write `"maintenance": true`. The reader every composer
runs (`parse_standard_pack_schedule`) takes the member out of the rule (`ScheduleRule::maintenance`)
and refuses any other value, `false` included, as `standard_pack_root_invalid`, `schedule_invalid`
at `/rules/<i>/maintenance`. (2) The composer marks `benefit_judged: true` only on a rule whose
package is not maintenance-role **and** that does not declare itself maintenance; nothing else of
a declared rule changes (its `priority`, its place in its tier, every gate). (3) The tools'
`benefit_coverage` counts a declared rule as not judged (never complete, pending or undeclared,
never `standard_pack_benefit_undeclared`) and gains `maintenance_declared`, the declared rules
that are not held, whatever their package's role, for the resource side's RS-8 check. (4) When a
game's composed rules use exactly two priority values, `actinglab standard-pack check` and
`package bundle --schedule` warn `standard_pack_priority_tier_mismatch` (keys `game`, `task_id`)
once per rule that declares itself maintenance and carries the lower value, or that is judged and
carries the higher, after the undeclared-value warnings; never a refusal.

**Why.** SS-2b judges by the package's maintenance role ("Classification" item 1: bundle
`maintenance[]`, navigation edges and `recovery_chain`, interrupt handlers and `then.run`, page
features), which is narrower than ruling 104's maintenance tier. SS-2b's implementer found judged
as business in the four repositories: the store update rule (no root file can give it a role),
readings packages beyond the first per server, and several return-home and recovery rules. Until
values exist each is `benefit_unknown` and never dispatched, so restoring the scheduler (ruling
116) would leave maintenance undone. A per-rule declaration lets the resource side put each rule
in its tier without a new root-file role.

**`false` is refused**, not read as "not declared": on a rule whose package is maintenance-role
it would read as "business" while the role still exempts the rule, a declaration that does
nothing; and with one spelling for "not declared" (no member) RS-8 can count and check the files
uniformly. **Raw V2 catalogs** set `benefit_judged` themselves as SS-2b allows; `maintenance` is
no V2 task member (`unknown_field`).

**Unchanged.** A `schedule.json` without the member composes byte for byte as with SS-2b alone:
the same documents, catalog hash and rules digest (the reader keeps such a rule's members and
their order as before). A declared rule on a maintenance-role package composes byte for byte as
without the declaration. The evaluator, the gate, the ranking and every record are SS-2b's: they
read the mark only. The Runtime's workbench records none of the tools' warnings. Game
neutrality: the Runtime names no game and no package.

**New codes and keys.** `standard_pack_priority_tier_mismatch` (warning / `declaration_error`;
`game`, `task_id`), a contract code beside SS-2's tiers warning and SS-2b's undeclared-value
warning, because no code says "a rule's declaration and its tier disagree"
(`standard_pack_priority_tiers_exceeded` counts values, `standard_pack_benefit_undeclared` names a
judged rule without values). `standard_pack_benefit_undeclared`'s text (pending) now names the
declaration. No key, **no new ledger record kind, no configuration key, no interface revision.**

**What changes live.** Nothing at deploy: a `schedule.json` that loads in 0.12.31 cannot write
the member (0.12.31 refuses it, below), so every production file composes as with SS-2b. Once the
resource side (RS-8) declares its maintenance rules, the first workbench check composes a new
generation (the declared rules lose the mark, so the rules digest changes) and activates it; the
declared rules then rank in the maintenance tier and are dispatched as before SS-2b. The scheduler
stays stopped by Alice's order meanwhile (`alice-116-scheduler-stop`); nothing here lifts or
works around a pause.

**Rollback** (to 0.12.31). The configuration and the ledger need nothing: no record, value or
code of this slice reaches the ledger (the new warning is the tools'; a refused shape is the
existing `standard_pack_root_invalid`). A composed generation carries no trace of the member (the
reader takes it out), so SS-2b's rollback steps for the marks stand as they are. A game root
whose `schedule.json` writes `maintenance` is refused by 0.12.31 (its reader passes the member
into the task, its compiler answers `unknown_field`, mapped to `standard_pack_root_invalid`,
`schedule_invalid` at `/rules/<i>/maintenance`, recorded once per game and file), and that game
then has no rules unless the active generation holds an older good file. So before rolling back,
take the member out of the game roots' `schedule.json`, or take the file out as SS-2b's recipe
already does.

### 1.228 Slice LAB-OBS-1 (0.12.33): an unmatched `observe --capture` no longer leaves a rejected `runtime.debug_observe`, and a rejected debug command names its reason (production defect of v0.12.32 on 10-31 11:2x: four `ac_lab_observe` calls with `capture=true` whose frame matched no page of the package answered `ok:true`, `state: no_match`, and each was followed by a `runtime.debug_observe` recorded as `command.rejected`, error, `values: {}`, effect `not_performed`; observes that matched a page left none; coordinator work order `rd-1031/brief-lab-obs-1.md`)

[contained-page-observation.md](contained-page-observation.md) (the LAB-OBS-1 paragraph) is the
contract. The number 1.228 is the coordinator's.

**Root cause.** The second request is actinglab's own: `observe --capture` (`run_runtime_observe`)
closes its debug session's `runtime.debug_observe`, opened with `requested`, by `RecordDebugEvent`.
It sent `completed` only for `recognized` and `failed` for `no_match`, `conflict` and `partial`,
although the observation stood and the answer was `ok`. The Runtime did not refuse that request: it
accepted it and wrote what it said, a failed non-run debug command being `command.rejected`
(`command_rejected`, error) without an outcome, hence `values: {}`. Neither the instance pause, a
lease (the request holds none) nor a missing field takes part. `do`, `ensure` and `wait` already
close an answer that stands as `completed` (`finish_runtime_debug_result`).

**What.** (1) `observe --capture` closes `runtime.debug_observe` with `completed` whatever the
observation's status; the status stays the answer's `state` and the observation's own terminal
(`PageUnmatched` for `no_match`). (2) `RuntimeDebugEvent` gains `failure_code`, a registered code,
written on a `failed` `observe`, `do`, `ensure` or `wait` and on nothing else
(`RuntimeDebugEvent::rejected`); `failed` stays for `lab_run`, recorded as `task.failed` as before.
Validation refuses a failed command without a registered code, and any other event with one, as
`invalid_runtime_debug_event` (the client before sending: `runtime_debug_event_invalid`; the Runtime:
denied, nothing recorded). (3) The Runtime records a failed command as `command.rejected` whose
outcome is `command_rejected` with `failure_code` (`RuntimeDebugEvent::outcome`). actinglab names the
Runtime outcome's code when the observe request itself failed, and the answer's code when `do`,
`ensure` or `wait` failed (relayed: a spelling the catalog does not list becomes
`outcome_relay_unregistered`).

**Why this fix.** The follow-up is needed: it is the terminal that pairs the `lab.request` of the
same debug session, as every Lab debug command has one. So it is kept, in the shape the Runtime
records as an accepted command. A `failed` terminal is still sent when the command fails, and it now
carries its reason.

**Unchanged.** A matching observe records the same `lab.request` and `command.validated`. The
observation request, its records and the answer are unchanged. Game-neutral; no configuration key.

**New codes and keys.** None. `command_rejected` (pending) declares the existing key `failure_code`
as optional. **No new ledger record kind, no new record member** (`command.rejected` already carries
`outcome`, ledger revision 3), **no configuration key, no interface revision**: only actinglab of
the same build sends `RecordDebugEvent`.

**What changes live.** After the deploy, an unmatched `ac_lab_observe` or `observe --capture` leaves
`command.validated` (info) instead of `command.rejected` (error), so the error count and diagnose stop
showing it. A failed Lab observe, do, ensure or wait shows its reason on its `command.rejected`.

**Rollback** (to 0.12.32). Nothing to do. The configuration and state files are untouched. The
records 0.12.33 wrote are of existing kinds, and 0.12.32 reads `failure_code` as a received value of
a key its table holds. After the rollback an unmatched observe again leaves a reasonless
`command.rejected`. actinglab and the Runtime roll back together; a 0.12.32 Runtime refuses the
0.12.33 failed event's `failure_code` (`deny_unknown_fields`).

| # | Shape | Kind | Code slice | First writer | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| LOB-1 | the terminal `RecordDebugEvent` of `observe --capture` | behaviour (no shape change) | LAB-OBS-1 | actinglab | `completed` for every status of an observation that stands; `failed` only when the command fails |
| LOB-2 | `RuntimeDebugEvent.failure_code` (a registered code; `RuntimeDebugEvent::rejected`, `::outcome`) | wire member addition (optional, absent when unused) | LAB-OBS-1 | actinglab's debug session | required on a failed `observe`, `do`, `ensure`, `wait`; refused elsewhere; `invalid_runtime_debug_event` |
| LOB-3 | `command.rejected` of a failed Lab debug command: outcome `command_rejected` with `failure_code` | rule of an existing record (shape unchanged) | LAB-OBS-1 | the Runtime (`record_debug_event`) | was the bare diagnostic code, `values: {}`; `command_rejected` declares `failure_code` optional |

### 1.229 Slice SS-2e (0.12.33): a business task that continues only maintenance links is judged by its net benefit (design `rd-1029/design-sch-state.md` §4.10: maintenance packages, the intermediate navigation steps of a chain and manual requests are not judged, 「链条整体的价值记在链头（业务包）上」; the resource side's RS-8 report of 10-31: many business chains of all four games start at a return home; coordinator work order `rd-1031/brief-ss2e.md`)

[scheduling/README.md](scheduling/README.md) ("Net benefit within a tier", "Who is judged") and
[scheduling/v2/README.md](scheduling/v2/README.md) (the SS-2b `benefit_judged` item) are the
contract. It narrows §1.225 (2). The number 1.229 is the coordinator's.

**What.** A candidate whose task the catalog marks `benefit_judged` and that is in its chain
head's run window (SS-2, §1.222 (2)) is exempt from the net-benefit judgment only when the chain it
continues has a business link: at least one of the links walked from it up to its head, every one
of them in its window, the head included, is marked. A marked candidate whose walked links are all
unmarked (maintenance tasks) is judged on its own, like a candidate in no window: the existing
`benefit_unknown` (with its `benefit_gap`) or `policy_benefit_nonpositive`, or its place in the
business tier by `B ÷ E`. In `M → A → B`, `M` unmarked and `A`, `B` marked, `A` is judged and `B`
rides with `A`. The walk (`evaluator/tie_break.rs`, `chain_head`) returns, beside the head, whether
it passed a marked link (`ChainWalk`); `build_candidate` reads that for `judged` alone.

**Why.** `judged` was `marked && chain_head.is_none() && !manual_request`, and `chain_head` is set
whenever the task continues a predecessor's latest successful run, whatever that predecessor's
tier. So a business task whose trigger requires the success of a return home under `all` was not
judged after every successful return home: it skipped `benefit_unknown` and
`policy_benefit_nonpositive`, and ranked with the head's priority among the unjudged business
candidates, which go before the judged ones. Design §4.10 exempts the steps of a chain whose value
is recorded on its head, a business package; a business task after a maintenance task is no such
step but a business decision of its own. The resource side found such chains in all four game
roots, and keeps two chain heads of one game in the business tier on purpose to avoid this.

**Why this change.** It is the smallest that gives the rule: the walk already visits exactly the
links in their windows, so it records one more bit as it goes. No second walk, no new input, and
the head stays the one SS-2 finds.

**Unchanged.** The tier (the task's own mark). SS-2's rank inheritance: every candidate in a window
ranks with the head the walk finds, so a judged successor of a maintenance task still carries its
head's `priority` and `strategic_weight_milli` (within the business tier they no longer order it,
§1.225 (3)), the fact refresh lends that rank as before, and the ` chain_head=` detail is as
before. Manual requests; unmarked candidates, a maintenance successor of a maintenance task
included; a successor of a business link; a candidate in no window; a catalog with no mark, byte
for byte (it judges no candidate). The gate, its reasons and values, the ranking and the records
are SS-2b's. Game neutrality. **No new code, value, key, configuration key, record kind, catalog
member or interface revision.**

**What changes live.** Nothing now: under ruling 116 all five instances are paused
(`alice-116-scheduler-stop`). Once the scheduler resumes, a business rule whose links up to its
chain head are all maintenance rules, such as one that follows a return home, waits for its values
(`benefit_unknown`, `no_effects`) like every business rule without them, instead of being
dispatched after each return home. A successor of a business rule still rides with it.

**Rollback** (to 0.12.32). Nothing to do: no ledger, state, catalog or configuration shape is new,
and the reasons the newly judged candidates answer are SS-2b's, which 0.12.32 reads. 0.12.32 again
exempts every candidate in a chain head's run window, successors of maintenance links included.

### 1.230 Slice PAUSE-AUTO (0.12.34): neither the daemon start's configured emulator start nor IDLE-1's wake starts an instance its own scheduling pause holds, and the pause is asked again on the start's key (Alice's ruling 117 A of 10-31 13:22, relayed from the AC审计 window, Workflow #386 comment 6539002530, with the constraint of review 6538837616 §3 that a start queued before the pause must not slip past it; coordinator work order `rd-1031/brief-pause-auto.md`)

[emulator-control.md](emulator-control.md) ("Configured start at daemon start", "Pauses
(PAUSE-AUTO)", "Emulator watch"), [scheduling-pause.md](scheduling-pause.md) and
[runtime-config.md](runtime-config.md) ("The `idle` section") are the contract. For the daemon
start and IDLE-1's wake, ruling 117 A replaces ruling 35's "a scheduling pause holds only
dispatches", as ruling 112 did for the watch (§1.226). The number 1.230 is the coordinator's.

**What.** Every automatic emulator start asks one question before it starts an emulator,
`automatic_start_hold` (`host/emulator_autostart.rs`): may this instance be started now. Today
the instance's own scheduling pause, in any stage (`draining`, `paused`, `released`, a restored
pause included), says no; the global pause does not.
- The configured start at daemon start (also a watchdog's or a deploy's daemon start) asks it
  before it requests a claim. A held instance whose emulator is stopped gets no claim and is not
  counted in `emulator_autostart_queued`; one `emulator_autostart_skipped` (info; `alias`,
  `skip_reason` `instance_paused`, no `watch_kind`; a `device_state_observed` record under the
  instance and its report line) says so.
- IDLE-1's wake after `stop_emulator` asks it before it queues anything (`IdleView::start_held`):
  the wake is not queued (`IdleStep::WakeHeld`), the instance stays kept closed owing it
  (`host.idle_state` unchanged), and one skip with `idle_action` `stop_emulator` says so per pause
  revision, however many idle checks find it due.
- The re-check: the daemon start's claim and an idle wake's claim ask it again on their key at
  every tick of their hold (`autostart_hold_ends`), so the last time just before the Start. A
  claim requested before the pause began (waiting for the network, its start turn or a
  blackout's end) ends there: it releases its key with no `command.*` record and no failure
  pair, starts nothing and records the same skip. An idle wake's claim so ended leaves the wake
  owed again (`withhold_idle_wake`, `IdlePlanner::wake_held`): kept closed, not woken, its wake at
  the time it was woken.
- The watch's restart claim (R3) asks it on its key the same way (the coordinator's ruling of
  10-31 on rulings 112 and 117 A, PR #1461's second commit: the restart claim the watch requested
  before the pause began, which WATCH-P let run, is the very slip-through 117 A forbids). Held, it
  ends as the two others do, its skip with `watch_kind` `restart`.
- So does the watch's recognition claim (EMU-BIND; the coordinator's ruling of 10-31 on ruling
  112, PR #1461's third commit: a paused instance is not recognized, and a recognition claim
  requested before the pause, for example one a blackout held queued, must not bind it after).
  Held on its key, it releases the key and binds, prepares and starts nothing, its skip with
  `watch_kind` `recognize`.
- The bound (the same ruling): a restart or recognition the watch counted when it requested the
  claim, and that the pause then ended on its key, did not happen, so it leaves the window again
  (`refund_watch_request`, `EmulatorWatch::refund_request`: the newest request of its kind for
  the instance, since the watch requests none while a claim holds or waits for the key). It
  takes no place among `emulator_control.restart_attempts`; a skip before a request already took
  none (WATCH-P).
- Each start records its skip once per pause revision and start (WATCH-P's in-memory skip
  memory, `SkippedStart`, never persisted; each of the watch's kinds shares one entry between its
  polls and its claim).
- After the resume: the next idle check queues the owed wake as before, the watch's next poll
  restarts or recognizes as before, and a next daemon start starts as before.

**Why.** On every daemon start or deploy the configured start started the emulator of a paused
instance, and IDLE-1's wake started a paused instance's stopped emulator; only the watch obeyed
the pause (WATCH-P). Production now holds all five instances under `alice-116-scheduler-stop`,
and the resource channel starts emulators by hand for its Lab maintenance.

**The seam for the player hold.** `HostShared::automatic_start_hold` is the one place an automatic
start asks; the watch now asks it too (it replaces WATCH-P's `instance_pause_revision`, same
answer). #429 R-7b adds the player hold there (its reason a second token of
`emulator_autostart_skip_reason`, `player_held` per WP-2 as §1.233 corrects it, registered by R-7a), and every automatic start obeys it
without another change.

**Unchanged.** An explicit emulator control (`actingctl emulator`, `ac_emulator`, Lab) never asks
and runs under a pause as before, its startup package held behind the pause (#411 A71). The
watch's WATCH-P behaviour before a request: it asks before it requests a restart or a recognition.
The global pause, blackouts, the idle hold of an
emulator the action stopped, idle stop itself, a `close_app` wake (it starts no emulator) and every
unpaused instance, byte for byte. The stuck-recovery ladder's emulator-restart rung already asks
the pause at its admission and before each step (A6). **No new code, key, vocabulary token,
configuration key, persisted shape or interface revision.** One more optional value on an existing
code: `idle_action` on `emulator_autostart_skipped` (the key exists; `emulator_autostart_queued`
already carries it for the wake).

**What changes live.** All five instances are paused. A daemon start or deploy no longer starts the
emulator of any of them that is stopped (one skip record each instead), no idle wake after
`stop_emulator` starts one, and no watch restart or recognition claim requested before a pause
starts or binds one after it, nor uses up the watch's bound. The daemon start does not run again
at the resume: an emulator it left
stopped is started by the watch's first poll after the resume (R3, while
`emulator_control.watch_enabled`) or by a person.

**Rollback** (to 0.12.33). Nothing to do: no ledger, state, catalog or configuration shape is new;
0.12.33 reads the skip records (the code and key exist, and an outcome's `values` are kept as a map
without a key check), the skip memory is not persisted, and a withheld wake is kept in
`host.idle_state` as an ordinary closed row. 0.12.33 starts paused instances on daemon start and
idle wake again, lets a watch restart or recognition claim requested before a pause start or
bind the emulator, and counts such a claim against the bound; the bound's memory is not persisted
either.
