|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PA-1 | `automatic_start_hold` (`emulator_autostart.rs`), asked by `enqueue_emulator_autostart`, `autostart_hold_ends` (the daemon start's, an idle wake's and the watch's restart and recognition claims), `watch_emulator` and the idle check (`IdleView::start_held`) | behaviour (configured start, idle wake, the watch's claims on their key) (host gate row "PAUSE-AUTO") | PAUSE-AUTO | — | the instance's own pause in any stage; the global pause and explicit controls unchanged; the seam R-7b extends |
| PA-4 | `refund_watch_request`, `EmulatorWatch::refund_request` (`emulator_watch.rs`), called when a watch claim ends held on its key | behaviour (the watch's bound) | PAUSE-AUTO | — | the request leaves the window again, so it takes no place among `restart_attempts` within `restart_window_ms` |
| PA-2 | `IdleStep::WakeHeld`, `IdlePlanner::wake_held`, `withhold_idle_wake` (`idle_action.rs`, `idle.rs`) | behaviour (idle planner) | PAUSE-AUTO | — | a held `stop_emulator` wake stays owed in `host.idle_state` (shape unchanged); the next check after the resume queues it |
| PA-3 | `idle_action` (existing key) on `emulator_autostart_skipped`, with `skip_reason` | new optional value of an existing code (no shape change) | PAUSE-AUTO | the idle check, an idle wake's claim | once per pause revision and start (`SkippedStart`); the daemon start's skip carries neither `watch_kind` nor `idle_action` |

### 1.231 Slice SS-4 (0.12.34): after a successful run whose basis got no reading of another value, the pair waits for one (Alice's ruling 105 A: no count-based last line, the no-progress guard and the failure retry cap replace counts; the 10-29 ruling confirmed with no objection on 10-31 13:22, Workflow #390 comment 6539002724; design `rd-1029/design-sch-state.md` §4.7 and the SS-4 entry of §5; plan `rd-1029/plan-state-driven.md`, the SS-4 row and the notes on removing the counts; coordinator work order `rd-1031/brief-ss4.md`)

[scheduling/README.md](scheduling/README.md) ("No-progress guard"),
[scheduling-blackout.md](scheduling-blackout.md) ("Order of the deferrals"),
[runtime-config.md](runtime-config.md) ("No-progress guard"),
[standard-pack-schedule.md](standard-pack-schedule.md) ("Tools", "Failure escalation without a
daily bound") and [component-interfaces.md](component-interfaces.md) (`actingd-config` 23) are the
contract. The number 1.231 is the coordinator's; §1.230 (PAUSE-AUTO) ships in the same release.

**What.** Each new dispatch intent's **basis** is captured as the evaluation that chose it read its
facts: of the parts that made its trigger true (every child of a true `all`, the first true child
of an `any`, every fact below a `not`), the `resource.` and `inventory.` facts they name, every
completion time a `fact_time_reached` names and the facts of the pools they project; and the
reading and capacity facts of the pools the task reserves; each with its reading (the value above
confidence 0, or none). Its admission arms the pair's guard. Before every evaluated cycle a guard one of whose basis
keys reads a value other than its admission's (a reading where there was none counts) is released
for good. While a guard is armed and the pair's own latest run is the guarded dispatch, succeeded,
under the same catalog generation, the pair is deferred after its trigger, feedback stop and
cooldown with the new info reason `policy_no_progress` {`basis_readings`, `served_by_dispatch_unix_ms`},
no wake, and is not a candidate. A newer reading of the same value is no progress; a key a reset
cleared reads nothing and releases nothing. A failed or cancelled run, an immediate rerun, a remedy
request or retry and an owed rerun are never held. `scheduling.no_progress.enabled` (default `true`,
settable, also per instance) turns it off; off, the evaluation is the one before. A dispatch with
no basis key (decided by a clock alone, or by a clock beside a lock) and one with more than 32 has
no guard. The standard-pack
composer adds the plan's hint `standard_pack_escalation_threshold_high` (warning) for a rule
without a daily bound whose `on_failure.escalation_threshold` is above 10; only `standard-pack
check` and `package bundle --schedule` report it.

**Why.** With SS-3's optional run counts, nothing but `daily_limit` stopped a task that keeps
succeeding without changing anything (a package that spends nothing, a broken reading, a game that
does not respond): it would run every cooldown. Ruling 105 A puts a state edge there, not a count:
the task runs at most once more and waits for a changed reading. The plan's warning covers the
other half, the failure path, which the guard leaves to `on_failure`: four repositories write
`escalation_threshold` 1000 beside their daily limits, and without the limit a failing task would
be retried about 1000 times before its pair is paused.

**Choices made here, and why.**
- *Which facts.* Design §4.7 names pools, stocks, remaining counts and completion-time keys "the
  admission read for that decision"; the game-neutral reading of that is the realistic families
  (`resource.`, `inventory.`, the keys recognition writes and a probe may name), every
  `fact_time_reached` key, and the catalog's pool readings, taken from the parts of the trigger
  that decided it and from the reserve gate. Left out: a lock, a health flag or a session fact
  (beside a clock it would arm a guard no run can release, and the daily task would stop after
  its first success); a branch of an `any` that did not decide it (`any` of a due clock and a
  stock gate is the clock's edge, and a stock the run does not change must not stop the hourly
  run); the feedback stop (it stops a pair, it does not admit one); and a pool the task only
  consumes or produces (no gate reads it, so no fact refresh is ever asked for it, and a guard on
  it could wait for ever).
- *A latch, not a comparison of states.* A probe run's `remaining = 0` and a later reset that clears
  it again (none → 0 → none) is progress; a comparison at the next reset alone would see none and
  hold the probe for ever. So the release is decided at every evaluated cycle and kept.
- *Memory only, no persistence.* The design does not require it. Persisting would put a new record
  or state member in the ledger and make the rollback refuse it; the guard bounds idle runs to one
  per pair, so losing it at a start costs at most one more run per pair, after which the guard is
  armed again. A new catalog generation likewise releases the guards of the pairs it decides (the
  basis was taken from the old rule), and turning the key off forgets an instance's guards, which
  gives the operator a release.
- *The warning in the composer.* The resource side meets it where it removes a daily limit
  (`standard-pack check`, `package bundle --schedule`), as SS-2's tier warning; the catalog
  compiler's own warnings stay empty, so no dry-run report and no compiled catalog changes.

**Interplay.**
- *SS-2b, SS-2e.* The guard sits before placement, so judged and unjudged candidates alike are
  held before the net-benefit gate and before every Runtime deferral of "Order of the deferrals"; a
  held decision ends with `policy_no_progress`, which `ac_schedule`, the not-run explanation and
  the dispatch decision records (as `why`) show, and the idle plan counts it neither due nor as a
  wake of its own.
- *SS-5 probes.* A probe run's reading releases the guard, and the known value decides; a probe run
  that publishes nothing is spent for its period by the probe, and after the next reset the guard
  holds it until a reading comes (the key named with no admission reading).
- *The fact refresh.* A trigger made Unknown by an expired basis reading still asks the maintenance
  package for it; a refresh that reads the same value releases nothing. A held pair asks for no
  reading of its own.
- *Chains.* A held head is not dispatched, so its edge successors are not triggered; a successor
  whose trigger reads no basis key has no guard.
- *116.* The guard queues and counts nothing, so a pause holds as before and leaves no backlog;
  under `alice-116-scheduler-stop` nothing is dispatched, so no guard is armed.

**What changes live.** Nothing now: every instance is paused under ruling 116. Once the scheduler
resumes, a rule with a basis that succeeds without any of it reading another value is dispatched
once and then waits (`policy_no_progress`), on top of the daily limits the repositories still
write. A rule without a basis key (a clock rule that reads no pool, stock, remaining count or
completion time) is unchanged.

**Rollback** (to 0.12.33). 0.12.33 has no guard: nothing is in the ledger or a state file to undo,
since the guard was memory only, and every pair it held is a candidate again under its written
counts. The reasons: `policy_no_progress` appears in the ledger only as the `why` of a related
candidate in a dispatch decision record, a code value 0.12.33 reads as it reads any (the reason
chain keeps its values as a map without a key check); the `basis_readings` values never leave
memory. The configuration: 0.12.33 refuses at start and in `check-config` a file that names
`scheduling.no_progress` or an `instances[]` entry's `scheduling.no_progress` (unknown members of
the section and the entry), and acsetup and the installers never write either; **so the operator
first removes those members from the configuration file**, if a person wrote them, and checks
with 0.12.33's `check-config`. Online overrides of `scheduling.no_progress.enabled` or
`instance.<id>.scheduling.no_progress.enabled` need nothing: 0.12.33 has no such key and drops
each row (`config_override_dropped`, listed in `StartReport.instructions_dropped`) without
refusing the record. The resource tools' new warning changes no file.

| # | Shape | Kind | Code slice | First writer | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SS4-1 | `policy_no_progress` (info / none; `basis_readings` records `{fact_key; reading_value, reading_digest, observed_at_unix_ms}`, at most 32; `served_by_dispatch_unix_ms`) | new outcome code (policy) | SS-4 | the policy evaluator | a pair's decision ends with it, state `deferred`, eligibility true, no wake; `reading_value` is the reading's canonical JSON up to 128 bytes, else `reading_digest`, its SHA-256 |
| SS4-2 | keys `reading_value` (name), `reading_digest` (hash), `basis_readings` (records) | new key-table entries | SS-4 | the policy evaluator | record fields only, but `basis_readings` |
| SS4-3 | `evaluate_with_no_progress`, `NoProgressGuards`, `NoProgressMemory` (`capture`, `admit`, `observe`, `guards`), `NoProgressBasis`, `NoProgressGuard`, `BasisReading`, `MAX_NO_PROGRESS_BASIS_KEYS` (32) | policy API (memory only) | SS-4 | policy crate; runtime-host's `PolicyHost` | `evaluate_with_instance_holds` is `evaluate_with_no_progress` with no guard, so every other entry point evaluates as before |
| SS4-4 | `scheduling.no_progress.enabled` (boolean, default `true`, settable) and `instance.<id>.scheduling.no_progress.enabled` (default `section:scheduling.no_progress.enabled`, settable) | new configuration keys (**`actingd-config` revision 23**) | SS-4 | the operator, `ac_config_set`, the configuration file | read by the host for every instance of the snapshot at every evaluated cycle; a Runtime before SS-4 refuses a file that names either member |
| SS4-5 | `standard_pack_escalation_threshold_high` (warning / declaration_error; `game`, `task_id`, `count`, `limit_count` 10) | new outcome code (contract) | SS-4 | the policy composer (`StandardPackComposition::escalation_warnings`) | reported by `actinglab standard-pack check` and `package bundle --schedule` after the tier hints; a hint, never a refusal |

### 1.232 Slice SS-2g (0.12.34): a V2 consumption may declare its expected amount in thousandths, as a production may (ACM-PRICE addendum 2.1 §3.5 and §7.8, design `rd-1031/design-acm-price-addendum2.1.md`; Alice's rulings 127–129 of 10-31 13:19 and 13:22, Workflow #424 comment 6539002371; the research channel's review of addendum 2, point 2, and the coordinator's choice: the expectation is the model's, not the package's last spend; coordinator work order `rd-1031/brief-ss2g.md`)

[scheduling/README.md](scheduling/README.md) ("Expected production (v2)" becomes "Expected
quantities (v2)"; "Net benefit within a tier"; "Task Reserves"),
[scheduling/v2/README.md](scheduling/v2/README.md),
[scheduling/v2/common.schema.json](scheduling/v2/common.schema.json) (`resourceEffect`) and
[remedies.md](remedies.md) (`run_cap`) are the contract. It widens §1.225's consumption to
thousandths. The number 1.232 is the coordinator's; §1.230 (PAUSE-AUTO) and §1.231 (SS-4) are in
flight in the same release.

**What.** (1) A V2 `consumes` entry may carry `expected_amount_milli` (an integer in
`0..=2^53−1`, at most a constant capacity × 1000, `effect_incompatible` above it) instead of
`amount`; V1, the pending marker and their exclusivity are unchanged (`limit_exceeded` at the
entry). The compiler (`validation.rs`, `validate_effects`) no longer requires the production
direction for the expected quantity, and the schema's second `resourceEffect` branch no longer
fixes `direction: produce`. (2) The net benefit's consumption of a pool is `C = Σ amount × 1000 +
Σ expected_amount_milli` thousandths (`resource_targets.rs`, `declared_consumption_milli`) and its
cost `C·W·σ/(1000·Q)`, exact (`evaluator/benefit.rs`). (3) Every reader of an integer consumption
(the reserve views and the reserve gate, the unshown consumption, SS-2's tie key, the selection
fields `task.consumes.<pool>`) reads `⌈C/1000⌉`: `declared_consumption` now returns it. Before,
its `units().unwrap_or(0)` read an expected entry as 0, and the reserve gate would have left it
out. (4) SS-6's `run_cap` is absent for a task that reserves a pool it consumes by expectation, as
it is for a goal-driven production declared by expectation: `declared_amount` already answers
`None` for an entry without an integer `amount`. `spend_allowance` is unchanged. (5) Forward
projection already answers `effect_evidence_insufficient` for an expected entry in either
direction (`forward.rs`, `uncertain_effect_gap`), unchanged.

**Why.** A task the package decides at run time (which project to start, which item to buy)
spends a different amount on each run. The model gives the expectation, in general a fraction of
a unit per run, and an integer would have to be wrong. The reserve readers
round up, so a reserve is never read as safer than the expectation says, and the package's
`spend_allowance` still stops the spend. Until this slice a rule group whose effect binding gives
an expected consumption composes no catalog, so the resource side's RS-6 waits for it (addendum
2.1 §3.5).

**Unchanged.** A catalog without an expected consumption decides byte for byte as before: the net
benefit's numerator is the `amount × 1000` of before, and `⌈C/1000⌉` of whole amounts is their
sum. `B`'s formula, unknown is never 0, the regenerating discount, the gates and their order, the
one-way rule, game neutrality. A production's expected quantity reads as before. **No
configuration key, no new code, no new value, no record kind, no interface revision.**

**What changes live.** Nothing now. No production rule declares a consumption by expectation (the
resource side writes those two kinds of rule only once this slice is deployed), no pool declares a
valuation, and all five instances are paused under ruling 116 (`alice-116-scheduler-stop`).

**Rollback** (to 0.12.33). The ledger and the configuration need nothing: no shape or value is
new. The catalog: a build without SS-2g refuses a consumed `expected_amount_milli`
(`limit_exceeded` at the entry), and its start compiles each whole generation it reads: the active
one, every generation an unsettled dispatch pins, and every generation a decision memory names,
each pair's latest completed policy dispatch included (§1.225's rollback and its correction). One
such entry anywhere in a generation stops that start, whichever task the dispatch or the memory
belongs to. So before rolling back, let 0.12.34 or later activate a generation without an expected
consumption (take the entry, or its rule, out of the game roots), with no dispatch and no decision
memory naming a generation that contains one. (Corrected in SS-2d, §1.235: this paragraph first
named only the dispatches of a task that declares such an entry.)

| # | Shape | Kind | Code slice | First writer | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SS2g-1 | `expected_amount_milli` on a V2 `consumes` entry | catalog format addition | SS-2g | `acmodel bindings apply` | absent serializes as nothing |
| SS2g-2 | the net benefit's consumption in thousandths (`declared_consumption_milli`) | behaviour (evaluation, score stage) | SS-2g | the policy evaluator | exact; integer catalogs unchanged |
| SS2g-3 | `⌈C/1000⌉` (`declared_consumption`) for the reserve views and gate, the unshown consumption, the tie key and the selection fields | behaviour (evaluation) | SS-2g | the policy evaluator | rounds up |
| SS2g-4 | SS-6 `run_cap`: absent when the task reserves a pool it consumes by expectation | behaviour (evaluation) | SS-2g | the policy evaluator | `spend_allowance` unchanged |

### 1.233 Slice R-7a (0.12.35): the player hold's frozen contract and wire shapes, `runtime-client` 4 (Workflow #429; Alice's rulings 134, no cancel and no reserved shape, and 135, every channel may end a hold and the channel is recorded in `source`, 10-31 14:08–14:18, #429 comment 6539887801; the frozen design `rd-1031/design-r7a-hold-v3.1.md`, frozen in #429 comment 6540633966; coordinator work order `rd-1031/brief-r7a-impl.md`)

[player-hold.md](player-hold.md) is the contract (the normative parts of the design's §2 to §6:
the requests, the phases, the identity, the one order of the control gates, the lost-receipt
settlement with its table and H-1 to H-6, the fences, persistence, interactions, codes and the
rollout). [runtime-interface.md](runtime-interface.md) gains "Player hold request kinds" (60
kinds, 12 general instructions; R-14 must let the Lab channel take both kinds, ruling 135),
[component-interfaces.md](component-interfaces.md) the `runtime-client` 4 and `player-hold` 1
rows, [scheduling-pause.md](scheduling-pause.md) "Relation to the player hold", and
[emulator-control.md](emulator-control.md)'s WATCH-P paragraph its correction. The number 1.233
is the coordinator's; SS-2d (§1.235) is in flight in the same release; R-7a2 (the next pull
request of the release: the call sites moved to the one order, `deferral_code` removed, the fence
at position 1d, `dispatch_resource_fenced`) and R-7b (the behaviour) follow.

**What.** (1) The contract crate (`runtime/player_hold.rs`): `PlayerHoldState`, `PlayerHoldPhase`,
`PlayerHoldSource`, `PlayerHoldExpectation`, `PlayerHoldOperation` (with `phase` and
`result.pauses_at_end`), `PlayerHoldNext`, `PlayerHoldStartupPackage`, `PlayerHoldStartupChoice`
(`run` | `skip`), `PlayerHoldRestoredFrom`, `InstanceGate`, `ControlGateCode`, `ControlGates`,
`InstanceControl`, `PlayerHoldAttempt` (every member public, serializable, unknown members refused;
in R-7a, not R-7b, the coordinator's decision 1 on §8.4), `PlayerHoldSettlement`, `PlayerHoldView`,
`PlayerHoldDecision`; the two requests and the two results (`PlayerHoldAcquired`,
`PlayerHoldReleased`, inline beside `kind`); the status members `player_hold`,
`player_hold_operation` and `control` and the start report members `player_holds_restored`,
`player_holds_dropped` and `player_hold_not_durable`, all absent when empty. (2) The checks: the
drain bounds, the expectation, the source gate `(User, Ui)`, `(Cli, Cli)`, `(Lab, Lab)` after the
shape (the design's fixed order), the hold's and the record's self-checks, the answer's
`next` / `pauses_at_end` group, a hold result only on a completed receipt, and O-7 in
`RuntimeControlPlaneStatus::validate`. (3) The pure functions: `ControlGates::evaluate`,
`instance_gates`, `hold_ended_with_pause`, `settle_player_hold` (P1, P2, A1 to A13, R1 to R11),
`with_derived_control`; `PLAYER_HOLD_CLOSE_ALLOWANCE_MS` = 30 000 (decision 2: until R-7b
measures it); `player_hold_acquire_receipt_wait`, `player_hold_release_receipt_wait` and the two
receipt-read deadlines. How `with_derived_control` remembers it was called (decision 3): a flag
off the wire and outside equality, with which `with_scheduling_pause` derives again, also when an
instance already carries a `control`. (4) `runtime-client`: `prepare_acquire_player_hold`,
`prepare_release_player_hold`, `submit_acquire_player_hold`, `submit_release_player_hold`,
`acquire_player_hold`, `release_player_hold`; each request's socket read timeout (the whole
formula) and receipt-read deadline (the formula without IO, cut to the session deadline), so a
receipt that never comes is `runtime_receipt_timeout`; the settlement of a dropped or timed-out
receipt from one `Status` read, with the post-conditions (same epoch: the new connection in
place; another epoch: a temporary client reads, the handle latched `runtime_owner_epoch_changed`;
unreadable: latched with that failure); `runtime_player_hold_unconfirmed` among the uncertain
codes, `runtime_player_hold_settled` among the codes that settle without a receipt;
`player_hold_settlement()` and `player_hold_attempt()`. (5) The host answers both kinds
`not_implemented` (`operation` `acquire_player_hold`, `release_player_hold`) on every channel,
records nothing and fills no new member, as R-0. (6) The codes, keys and vocabularies of the
design's §6.1, `since` 0.12.35, the ones R-7a never produces included (`player_hold_fact_untagged`
among them; `player_hold_interrupted` warning, not uncertain, decision 4), and
`emulator_autostart_skip_reason` `player_held`. (7) `component-interfaces.json` declares
`runtime-client` [2, 4].

**Deviations from the design's wording, no shape change.** (a) The four effective codes are
`dispatch_*` codes of runtime-host, which the contract crate cannot build, so `control.code` and
`ControlGates::code()` are the contract's vocabulary `control_gate_code`, whose tokens are those
four spellings; the host maps it to its code (R-7a2). (b) Value keys the design names but the key
table cannot take: `phase` is the install phase's key (`hold_phase`), `final` is a Rust keyword
(`settlement_final`), `outcome` names the envelope (`settlement_outcome`, also the decision's
member), and an instance alias is `alias`; the settlement's other values take the same prefixes
(`settlement_rule`, `settlement_trigger`, `settlement_observed`, `hold_revision`, `hold_next`,
`hold_restored`). (c) A missing `source.channel` does not decode, rather than decoding and failing
`invalid_player_hold_state`: the member is required. (d) In rows A7 and R8 the settlement is typed
only, so `runtime_operation_unsupported` keeps its registration. (e) EC's and SP's "按 R-7a §2.6"
sentences (the design's §2.6 rows 7 and 8) go with R-7a2, which changes those orders (the design's
§7.1).

**Why.** A person who plays on a device must hold it against every automatic mechanism, and the
console, the CLI, MCP and the Lab must read one state and one code (ruling 135). Ruling 116's five
pauses make a hold built as a pause impossible. The console pins the shapes once, before the
behaviour (§6.2's three steps).

**Unchanged.** Every existing request, answer and status member, the pause table and its fact, the
dispatch order (`deferral_code` stays global first until R-7a2), the watch, the autostart, IDLE-1,
the ledger and the configuration (no key; the default tag list is R-7b's). A console of
`runtime-client` 3 reads every 0.12.35 answer, since none carries a new member.

**What changes live.** Nothing: no request of the new kinds is sent, and the Runtime would refuse
it.

**Rollback** (to 0.12.34). Nothing is persisted and no behaviour is undone: roll back as usual. A
console already on revision 4 that sends a new request to 0.12.34 has its connection dropped; its
client reconnects in the same owner epoch and reports `runtime_operation_unsupported` (rows A7,
R8), the handle usable. 0.12.34 declares `runtime-client` [2, 3], so an installer of [4, 4] (R-7b's)
would not update to it; R-7a itself declares [2, 4] and rolls back freely.

### 1.234 Slice R-7a2 (0.12.35): every dispatch site takes its code from the one order of the control gates; the fence defers at position 1d with `dispatch_resource_fenced` (Workflow #429; R-7a's second pull request; the coordinator's decision of 10-31 14:4x on the design's §8.2 item 9: the order player hold → instance pause → global pause → resource fence and its two behaviour changes are confirmed, an engineering consistency rather than a product choice, and R-7a2 ships in R-7a's release, in production before 114-B; the frozen design `rd-1031/design-r7a-hold-v3.1.md` §2.6 and §7.1 "R-7a2"; coordinator work order `rd-1031/brief-r7a2.md`)

[player-hold.md](player-hold.md), "The one order of the control gates" (R-7a §2.6), is the
contract. [scheduling-pause.md](scheduling-pause.md) ("The dispatch gate"),
[scheduling-blackout.md](scheduling-blackout.md) ("Order of the deferrals": position 1 is split
into 1a to 1d), [scheduling/README.md](scheduling/README.md) (the pause paragraph, the fact
refresh's holds and the clock-slot row "control") and [emulator-control.md](emulator-control.md)
(`startup_package_withheld` names the instance's pause by that order) follow it: the design's §2.6
rows 7 and 8, which §1.233 (e) left to this slice. The number 1.234 is the coordinator's; it builds
on §1.233 (R-7a, merged at its base f57f7d20). R-7b (the player hold's behaviour) follows; 114-A
(§1.236) and R-15b (§1.237) may be in flight in the same release.

**What.** (1) `SchedulingPauseTable::deferral_code` (the global pause first) is removed. The pause
table gives `control_gates(alias, resource_fence)`: `ControlGates::evaluate` with the player hold
false until R-7b, the instance's own pause in any stage, the global pause and the fence its caller
read at the same step. The host maps the contract's `control_gate_code` back to its runtime-host
code in one place (`control_gates.rs`: `host_code`, `effective_code`), and a test holds every word
against the registered code word by word, so a rename on either side fails until both change.
(2) Policy evaluation (§2.6 rows 4a and 5): as a cycle starts, beside the pause snapshot, the
aliases of every fenced instance (any stage) are read once; the closure's position 1 is the
effective code of the instance's control gates (1a to 1d), position 2 its queue as before. A fenced
instance's candidate is `Deferred` with `dispatch_resource_fenced` (value `instance_id`, the
alias) and no wake. The fact refresh's holds and its `gate_code` (row 4b) take the same code, so an
instance a control gate holds raises no fact refresh demand. ScheduleExplanation follows the
evaluation (row 5). (3) Policy admission (row 4c): under the admission lock the control gates are
read now, in the same order, before the instance's queue, the performance and the capacity gates;
the refusal is the effective code: `dispatch_paused_instance` with both pauses,
`dispatch_resource_fenced` (value `instance_id`, the instance's opaque identifier, as the queue's
refusal names it) for an intent evaluated before the fence. The fence's former check after the
performance gate (`instance_resources_fenced`) is gone. (4) The clock slot's gate class
`OperatorPause` is renamed `Control` and takes `dispatch_resource_fenced` (row 4e): a fenced due
slot is `clock_slot_deferred` at first sight; `dispatch_player_held` joins it with R-7b. (5) The
recovery ladder's A6 (row 4d) reads only whether a pause holds the instance (`pauses`), as before.
(6) The descriptions of `dispatch_paused_global`, `dispatch_paused_instance`,
`dispatch_resource_fenced`, `instance_resources_fenced` and `clock_slot_deferred` say so; no
category, value, key or `since` changes. R-7a2 is the first writer of `dispatch_resource_fenced`
(§1.233 R7A-6 names R-7b for the host codes; for this one it is R-7a2).

**Unchanged.** Every wire shape and status member: no `control` is filled, `runtime-client` stays
[2, 4]. The pause table, its fact and its revisions; the routine gate and the instance's queue; the
fence itself, its ladder, its recheck and its lift. A device request that meets a fence, and the
fence's own records, keep `instance_resources_fenced` (§2.6 O-1). The recovery ladder's admission;
the watch, the daemon-start autostart and IDLE-1 (`automatic_start_hold`); the configuration, the
ledger's shapes and the state files.

**What changes live.** (a) With both pauses in effect the reason and the admission's refusal are
`dispatch_paused_instance`, before `dispatch_paused_global`. Ruling 116's five instances keep
`dispatch_paused_instance` whether the global pause is set or lifted, so ScheduleExplanation's
`why` stays and its `since_unix_ms` no longer restarts; so do the fact refresh's `gate_code`, the
rejection records and 114's history. (b) A fenced instance: the admission refuses an intent
evaluated before the fence with `dispatch_resource_fenced` (info / none) instead of
`instance_resources_fenced` (error / environment_fault), so counts by error category see fewer
rows. A candidate reaches the closure only past its placement: on an instance whose device the host
self-checks (every emulator instance), the fence also withholds its policy availability (Workflow
#403), so its candidates stay `Blocked` with `instance_unavailable` at placement, before position 1,
as they did before this slice; position 1d decides for an instance whose availability the fence
does not withhold, and at admission. (c) In production all five instances carry ruling 116's pause,
so nothing is dispatched either way.

**Rollback** (to 0.12.34). Nothing is persisted and no shape changed: roll back as usual. 0.12.34
puts the global pause first again and refuses a fenced instance at admission with
`instance_resources_fenced`. The records 0.12.35 wrote keep their codes: `dispatch_resource_fenced`
rides only in existing reason chains, rejection outcomes and a clock-slot record's `gate_code`,
which 0.12.34 reads as it reads any code, its values kept as a map without a key check (§1.231's
rollback), and whose suspension report reads a clock-slot record's `gate_code` as any received
code (`CodeStr`). The configuration and the state files need nothing.

### 1.235 Slice SS-2d (0.12.35): a judged candidate whose net benefit is within its rounding error is neither positive nor negative; a model-verified realization task may run in the last place of its tier (Alice's ruling 127, 10-31 13:19 「127我认同你的判断」, the review's version, Workflow #424 comment 6538837139 §4 and the coordinator's record 6539002371: cost discounts only where overflow or regeneration loss is verifiable; the zero reduced-value fallback only for necessary realization or conversion tasks with a real downstream use and verifiable progress, bound by eligibility, the reserve line, failure and no-progress guards, never a zero-benefit loop; design `rd-1031/design-acm-price-addendum2.1.md` §7; coordinator work order `rd-1031/brief-ss2d.md`)

[scheduling/README.md](scheduling/README.md) ("Net benefit within a tier", "Within tolerance"),
[scheduling/v2/README.md](scheduling/v2/README.md) (`benefit_realization`),
[scheduling/v2/tasks.schema.json](scheduling/v2/tasks.schema.json),
[standard-pack-schedule.md](standard-pack-schedule.md) ("The realization mark", the rule member
`realization` and the count) and [resource-targets.md](resource-targets.md) ("Net benefit") are
the contract. It narrows §1.225 (2) and reads §1.232's thousandths. The number 1.235 is the
coordinator's; §1.233 (R-7a) and §1.234 (R-7a2) are in flight in other crates. It depends on
§1.231 (SS-4, the no-progress guard) and §1.232 (SS-2g), both merged at its base f64b3a12.

**What.** (1) A judged candidate's exact sum `S` (before the floor) has the rounding bound
`ε = Σ_produces [R/(2000·Q) + n·(2W+1)/(4000·Q)] + Σ_consumes σ·[C/(2000·Q) + m·(2W+1)/(4000·Q)]`,
with `R` and `C` the per-run production and consumption in thousandths (`per_run_yield`,
SS-2g's `declared_consumption_milli`), `n` and `m` the pool's `expected_amount_milli` entries in
each direction, `W` the weight `B` reads and `σ` the regenerating share; an exact rational the
evaluator sums as it sums `S` (`evaluator/benefit.rs`, `judge`). `|S| ≤ ε` is within tolerance:
`benefit_within_tolerance` (info; `benefit_milli` ⌊S⌋, `tolerance_milli` ⌈ε⌉, `zero_tier`; the
developer text adds `sum=` and `tolerance=` as exact reduced fractions). Outside the band the gate
is §1.225's: `B = ⌊S⌋ > 0` ranks by `B ÷ E` as before, any other known `B` is
`policy_benefit_nonpositive` as before (a `B` of 0 with `S > ε` included, so the band only carves
out of the two old outcomes). (2) A V2 task may carry `benefit_realization: true`, composed from
the `schedule.json` rule member `"realization": true`, which only `acmodel bindings apply` writes
from the model's verdict. The compiler (`validation.rs`, `validate_realization` and
`validate_realization_cycles`) requires `benefit_judged: true` (`missing_required_field` at
`benefit_judged`), a `consumes` and a `produces` entry (`missing_required_field` at the empty
list), a reserve on every consumed pool (`missing_required_field` at `reserves`), a fact reading
of every consumed pool (`effect_incompatible` at the entry) and no cycle among the marked tasks
through their pools (`realization_cycle` at each one's `benefit_realization`). The compiler binds
no task to an instance, so the cycle check is over the marked tasks of the whole catalog by pool
id, stricter than per instance; a composed catalog's ids are per instance already once a rule is
copied to two. V1 refuses the member (`unknown_field`). The reader takes `realization` out of the
rule (`ScheduleRule::realization`; only `true`, and never beside `"maintenance": true`), the
composer refuses it on a rule whose package is maintenance-role and refuses a rule that writes
`benefit_realization` (`schedule_invalid` at the member), maps `realization_cycle` back to the
rule's `realization`, and counts the marked judged rules (`BenefitCoverage.realization`). (3) A
marked candidate within tolerance whose `B` is known, that produces a pool weighed above 0 on its
instance and whose latest run there did not fail is released (`zero_tier: released`): it takes
part in the allocation after every unjudged and every positive judged candidate of the business
tier, of every instance (`PlacementCandidate.zero_tier`, `allocation_order`), a promotion not
lifting it, among such candidates by `affinity`, SS-2's key and the hash; every gate before and
after it applies, the reserve gate, the shared run limits, every pause and hold, and SS-4's
no-progress guard included (the guard's basis holds the readings of the pools it reserves, which
are every pool it consumes). Any other candidate within tolerance is deferred with `zero_tier`
`unmarked`, `no_downstream_value` or `latest_failed`, waking at a regenerating pool's next step as
a not-positive one does. (4) The idle plan counts no decision within tolerance that was not
selected as due or as a wake of its own (`schedule_explanation.rs`, `IdleDraft::add`).

**Why.** Ruling 127 (ii), the review's version: a conversion at the margin of the modelled steady
state has a reduced value of exactly 0, and the pools' rounding then gives `B` a sign of a few
milli in either direction; §1.225 dispatched the positive ones and held the negative ones, so a
necessary realization never ran and a zero-value conversion could run as if positive. The bound
is computed from the two roundings the sum contains (the exported weight, half to even, and each
expected quantity, half to even), not guessed; only the model knows whether a task has a real
downstream use and whether one more run wastes anything, so the task carries the model's verdict.
Ruling 127 (i): §1.225's discount already applies only to a regenerating projection, the
declaration that regeneration (or a store's production) is lost at capacity; a non-regenerating
pool costs `W` however full it is, and that is unchanged.

**Unchanged.** `B`'s formula, the regenerating discount, unknown is never 0, the tiers, SS-2e's
chain riding (a successor of a business link is not judged and never within tolerance), manual
requests, maintenance tasks, the reserve gate's steps, SS-6's spend values, the one-way rule,
game neutrality. A catalog in which no judged candidate falls within tolerance decides, ranks and
records byte for byte as with §1.225 and §1.229; a catalog without `benefit_realization` keeps its
hash. **No configuration key.**

**New codes and keys.** `benefit_within_tolerance` (policy code, info), because no code says "the
sign of this benefit is within its rounding error"; values `tolerance_milli` (integer) and
`zero_tier` (vocabulary `zero_tier`: `released`, `unmarked`, `no_downstream_value`,
`latest_failed`); the catalog diagnostic `realization_cycle` (policy code, error, prefix
`realization_`), because no diagnostic says "these tasks form a cycle"; the V2 task member
`benefit_realization`; the `schedule.json` rule member `realization`; the tools' count
`benefit_coverage.realization`. No new ledger record kind, no interface revision.

**What changes live.** Nothing now: no pool declares a valuation, no rule carries the mark, and
all five instances are paused under ruling 116 (`alice-116-scheduler-stop`). Once values exist and
the scheduler resumes on Alice's word, a candidate whose `S` is within `ε` is no longer dispatched
as positive on a rounding remainder, and a marked realization runs only when its instance has
nothing of positive benefit.

**Rollback** (to 0.12.34). The ledger: the new code and its values ride only in existing reason
chains (a released candidate's dispatch carries `benefit_within_tolerance` in its chain, and a
deferred one may be a related candidate's `why`), which 0.12.34 reads as it reads any code, its
values kept as a map without a key check (§1.231's rollback). The configuration and the state
files: nothing is new. The catalog: a build without SS-2d refuses a task's `benefit_realization`
(`unknown_field`) and a rule's `realization` (it reaches the composed task, `unknown_field`, so
`schedule_invalid` at the rule), and its start compiles each whole generation it reads: the active
one, every generation an unsettled dispatch pins, and every generation a decision memory names,
each pair's latest completed policy dispatch included. So before rolling back, let 0.12.35 or
later activate a generation without the member (take `realization` out of the game roots), with no
dispatch and no decision memory naming a generation that carries it; while the scheduler is
stopped on every instance no such dispatch exists. The tools' new count is output only.

**Also in this slice.** §1.232's rollback paragraph is corrected to the whole-generation wording
(the coordinator's correction of 10-31, from the 0.12.34 release check): a 0.12.33 start compiles
each whole generation it reads, so no dispatch or decision memory may name a generation that
contains an expected consumption, whichever task it belongs to.

| SS2d-2 | `benefit_within_tolerance` with `benefit_milli`, `tolerance_milli`, `zero_tier` | new policy code and values | SS-2d | the policy evaluator | info; on a released candidate's decision too |
| SS2d-3 | V2 task member `benefit_realization`; `schedule.json` rule member `realization`; `BenefitCoverage.realization` | catalog format addition, tools output addition | SS-2d | `acmodel bindings apply` | absent serializes as nothing; the compiler's four requirements and `realization_cycle` |
| SS2d-4 | `allocation_order`: the released candidates last in the business tier, a promotion not lifting them | behaviour (evaluation) | SS-2d | — | only when a candidate is released; otherwise the order of before |
| SS2d-5 | the idle plan: a decision within tolerance that was not selected is neither due nor a wake | behaviour (runtime-host, IDLE-1) | SS-2d | `schedule_explanation.rs` (`IdleDraft::add`) | as SS2b-7, its own wake excluded too |

### 1.236 Slice 114-A (0.12.36): the "why it did not run" record's shapes, the ledger's own copies, the index prefixes, ledger revision 5 and every vocabulary, reader first (Alice's 114 of 10-30 23:2x–23:3x, method 2: only the changes are copied and updated incrementally; her 118 A, 119 A and 120 A of 10-31 13:22, relayed from the AC审计 window, Workflow #386 comment 6539002530; the frozen design `rd-1031/design-114-reasons-v5.md` with the coordinator's freeze addendum `rd-1031/design-114-reasons-v5-freeze-addendum.md`, which wins where they differ, after the UI channel's last review of v5; coordinator work order `rd-1031/brief-114a.md`)

[ledger-observer.md](ledger-observer.md) §11.8 is the contract of the record and §11.1 names its two
keys; [scheduling/README.md](scheduling/README.md), "Why A Candidate Does Not Run", says what it

R-15b (§1.237) may be in flight in the same release. 114-B (the recorder and the write side),
114-C (the start) and 114-D (`ScheduleHistory`, `runtime-client` 5) follow.

**What.** (1) The record type `policy.not_run_changed` (family `policy`, action

common head (`NotRunHead`: `instance_alias`, `stream`, `prev`, `base`, `evaluated_at_unix_ms`,
`eval_seq`, `catalog_hash`, `budget`, `prior?`, `closes?`), the four kinds' members
(`NotRunChange`, `NotRunBaseline`, `NotRunSuppressed`, `NotRunRetired`), `NotRunPrior`,
`NotRunCloses`, `NotRunRow`, `NotRunSummary`, `NotRunFrom`, `NotRunTo`, `NotRunGone`,
`NotRunSelected`, and the ledger's own copies `NotRunControl` (`NotRunPlayerHold`,
`NotRunGlobalPause`, `NotRunInstancePause`, `NotRunResourceFence`, `effective`) and

compact JSON), the closed vocabularies (decoded), the self-consistency that depends on no code
(design §2.1 item 3 and the freeze addendum) and the spelling of every code
(`validate_policy_token`: `why`, a row's `from.code`, every `dispatch_code`, the fence's `cause`,
the operation's `code` and `selfcheck_failure_code`). Shape refusals are `invalid_policy_payload`
(`codes.rs:958` on f57f7d20; the design's `:940`); a spelling keeps `invalid_policy_token` and the
catalog hash `invalid_catalog_hash`, the rules every policy record shares. No code is added. (3)
The index (`global/index.rs`, `not_run_keys` in `tagged_keys`, so `row_names_record` and
`names_key` follow): `not_run/<alias>/<task>` (`NOT_RUN_INDEX_PREFIX`) for each key a change set
changes, a baseline part's `rows`, `selected` and `gone`, a retirement's `gone`, and
`not_run_stream/<alias>` (`NOT_RUN_STREAM_INDEX_PREFIX`) for every record. (4) The vocabularies,
plain enums with their frozen order (`ALL`), not outcome vocabularies: the ledger's fifteen
(`not_run_kind`, `not_run_baseline_reason`, `not_run_gone_reason`, `not_run_dispatch`,
`not_run_layer`, `not_run_value_gate`, `not_run_class`, `not_run_candidate_state`,
`not_run_candidate_eligibility`, `not_run_instance_pause_stage`, `not_run_previous_close`,
`not_run_suppressed_unknown`, `not_run_retired_reason`, `not_run_trigger`, `not_run_check`), the
ledger's copies of R-7a's eight (`instance_gate`, `player_hold_phase`,
`player_hold_source_actor`, `player_hold_operation_kind`, `player_hold_operation_state`,
`player_hold_next`, `player_hold_startup_package`, `player_hold_restored_from`) with `channel`,
`via` and `startup_package_withheld`, and the eleven of `ScheduleHistory`
(`runtime/schedule_history.rs`: `schedule_history_scope`, `_task_kind`, `_precision`,
`_unknown_because`, `_inconsistent_kind`, `_incomplete_because`, `_dispatch`, `_head_state`,
`_close`, `_retired_reason`, `_segment_role`), which 114-D uses without adding a word. (5)
`component-interfaces.json` declares `ledger` [3, 5].

**The R-7a alignment** (the freeze addendum §2, six items, no shape change). (1) The value key of
114-B's check code is `not_run_check`, named as R-7a's settlement keys are (`settlement_rule`,
`keys.rs:662`, not `rule`); the instance alias of its values is the existing key `alias`
(`keys.rs:15`). (2) `ControlGates::code()` returns `Option<ControlGateCode>`, not a `Code`: 114-B's
write side compares a control row's `why` and 114-D's reader turns a written `effective` into its
code through `InstanceGate::code()` and R-7a2's host mapping. (3) A hold or operation `source`
without `channel` does not decode; it is not a `validate` refusal. (4) The hold copy carries every
condition of R-7a's `PlayerHoldState::validate` (revision and since not 0; both deadlines in the
three acquire phases and neither after, stricter than the design's "only in"; `close_started`
only in `handing_back`; `reached_held` never while acquiring nor on a hold restored from
`acquiring`, otherwise present; the two `restored_*` together; `via` only on `lab`) and the
operation copy every condition of `PlayerHoldOperation::validate` on its flattened result (by
state, by kind, the identity of an acquire with the ended hold, since not 0, R-7a §3.2's result
self-check without the complete `selfcheck` the copy does not keep); an operation's `phase` and
`failed_phase` are never `held`, a ledger tightening of R-7a's five words. (5) The reused
vocabularies are the ledger's own enums; a guard test holds each word for word equal to R-7a's
`ALL`, and `channel`, `via`, `startup_package_withheld`, `InstancePauseStage` and
`ScheduleExplanation`'s three enums by an exhaustive match from the source. (6) The file:line
citations here are checked on f57f7d20.

**The freeze addendum's other items in this slice.** `retired{recorder_faulted}` names the failed
write-side check as `check` (words of `not_run_check`; minor 10), which only that reason carries
and which carries no `gone`; the precision word of ruling 118 A's class is `turn`, not `class`
(minor 11). `head.retired`, `head.state` and the answer's `HeadPrior` are 114-D's shapes: this
slice freezes their words only (`schedule_history_head_state` with `recorder_faulted`;
`head.retired.reason` uses `not_run_retired_reason`); the record's `Prior` keeps
`first_evaluated_at_unix_ms` required (§1).

**Checks beyond the design's list, all shape only.** A change set carries at least one of
`entries`, `control`, `summary` and `player_hold_end` (design §2.5: it is empty only when one of
the others is there); a baseline part's `base` is `null` exactly on part 1 (§2.2); the pause
copies' `pause_reason` is the existing name type `SchedulingPauseReason` (`1..=64` bytes of
`[a-z0-9_.-]`), not a vocabulary; the alias passes `validate_instance_alias` and `catalog_hash`
the policy records' `validate_catalog_hash`.

**Why.** A reader that refuses a record stops a Runtime's start (the newest
`open_verify_tail_records` records are authenticated) and fails a whole page online and offline
(design §1.9 item 1), so the reader ships a release before the first writer and checks only what
changes with the shape; codes, the golden table and the gates' order are the write side's.

**Unchanged.** Every existing record, the SQLite format, `actingcommand.event.v3`, the tables, the
indexes and every view's type list (so the view DDL), every request and answer, the
configuration, the policy and the host's behaviour. The host's dispatch recovery refuses the new
type as it refuses the other value records (`policy_host.rs`, `PolicyRecoveryQueryMismatch`); it
never queries it.

**What changes live.** Nothing is written. The update needs `actingctl install
--accept-ledger-one-way` (R*.max 5 > Rp.max 4, logged), and the deploy record checks that the
console in use declares `ledger` with max ≥ 5 (UI-0a, pinned to this slice's pull request head,
≥ R-7a), as design §11.2 and §11.7 require: until UI-2a, no installer checks the console's edge.

**Rollback** (to 0.12.35). 0.12.35 declares `ledger` [3, 4]. `actingctl install` refuses the
rollback (Rp.max 5 is not in [3, 4]) whether or not a revision-5 record exists, as for revision 4;
going back before 114-A is outside the guarantee (Alice 10-11, no old-version compatibility), and
the deploy note says so. What an older Runtime would do with revision 5: 114-A writes no record,
so a ledger of 0.12.36 holds none and a 0.12.35 Runtime put back by hand reads it; once 114-B has
written one, a Runtime of 0.12.35 or earlier cannot decode it (`EventType` has no catch-all,
`corrupt_ledger_record`): its start fails while such a record is among the newest
`open_verify_tail_records` records, and an online or offline page that holds one fails whole
(`runtime_receipt_decode_failed` on a console pinned before 114-A). From 114-A on, a rollback
within revision 5 is free: this reader reads a later build's records with codes or golden-table
classes it does not know.

`convert_checks` values and inventory; the two old sentences of "Formal stop, start and the hold"
(a stopped Runtime gets `install start`, never `release-hold`); "Tools never deletes anything" kept

(2) The contract crate (`installation/selection_v2.rs`): `InstallSelectionV2`, `InstallSlotDocument`,
`InstallMemberIdentity`, `InstallSelectionMembers`, `InstallSlotMember`, `InstallSlotMembers`, with

`INSTALL_SELECTION_V2_SCHEMA`, `INSTALL_SLOT_SCHEMA`, `INSTALL_SLOT_DOCUMENT_FILE`,

`ENTRY_NO_DIALOG_ENV` (`ACTINGCOMMAND_ENTRY_NO_DIALOG`); no consumer calls them. (3) The release

beside another release zip. (4) The codes and words of the block, `since` 0.12.35: 28
`install_refusal`, 19 `install_caveat`, 1 `release_check` (`selection_schema_mismatch`) and 5
`install_guard` tokens in the vocabularies and their enums; 34 catalog vocabularies of the read

`install_attempt_phase` …); the keys `attempt_phase`, `hold_reason`, `s0_from`,

**Deviations from the design's wording, no shape change.** (a) The refusals the design calls fatal

0.12.34, whose reader refuses the folder (`zip_set`), but its `undo` takes it as any stage; finish
or undo it before rolling back. Roll back with the single-location `rollback` as usual.

### 1.238 Slice R-0b (0.12.36): `Status.activity` filled for all seven kinds, `runtime-client` [3, 4] (Workflow #429 contract item 4 and the A.8 row R-0b, `rd-1029/429-A-runtime.md`; the console's second progress line, its stop button and the global pause's "finishing" read what each instance does now; coordinator work order `rd-1031/brief-r0b.md`)

[runtime-interface.md](runtime-interface.md) gains "What an instance does now
(`RuntimeInstanceStatus.activity`)" under "Workbench request kinds": what each kind shows while,
its `request_id` and `package_id`, the end of every activity however it ends, and the rule for
more than one at once; the interface table's `activity` row and rule 3 of its revision rules say
R-0b fills it. [component-interfaces.md](component-interfaces.md)'s `runtime-client` revision-3 row
names 0.12.36 as the release that raises `min` to 3. The number 1.238 is the coordinator's; R-4
(§1.239) and R-11 (§1.240) are in flight in the same release.

**What.** (1) The host keeps every instance's activities in memory (`host/instance_activity.rs`, a
leaf lock holding no ledger handle): each begins with a guard and leaves when the guard drops. The
seven kinds begin where the table of the contract says: the policy run and the direct run before
their execution (their package read, with the run's request and its `package_id`), the host's run
(a startup package on its claim, a ladder rung's package on the ladder's key), an instance resume's
reconnect, a `SelfCheckInstance` from its grant and the daemon start's preparation, an emulator
start, stop or restart (one control across a restart's phases; a ladder's restart rung on the
ladder's key), and a ladder from its grant until just before its key's release. `since_unix_ms` is
the Runtime clock's wall reading (the clock seam). (2) `Status` reads the table, and nothing else,
before the registry lock and fills each instance's `activity` with the one the rule shows; an
instance with none has no member. (3) The rule for more than one at once: an activity that took
the instance's key itself before one on another activity's key, then the one that began last (the
order they began, not the clock). (4) The location `begin_instance_activity` (`since` 0.12.36) for
a failure to register an activity, fatal as every poisoned host lock is; no outcome code is added.
(5) `distribution/windows/component-interfaces.json` declares `runtime-client` [3, 4].

**Why this rule.** The work order's preference, the activity that holds the instance's lease or
fence first and then the most recent, made precise on the key: every activity that occupies an
instance either took its key (lease or claim) or runs on the key another activity holds, so the
key holder is what the instance does and what decides when it is free again, and a borrowed-key
activity is one step of it (a ladder shows over its rung's run and over its emulator restart). The
key passes from one activity to the next while the first still ends (an emulator control hands its
key to its startup package), and then the later one is what the instance does. "Most recent" is
the order of beginning, so a wall clock that steps back cannot reorder two activities.

**Clients of revision 3 or more.** actingctl (its MCP included) and actinglab of the same build
read and send through the workspace's `actingcommand-contract` and `actingcommand-runtime-client`,
which carry every revision-3 and revision-4 shape (`activity` since 0.12.30); `mcp-entry` only pipes
JSON-RPC to actingctl. The UI's v0.12.0 and v0.12.1 declare [3, 4].

**Unchanged.** Every request and answer shape (`activity` has had its shape since 0.12.30), the
ledger (nothing appended, nothing read for it), the configuration, the codes, the dispatch order,
the leases and the claims.

**What changes live.** `Status` carries `activity` for an instance that does one of the seven
kinds; a reader of revision 2 refuses such a status, which is why `min` rises. As the installer,
this build no longer meets a live build whose `runtime-client` `max` is 2
(`installer_meets_previous`): an update reaches 0.12.36 from 0.12.30 or later (production runs
0.12.34 or later).

**Rollback** (to 0.12.35). Nothing persisted: roll back as usual. 0.12.35 answers no `activity`; it
declares [2, 4], which still meets a console of [3, 4].

### 1.240 Slice R-11 (0.12.36): a game root's optional `ui.json`, and `task_ids` and the Runtime-derived `irreversible` on the installation rows of `actingctl packs` and `ac_packs` (Workflow #429 A.7.3 and A.7.4, the R-11 rows of A.7.4 and A.8 of `rd-1029/429-A-runtime.md`; the coordinator's decisions recorded there: offline, no revision bump, `irreversible` in the package rows; coordinator work order `rd-1031/brief-r11.md`)

[package-reference.md](package-reference.md) ("Standard package root", `ui.json`),
[runtime-interface.md](runtime-interface.md) (the `packs` row) and
[standard-pack-schedule.md](standard-pack-schedule.md) ("The readers of composer mode") are the
contract. The number 1.240 is the coordinator's; R-0b (§1.238) and R-4 (§1.239) are in flight in
the same release. Nothing persisted, no wire shape of the Runtime and no interface revision
changes: `actingctl packs` and `ac_packs` read the install root offline, as before.

**What.** (1) The contract crate (`standard_pack_ui.rs`): `STANDARD_PACK_UI_FILE` (`ui.json`),
`STANDARD_PACK_UI_SCHEMA_VERSION` (`actingcommand.ui.v1`), the limits `MAX_STANDARD_PACK_UI_BYTES`,
`MAX_STANDARD_PACK_UI_ISSUES` and `MAX_PACK_UI_*`, `StandardPackUi` (the document as written, its
member order kept; `pack(package_id)`, `display()`), `parse_standard_pack_ui` (shape, limits and
references only, every violation at its JSON pointer, at most 64, no string interpreted) and
`read_standard_pack_root_with_ui` (`read_standard_pack_root`, and `ui.json` without `bundle.json`
is `bundle_missing`). (2) `actingctl packs` / `ac_packs`: each game of `standard_packs` carries
`ui` and `display`; each composed installation row carries `task_ids` (the composed tasks of its
package, in id order, until SS-7), `irreversible` (an entry of the package's `control.json`
`provides` declares `irreversible: true`, read with the contract's `ProvidedCapability` as the
Runtime reads it) and, from its game's valid `ui.json`, `ui` (the package's entry) and `display`.
(3) The `standard_pack_problem` tokens `ui_out_of_limits`, `ui_duplicate`, `ui_group_unknown` and
`ui_parameter_undeclared` (`since` 0.12.36); the codes `standard_pack_root_invalid` (each
violation of a refused `ui.json`; reused tokens `malformed`, `game_mismatch`, `package_not_listed`,
`bundle_missing`) and `package_binding_unreadable` (a `ui.json` or composed package's control file
that cannot be read) are reused, their descriptions extended. No code, key or location is new.

**Decisions within the work order.** (a) Package-level parameter declarations (A.7.2) arrive with
R-10; until then no package declares one, so any name under a pack's `parameters` is
`ui_parameter_undeclared`, and a valid file has none. R-10 gives the check its declarations.
(b) An aspect ratio is checked for the form `<w>:<h>` only, its numbers never used; every other
string is opaque and only measured in bytes. (c) A refused `ui.json`, like a refused table, never
breaks its game root, and `ui.json` alone makes a directory a game root for its readers only
(`bundle_missing` there); the Runtime's root reader and check-config do not read the file.
(d) `task_ids`, `irreversible`, `ui` and `display` are on composed rows (composer mode) only: a
catalog-mode binding has no game root and no composition, and its rows are unchanged.
(e) `irreversible` is absent, with `package_binding_unreadable`, when the package's control file
cannot be read, is over 1 MiB or does not decode; the row is listed.

**Why.** UI-3b needs, before SS-7, which tasks run each package and the Runtime's own risk mark,
and a place for each pack's display names that the Runtime never interprets (A.7.3).

**What changes live.** `actingctl packs` and `ac_packs` in composer mode add `task_ids` and
`irreversible` to every composed row, and a `package_binding_unreadable` warning for a composed
package without a readable `control.json`. A game root without `ui.json` answers as before
otherwise; no resource repository's standard package carries one yet.

**Rollback** (to 0.12.35). Nothing persisted changes; the members disappear from the answer and a
`ui.json` is ignored again.

### 1.241 Slice LN-VERIFY (0.12.36): `ledger-maintenance verify` is the start's bounded check by default, and the complete read moves behind `--full` (#422; brief rd-1031/brief-ln-verify.md)

[ledger-maintenance.md](ledger-maintenance.md) ("`verify` of a formal root"),
[install-cli.md](install-cli.md) ("Ledger verify"),
[component-interfaces.md](component-interfaces.md),
[ledger-observer.md](ledger-observer.md) (§15), [ledger-store.md](ledger-store.md),
[runtime-database.md](runtime-database.md), [runtime-config.md](runtime-config.md) and
[actingd-check-config.md](actingd-check-config.md) are the contract. The number 1.241 is the
coordinator's. No code, key, location, schema or interface revision is new; `ledger_observer.open_verify_tail_records`
gains a reader.

**What.** (1) `actingd ledger-maintenance verify --config <config>` on a formal root, without flags,
reports the new `status` word `verified-sqlite-bounded`: `LedgerMaintenance::verify_formal_bounded`
runs `verify_open_tail`, the start's own check (`TailOpen::Maintenance`: the format and the views,
the keyed meta row and head, `MAX(sequence)`, the newest `open_verify_tail_records` records, each
authenticated with this binary's decoder), plus the contiguity of the stored sequences
(`verify_sequence_extent`), on `open_existing_unchecked`. It reads no older record and no State
table, runs no whole-file `quick_check(1)` and no `maintenance_digest`, does not look at the
retention state (the next start completes an unsettled eviction, as it always does) and takes none
of the writer's steps. (2) `--full` (`LedgerMaintenanceRequest::full`) is the complete read as it
was, `verified-sqlite`; `--frame-query` implies it; another operation refuses it
(`maintenance_arguments_invalid`). (3) A Segment or candidate root behaves as before. (4) Exit codes
and the failure shape do not change: the same code and operation as the complete read for the same
damage, with the `ledger_open_measured` note link once the read is under way.

**Decisions within the work order.** (a) The tail is `ledger_observer.open_verify_tail_records` from
the file (`ActingdConfigFile::maintenance_manifest`), so that the check authenticates as many records
as the start; only that member reaches the manifest, only for `verify` without flags, and a value the
key does not take is `maintenance_config_invalid`. (b) `RuntimeStateStore::from_database`'s validation
does not run in the bounded mode either: it does not authenticate the ledger, and the next start runs
it. (c) `verify_sequence_extent` walks one whole index: its memory does not grow with the history, its
time follows that index's size. It is the statement the installer's head read and the offline open
already run on production.

**Why.** v0.12.36 moves `ledger` from [3, 4] to [3, 5], so the deploy has a `LedgerVerify` step: with
the Runtime stopped, before anything is swapped, the live v0.12.35 installer runs the target's
`ledger-maintenance verify --config <config>`. The complete read keeps every event in memory with no
budget (10.07 GB and about 2.43 million events on the production ledger; the same kind of read reached
12 GB in 60 s, #422 6503130154; v0.11.3's cold verify failed at 120.76 s), and a timeout leaves the
operation unfinished with the Runtime stopped. Alice's standing ruling (10-08): skip the cold gate and
let the new version verify on its own start. The live installer passes exactly those arguments, so the
fix is the target's default.

**What changes live.** An update whose `ledger` range changes gets the bounded check. A damaged older
record is no longer found by that gate: it is found when it is read, by the background re-check or by
`--full`. `acsetup` in the UI repository passes the same arguments, so its gate runs the bounded check
too; it reads the report itself, and that reading, which this slice leaves as it is, accepts only the
report `actingcommand.ledger-maintenance.v1` with `verified-sqlite` or `verified-segment` (the report
has been v2 since #378 A6a).

### 1.242 Slice INST-UNDO-EDGE (0.12.36): `install undo` cannot go around the interface edge or the gate that refuse a rollback (found by the v0.12.36 release agent reading the installer; it lands before 114-B's first record; coordinator work order `rd-1031/brief-inst-undo-edge.md`; the coordinator's decisions of 11-01 on the first report: the whole gate once started, `next.undo` left out when certain to be refused)

[install-cli.md](install-cli.md) ("Undo and resume", "An undo once the build has started") is the
contract. The number 1.242 is the coordinator's; §1.241 and §1.243 are in flight in the same
release. No code, key, vocabulary, journal member or interface revision is new.

**What.** (1) Once a Runtime of the undone build has started, including the one a composite started
inside its own operation, `install undo` of an update or rollback, finished or not, is a rollback:
the interface edges first, then the whole rollback gate (`ledger_readability`, `open_time`,
`config`). Failed edges refuse `interface_edge` (`commit_sha`, `count`, the result's `edges`), their
ranges those of the operation's journalled plan; a failed part refuses `rollback_gate_failed`; both
with nothing changed. An unfinished operation in which no Runtime of the target started, a plain
update and a start refused before its spawn undo as before, unjudged. (2) A composite's success
leaves `next.undo` out when the edges would refuse that undo.

**Before.** The edge and the gate were judged only for a finished operation whose owner record began
after the operation's end. The composite's own start is before that end, so stopping its Runtime
with `request-shutdown` let `undo` swap back with no check. An unfinished operation was never
judged. The same held after an automatic rollback its gate had refused (`rollback_gate_failed`).

**Decisions within the work order.** (a) A start step begun with no evidence counts while the
operation is unfinished, since the journal cannot tell it from no spawn and `resume` remains; a
finished one is a start refused before its spawn. (b) An owner record of a finished operation that
began after the operation did also counts. (c) An automatic rollback that recorded itself has passed
its gate and its files may be reversed already: its undo goes on unjudged. (d) A gate that passes
adds its caveats (`open_time_from_other_build`) as `note` links of the undo's result.

**Accepted by the coordinator (11-01).**
- A finished composite rollback across `ledger` is refused by `one_way` on undo, since the undo cannot acknowledge it; the forward path is an update with `--accept-ledger-one-way`.
- A narrow gap stays: a start that spawned, crashed and whose resumed start failed to spawn loses its evidence, and only an owner record then counts it.

**Why.** Once 114-B writes a record, a build whose `ledger` range ends below it cannot decode it and
its start fails: the undo would swap back to a Runtime that cannot start. Once a build has started,
an undo is a rollback, and a refused automatic rollback can only be fixed forward.

**What changes live.** `install undo` after a composite: the gate now runs, reading the ledger with
the previous build's reader, and a failed edge or part refuses what used to be done. A one-way
composite's success no longer names `next.undo`. Nothing persisted changes.

**Rollback** (to 0.12.35). Nothing persisted changes; `undo` judges a composite's own start no more.

| # | Shape | Kind | Code slice | First writer | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| UE-1 | `install undo`: `interface_edge`, then `rollback_gate_failed`, when a Runtime of the undone build has started; result member `edges` | install command | INST-UNDO-EDGE | INST-UNDO-EDGE | `since` 0.12.36; reused code and refusal words |
| UE-2 | `next.undo` of a composite's success left out when the edges would refuse it | install command | INST-UNDO-EDGE | INST-UNDO-EDGE | `since` 0.12.36 |

### 1.247 Slice AGT-T1 (0.12.37): the first transport and `actingctl agent-channel` (Workflow #432; design `rd-1031/agt/model-agt-v2.md` §5.1, §5.2, §6.1, §6.3, §6.7, §7.2, §10, §11; coordinator work order `rd-1031/agt/brief-agt-t1.md`)

### 1.248 Slice PF-1 (0.12.37): one capacity decision per chunk of a stream (Workflow #407; design `rd-1031/check-speed/model-check.md` §3, §7; coordinator work order `rd-1031/check-speed/brief-slices.md`)

[capacity-admission.md](capacity-admission.md) and [runtime-config.md](runtime-config.md) ("The `artifact_store` section") are the contract. The number 1.248 is the coordinator's. No ledger shape, no wire shape, no outcome code changes.

**Why.** Every write of a stream took a capacity decision. A diagnostic stream writes once per record, 107 to 426 records a frame; one measured run spent 17.25 s of its 18.25 s of diagnostic writing on those decisions. The new fast path (§7's ACT slices) reads more frames, so this comes first.

**What changes live.** Nothing a run records or decides, except that a refusal or a binding change on a stream may surface up to one chunk (1 MiB) later. A decision still asks about the bytes of the write that needs it, so it is refused under the same condition with the same code, and never earlier. `capacity_admit` in task timing still counts one check per write, now mostly the chunk's count, so its attempts are unchanged and its total falls.

**The edges** (CHECK-M addendum item 2; [capacity-admission.md](capacity-admission.md), [task-diagnostic-stream.md](task-diagnostic-stream.md)). The allowance is cached **per stream**, a count on the stream that is not shared and that the owner never holds. "At most one chunk late" is per stream; the whole machine's bound is the chunk times the live streams. A single write beyond what is left, or larger than a chunk, takes one decision for all of its own bytes before any is written, and what was left does not count towards it. A change of bound volume is seen at that stream's next decision, at most a chunk of bytes later, with today's refusal and reason. An I/O failure inside a chunk takes no decision, is the stream's fatal `artifact_write_failed` at once, and ends the stream's count with it, so nothing leaks to another stream or a later decision.

**Rollback** (to 0.12.36). Nothing persisted. A file that names `artifact_store` is refused by the older build, as any newer section is; an instruction value of the key is reported as not restored.

### 1.250 Slices ACT-1 and ACT-2 (0.12.37): the settled path of a step after its input, and the gap between two actions (Workflow #407; coordinator work order `rd-1031/check-speed/brief-slices.md`; design `model-check.md` §1.6, §1.7, §7)

[performance-control.md](performance-control.md) ("Step pacing") and
[runtime-config.md](runtime-config.md) ("The `execution` section") are the contract. The number 1.250
is the coordinator's. **Off by default:** under `execution.action_gap.mode` `declared` every step's
order is the one before these slices. No package changes.

**What.** Under `settled` a tap reads frames from the first frame after its input and goes on the
first destination frame; `post_delay_ms` is the limit of that reading and is never added. A
`fixed` or `random` gap finishes before the frame that decides the input and its guard, asked once
per step; `performance` keeps only the pre-input wait. The path's frames and waits are recorded as a
confirmation's, and the blind wait's boundary stays, empty.

**What changes live.** Nothing until someone sets `settled`. With it, the frames of a step grow from
about one to one per `poll_ms` until its destination shows, and the next step's guard judges an
earlier frame.

keep the row shape. A configuration file that names the keys is refused by an older Runtime

dropped with its record; a file that does not name them is read as before.

A fields run has no comparison key, so fields have no such problem.

### 1.257 Slice LOAD-1 (0.12.37): a game's loading pages, declared once at the repository root, copied into each pack and checked by the tools (Workflow #407; design `rd-1031/check-speed/model-loading.md` §2, §7 LOAD-1; coordinator work order `rd-1031/check-speed/brief-load-1.md`)

[resource-declarations.md](resource-declarations.md) ("Loading pages") and
[package-reference.md](package-reference.md) ("Self-contained source layout", "Content-directory
tools and the bundle index", "Standard package root") are the contract. The number 1.257 is the
coordinator's. **No run-time behaviour changes:** no Runtime component reads `loading.json` or a
pack's copy (LOAD-2 compiles the copy, LOAD-3 runs it). No ledger shape, no wire shape, no
configuration key and no outcome code is new.

**What.** (1) The contract crate (`standard_pack_loading.rs`): `loading.json`
(`actingcommand.loading.v1`) and a pack's copy (`actingcommand.pack-loading.v1`), their limits,
`parse_standard_pack_loading`, `parse_pack_loading`, the copy a server takes
(`StandardPackLoading::for_server`) and the types LOAD-2 compiles (`PackLoading`, `LoadingPage`,
`LoadingTarget`, `LoadingCoordinateSpace`). (2) `actinglab package loading --root-file
--packs-root (--write | --check)`. (3) `package bundle --loading` checks every pack's copy first
and lays `loading.json` and its templates beside `bundle.json`; without it a pack that carries a
copy is refused. (4) `actinglab standard-pack check` checks every package's copy against a game
root's `loading.json`, and without the file refuses a package that carries one. (5) `resource
verify` passes a repository's `loading.json` to `package bundle` as `--loading`.

**Decisions within the work order.** (a) Every refusal is `standard_pack_root_invalid` (with
`package_id`, optional, when the issue is a pack's), every issue listed in `details.issues`. (b) A
copy is compared by reading it (`parse_pack_loading`), the templates byte for byte, so a copy
another tool formats differently is current. (c) `--write` removes nothing: a pack that holds a
file its copy no longer has is refused first, naming the file. (d) Without a root file, a pack's
copy is stale, so no copy is bundled or installed unchecked. (e) A target is carried as written:
only its `id`, its `template` and that it has a `region` are checked here; the pack's declaration
gate checks the rest when LOAD-2 compiles the copy. (f) Template names are lowercase, so two never
differ only in case.

**Interface.** `package` stays [3, 6]: the copy joins revision 6 (with DB-2 §1.244 and
OCR-SCALE-1 §1.251), since this PR merges before 0.12.37 is cut, and adds no step. No loader of
this release or an older one reads it, so a pack that carries one runs as without it; **the
Runtime is deployed first, then the packs.**

**What changes live.** Nothing until a resource repository writes `loading.json`; no repository
and no pack holds one or a `resources/loading/` today. `standard-pack check` and `package bundle`
then also refuse a pack that carries a copy without a root file.

**Rollback** (to 0.12.36). Nothing persisted changes; an older build ignores `loading.json` and a
pack's copy.

[resource-declarations.md](resource-declarations.md) ("Loading pages": "The compiled copy",
"Operation-level loading"; the `resource validate` table), [linear-steps.md](linear-steps.md)
(the admission table) and [package-reference.md](package-reference.md) (`package check`, the
source layout, `standard-pack check`) are the contract. The number 1.258 is the coordinator's.
**No run-time behaviour changes:** a compiled loading set is admitted and reported, and nothing
waits on it (LOAD-3 runs it in a page graph, LOAD-4 in a step plan). No ledger shape, wire shape,
configuration key or outcome code is new.

`resources/loading.json` with `parse_pack_loading` and holds it against its pack: its coordinate
space, the declaration gate of its targets (task schema `0.9` rules, no colour `digest`), the
pack's match metric, no page or target id the pack declares, every template present and not of
one colour, no other file below `resources/loading/`. Its targets join the derived recognition
pack under their own ids; its pages join the derived page set as `loading: {max_ms, pages}`, each
id under the game. (2) The page detector keeps them beside its pages: `loading_page_ids`,
`loading_max_ms`, `with_loading_pages`; `page_ids`, `contains_page` and `evaluate_all_*` leave them
out, `evaluate_pages_outcomes_in_context` finds them by id; a loading page reads template and
colour targets only. (3) `expect_after.loading` (`"off"` or `{except?, add?, max_ms?}`) at the
declaration gate and in kernel admission (`TaskProgram::validate_loading`), in both execution
modes; the source build takes each `add` page into the task's page set. (4) A step plan admits a
wait page and `loading`; `reason=wait` refuses wait steps only, and a page its loading adds, or its
wait page, that is its own `from`, destination or transition page is `reason=loading_page`. (5)
`package check` answers `loading: {pages, max_ms}` for a pack that carries a copy. (6) `resource
validate` takes `loading.json` (family `standard_pack_loading`) and `<pack>/resources/loading.json`
(family `pack_loading`), the copy against the one the root file makes, and names a stale one.

### 1.259 Slice AGT-T1b (0.12.37): a Claude Code channel restores its stopped session through Claude Desktop before a send (Workflow #432; Alice's ruling of 2026-11-02 on pending item 159, the wake only, the delivery staying the cross-session kind she chose the same evening; design `rd-1031/agt/model-agt-v2.md` §5.4, §7.2, §8; coordinator work order `rd-1031/agt/brief-agt-t1b.md`)

[agent-forward.md](agent-forward.md), "Restoring a stopped session", is the contract. The number 1.259 is the coordinator's. **No ledger shape, outcome code, configuration key, row reason or problem word and no interface revision changes:** a restore ends in the neutral words §1.246 already has, and its named word goes into the delivery detail.

**What changes live.** A registered Claude channel's message to a stopped session (no live record, an ended one, or one whose process has gone), which waited `deferred` (`target_offline`) until the session came back, now first has Claude Desktop bring that session's conversation up, unless the channel's switch is off or a quiet window or the hold covers now; the message then goes over the inbox as before. It switches the conversation Claude Desktop shows, restores a minimized window without taking the focus, and waits while the window holds an unsent draft. Nothing is typed into the window. **A message restores at most once** (a retry never runs the helper again, across restarts), and **a session whose restore got no registration by its deadline is marked and restored by no message again until it registers**; its messages wait (`wake_spent`, `restore_unanswered`) and end loudly at give-up as before (the coordinator's change of 2026-11-02).

**Rollback** (to a build without this slice). An older build reads no unknown member in a channel line, so a registry whose Claude lines carry `restore` is unreadable to it and its channels wait `registry_unreadable`: after a rollback, remove the member from each line (or `remove` and `add` each channel with the older `actingctl`). The compiled helper under `claude-input\` and `claude-woken.json` stay on disk and are ignored. A session record that carries the mark is of another shape to it (`failed`, `protocol_changed` for that channel) until the session's next registration rewrites it.

| AGTT1B-5 | the restore arm of the Claude transport; detail words `quiet`, `draft_present`, `input_busy`, `no_window`, `window_not_unique`, `not_registered`, `wake_spent`, `restore_unanswered` | behaviour of AGTT1-5 | AGT-T1b | the worker | `deferred` with `target_offline`, `target_awaiting_input`, `ipc_unavailable`, `target_not_loaded` or `target_unresponsive`; `failed` with `channel_unknown`, `protocol_changed`, `owner_mismatch` or `helper_failed`; never `unknown`, since nothing is written before the session's record is there |
