| AGTT1B-8 | the optional member `restore_unanswered_at_unix_ms` of a session record (AGTT1-3), and a record that holds only it (offline, no pipe, no token, owner 0) when no session ever registered | additive member of AGTT1-3, same schema | AGT-T1b | the worker, when a restore's helper was cut off at its deadline or no live record came by it | while set, no message restores the session (`restore_unanswered`); the hook's and `claude-register`'s new record never carries it, so a registration clears it; a record that turned live meanwhile is not marked; a mark that cannot be written fails that send (`helper_failed`) |

**Departures from the adapted source** (each is in the contract):
- No Claude Desktop window, and several, answer `queued` (`no_window`, `window_not_unique`) and the message waits, as the work order asks; the source fails both.
- A queued answer carries a fixed word beside its text, and the helper's own account check answers `problem: account_changed`, so the Runtime maps both without reading the text.
- The helper's request is `local_session`, `account_id` and `wake_only` only, and it refuses any other member; the input path, `text`, `allow_switch` and `prepare_only` are gone.
- An abandoned lock counts as held by the new run; in the source a helper that died holding it would fail every later run.
- The compiler writes `.build.exe`, renamed into place on success, so a compile cut off at the deadline leaves no program that looks finished.
- The source's own UI lock and private-folder ACL are not carried: the worker sends one message at a time, the helper's named mutex is the shared lock, and the folder has the state root's access rules.
- No `config.json`, or no folder of the active account, is "no conversation" (`channel_unknown`), where the source fails reading it; the account must be a hyphenated UUID.
- One deadline: the restore takes at most 25 s of the send's; when the session's record arrives with no time left the message waits (`target_unresponsive`) instead of risking an `unknown` write.
- One restore per message and none for a session that did not answer (the coordinator's change): the source wakes on every send. **Where the mark lives, and why:** in the session's own record, not in the worker's memory and not in the registry: it survives restarts and deploys, the registry stays the person's file, and a registration needs no new step to clear it, since the hook writes a new record without it. The per-message ids live in their own file for the same reason, and because a registration must not reset them.

**Tests:** the nine of the work order and the coordinator's three (`a_retry_of_the_same_message_never_wakes_again`, `a_channel_whose_wake_got_no_registration_is_not_woken_again_until_it_registers`, `a_registration_clears_the_unanswered_mark`), in the crate's own test module (host gate row "AGT-T1b"); `loaded_without_registration_by_the_deadline_is_deferred` now also pins the mark-only record. Adapted, with the same assertions: the Claude transport's existing tests send with the switch off, the path they pin, through a forwarder whose restorer may not be used; the Codex and DSH tests, and the worker's test send, add a `quiet` that answers false. Nothing is verified against a live Claude Desktop: the helper was compiled once and never run.

### 1.260 Slice LOAD-3 (0.12.37): a page graph's waits on the package's loading pages, `execution.loading.mode`, and their diagnostics (Workflow #407; design `rd-1031/check-speed/model-loading.md` §3, §4, §6, §7 LOAD-3; coordinator work order `rd-1031/check-speed/brief-load-3.md`)

[resource-declarations.md](resource-declarations.md) ("Loading pages": "Waits on loading pages"),
[performance-control.md](performance-control.md) ("Step pacing") and
[runtime-config.md](runtime-config.md) ("The `execution` section") are the contract. The number 1.260
is the coordinator's. **Off by default:** under `execution.loading.mode` `off` (and for every Lab
operation) no loading page is evaluated and every decision is the one before this slice; `shadow`
evaluates and records them and changes no decision. No package changes; `linear_steps` waits are
LOAD-4's.

**What.** (1) One frame judgement (`contained_task/loading.rs`, `PreparedContainedTask::judge_frame`)
for the settled path, the confirmation, the failure decision's confirmation, a wait step's wait, a
page wait and an observation window: a recognition conflict, an error page, a transition frame (a
loading page held, or a page the confirmation adds as one), what the wait waits for, anything else.
ACT-4's final-state judgement is its row 4 and is never asked on a transition frame. (2) One
allowance per input (`LoadingAllowance`), shared by the settled path, the confirmation with its
extra rounds and observe-only retries and the failure decision's confirmation; one per wait step and
one per page wait (the pack's). A transition frame is offered to the shared interrupt pages first;
otherwise it spends the time since the wait's frame before it and pauses the wait; after the
allowance it ends the wait through its own path and code with the loading values, no further time
and no extra round. Under `on` a wait page is one of the loading pages, so the silent fall-back past
its `max_ms` goes; under `off` and `shadow` it stays. (3) A transition frame is never the failure's
frame, a decision frame, an entry, final-state or flip evidence, fed to a collector, or still. (4) The
frame's loading pages are evaluated by id once its page recognition is recorded, in a scene context
of their own (the page recognition's context holds the run's sample recorder, and a loading copy's
targets are its own), timed on the run's clock. (5) The host hands the mode with each step's pacing,
writes each evaluation as page rows of the phase `loading` (never the frame's page recognition) and
each transition as `contained_task_loading_recorded`.

the allowance counts every transition frame, without asking the shared interrupt pages first, since
asking may act on the screen; a failed evaluation of the loading pages fails the run under `on` with
the page recognition's code and under `shadow` only records its row. (c) `loading_page_id` is a
stretch's first loading page: a stretch that passes from one loading page to another is one stretch.

(AGT-1a, STILL-1, ACT-1/ACT-2), so no second step ([component-interfaces.md](component-interfaces.md)).

carry loading copies; none does today.

### 1.261 Slice SUB-LAG-1 (0.12.37): an event subscriber that falls behind ends only its own subscription and request, not the Runtime (#419, Alice's hard rule that only a global fault may stop the whole program; found by the UI channel and confirmed by the coordinator at v0.12.36 `6b430f41`; coordinator work order `rd-1031/brief-sub-lag-1.md`)

[runtime-interface.md](runtime-interface.md) ("A subscriber that falls behind"), [ledger-store.md](ledger-store.md) ("Reads, projections and subscriptions") and the ledger fragment of the outcome catalog are the contract. The number 1.261 is the coordinator's. **No persisted ledger shape and no new outcome code**: the lag keeps `subscription_lagged` (error, ladder class `none`, pending), whose `values` gain `ledger_sequence` and `resume_after_sequence` (optional). One outcome key is new, `resume_after_sequence` (integer), `since` 0.12.37. No configuration key, no `actingd-config`, `ledger`, `runtime-client` or `runtime-outcomes` revision: the receipt's shape is unchanged, and the failure is a code and values the catalog already allowed on it.

**The defect.** When a subscriber's live queue was full, the ledger sent it `subscription_lagged` as a fatal failure; the host turned every receive failure other than a timeout into a fatal `ledger_failure` of `receive_runtime_subscription`, and a fatal request failure poisons the whole Runtime. One slow reader of `SubscribeEvents` (the console, a script, any client) could stop production.

**Where the fix sits, and why.** At the source, and relayed by the host. The ledger now builds the lag as a request-level failure (`GlobalLedgerError::subscription_lagged`, not terminal, its outcome carrying `ledger_sequence`): a lag is the subscriber's state, not a ledger fault, so `is_fatal()` must not say otherwise to any reader of the ledger, and it now agrees with the catalog's category, `error`. That alone is not enough, since the host maps every non-fatal ledger code other than an unanswered read to the fatal `ledger_failure` (`ledger_read_error`), so the host relays the lag in its own branch: `failed`, `subscription_lagged` on top (`runtime_unavailable`, `host_halted` false), the ledger's values, this request's operation and `resume_after_sequence`. Every other end of a subscription keeps its handling; a writer failure (`notify_terminal_failure` with the writer's own error, `writer_unavailable`, an invalid replay or sequence) stays fatal and stops the Runtime.

| # | Shape | Kind | Code slice | First writer | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SUBLAG-1 | `subscription_lagged` from the ledger's live delivery is an error, never terminal (`is_fatal()` false), with `ledger_sequence` (the event the queue could not take); it still preempts any replay or buffered event, removes that subscriber and stays latched on its subscription | behaviour of an existing code | SUB-LAG-1 | ledger | the writer and every other subscriber go on; the subscriber resumes from `resume_cursor()` |
| SUBLAG-2 | a `SubscribeEvents` whose subscription lagged is answered `failed`: `subscription_lagged` (`operation` `receive_runtime_subscription`, `runtime_code` `runtime_unavailable`, `host_halted` false, `ledger_sequence`, `resume_after_sequence`); nothing latches | behaviour | SUB-LAG-1 | runtime-host | was a fatal `ledger_failure` that poisoned the Runtime |
| SUBLAG-3 | `resume_after_sequence`: the sequence before the first event the request had gathered (they are not answered), or, when it gathered none, the last sequence its subscription had read, filtered-out events included | value rule | SUB-LAG-1 | runtime-host | every event after it comes again; nothing is lost |
| SUBLAG-4 | a denied or failed receipt keeps its top's `resume_after_sequence` in codes mode, as it keeps `host_halted` and `current_version` (`receipt_envelope`) | contract behaviour (R4-4's form) | SUB-LAG-1 | contract crate | only `subscription_lagged` carries the key; the console reads the cursor in its default detail |
| SUBLAG-5 | `resume_after_sequence` (integer) | new outcome key | SUB-LAG-1 | runtime-host | `since` 0.12.37; `subscription_lagged`'s `values` gain `ledger_sequence` and `resume_after_sequence` (optional), with its text written |

**Every receiver of a subscription's end, checked.** In the ledger the lag has one source (`deliver_live_event`); `notify_terminal_failure` (a writer failure, a clean close) is unchanged. In the Runtime, `subscribe_events` is the one reader of a ledger subscription (the policy monitor stopped subscribing at #383 AO-7): changed. Its other ends are unchanged: a timeout answers the batch it gathered; `subscription_closed` comes only from the writer's close and keeps its handling; a replay page the writer did not answer stays a request failure. The typed client returns a non-fatal rejection without latching its connection (unchanged); `actinglab lab watch` reports the failure and ends that call (unchanged); actingctl and MCP read events by `QueryEvents` pages and hold no subscription.

**Tests:** `a_lagged_subscription_ends_only_its_request`, `the_runtime_keeps_serving_after_a_subscriber_lags` and `a_lagged_subscriber_can_resume_from_its_cursor` (`crates/runtime-host/src/tests/gate_sub_lag_1.rs`; the subscriber is made to lag by a test hook, `AFTER_SUBSCRIBE_FOR_TEST`, run right after its subscription registered, in which another connection records more client actions than the live queue holds), and `a_writer_failure_is_still_fatal_to_subscribers` (`crates/ledger/src/global/tests/gate_sub_lag_1.rs`, on both stores), in the host and ledger gate maps beside the subscription rows. Adapted, as the requirement changes: `slow_subscription_receives_bounded_lag_failure` asserted the lag fatal; it now asserts it is not.

**Rollback** (to 0.12.36). Nothing persisted changes. A 0.12.36 Runtime poisons itself on a lag again; a console that reads `resume_after_sequence` finds it absent there and resubscribes from its own last cursor.

### 1.262 Slice LOAD-4 (0.12.38): a step plan's waits on loading pages, and a loading set with no limit refused at admission (Workflow #407; design `rd-1031/check-speed/model-loading.md` §5, §7 LOAD-4; coordinator work order `rd-1031/check-speed/brief-load-4.md`)

[linear-steps.md](linear-steps.md) ("Loading pages", the admission and failure tables) and
[resource-declarations.md](resource-declarations.md) ("Operation-level loading", "Waits on loading
pages") are the contract. The number 1.262 is the coordinator's. **Off by default:** under
`execution.loading.mode` `off` and `shadow` a `linear_steps` run decides as before LOAD-4 (`shadow`
evaluates and records). No configuration key, ledger shape, wire shape or outcome code is new.

**What.** (1) A step plan's waits (the entry, the intermediate page, the next step's page, the
candidates of a run of optional operations, the retry decision and the arrival after a late gate)
evaluate the wait's loading pages on the frame their candidates are evaluated on and ask LOAD-3's
one judgement (`judge_frame`, any candidate that passes being what the wait waits for): a loading
page comes before every candidate. The pages a confirmation adds (`loading.add`, its wait page) are
evaluated by id with them, since a linear wait recognizes no page but its candidates
(`LoadingAllowance::for_linear_input`). (2) Under `on` a transition frame is offered to the shared
interrupt pages first, otherwise it spends the allowance and pauses the wait as a handled interrupt
does (the arrival budget, a skip target's settle and first sighting, an extra round's end); it is
never a candidate, the intermediate page or the step's own page. (3) One allowance per input, shared
by the attempt's waits and its retry decision's, so a loading screen adds no input; the entry wait
has its own, the pack's. (4) A transition frame after the allowance ends the wait: the entry with
`contained_task_linear_entry_unmatched`, an attempt's waits and its retry decision's with
`page_confirmation_failed` (the intermediate page's wait too), an application step's with
`contained_task_linear_application_unconfirmed`, each with the loading values. (5) Admission, both
modes (`TaskProgram::validate_loading`, through `TaskOperation::confirmation_loading`, the set and
limit the allowance reads too): an operation whose loading pages have no limit named anywhere is
refused. LOAD-3's allowance of zero for such a set stays as a guard.

| # | Shape | Kind | Code slice | First writer | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| LD4-1 | a step plan's waits under `execution.loading.mode` | rule (no shape change) (the six `gate_load4` run tests) | LOAD-4 | LOAD-4 | `off` and `shadow` keep every decision; the fresh frame of a step's page before its input (ACT-2's gap, an observe-only retry) is one observation and evaluates no loading page |
| LD4-2 | `program_problem` token `loading_max_missing` on `contained_task_program_invalid`, `json_pointer` `/operations/<i>/expect_after/loading` | new token of an existing vocabulary | LOAD-4 | LOAD-4 | `since` 0.12.38; in a page graph and a step plan (`a_loading_set_without_any_limit_is_refused_at_admission`, `a_linear_loading_set_without_any_limit_is_refused_at_admission`); only `add` can bring such pages: a copy's pages come with its `max_ms`, a wait page with its own |
| LD4-3 | `loading_page_id`, `loading_ms`, `loading_limit_ms` optional on `contained_task_linear_entry_unmatched` and `contained_task_linear_application_unconfirmed` | optional values of existing codes | LOAD-4 | LOAD-4 | `since` 0.12.38; present only when the wait ended on its allowance; `page_confirmation_failed` already takes them (LD3-4) |
| LD4-4 | `ConfirmationLoading`, `TaskOperation::confirmation_loading`, `LoadingAllowance::for_linear_input` (`execution-kernel`) | Runtime-internal interface (memory only) | LOAD-4 | LOAD-4 | one reading of a confirmation's loading pages and limit for admission and the allowance |

**Decisions within the work order.** (a) The intermediate page's wait that ends on the allowance is
`page_confirmation_failed` with the loading values, not `contained_task_linear_intermediate_unobserved`,
as the design's §5 names the confirmation's code for the arrival and the intermediate page alike;
`intermediate_seen` and the rest of the detail are as before. (b) An application step's wait follows
the same allowance; its failure keeps its own code, `contained_task_linear_application_unconfirmed`,
which takes the loading values too (§5 names only the two codes above; without them an application
step's wait cut short by its allowance would carry nothing that says so). (c) An attempt whose wait
ended on the allowance still goes to its retry decision, as a page-graph attempt goes to its failure
decision; the decision shares the spent allowance, so its first transition frame ends it.

**Interface.** `package` stays [3, 6], no step for 0.12.38 ([component-interfaces.md](component-interfaces.md)):
LOAD-4 declares no new member. A step plan's `expect_after.loading` and wait page are LOAD-2's
members, which 0.12.37 admits and does not run; running them is behaviour, and `loading_max_missing`
is a stricter refusal of an already-admitted shape (pages `add`ed to a pack without a copy, with no
`max_ms`), which 0.12.37 admits (a page graph runs it with an allowance of zero). `actingd-config`
and `ledger` do not change.

**What changes live.** Nothing until an instance runs `shadow` or `on` with packs that carry loading
copies or declare `loading`; none does today. A pack that declares `loading.add` without a limit in a
pack without a copy is refused from 0.12.38; no pack declares `loading` today.

**Rollback** (to 0.12.37). Nothing persisted changes but the rows in a run's diagnostics, which keep
their shape. 0.12.37 runs a step plan's waits as without loading pages and admits a loading set
with no limit, giving it an allowance of zero in a page graph.

### 1.263 Slice AGT-2b (0.12.38): the daily summary, a timer rule's wake (Workflow #432; Alice's words of 2026-11-02 19:4x on pending item 158, 「定时汇报以及别的希望提醒的，都可以走这个通道」; design `rd-1031/agt/model-agt-v2.md` §4, §5.3, §10; coordinator work order `rd-1031/agt/brief-agt-2b.md`)

[agent-wake.md](agent-wake.md), "The daily summary", is the contract. The number 1.263 is the coordinator's. This is the first step of 0.12.38's `actingd-config` revision; later slices of the release join it.

**What changes live.** Nothing in production, where no `agent_wake` section is configured. With a section that has a `daily_summary` rule, the worker makes that rule's summary once a local day of the rule's own offset, at its minute, or after a start or after a quiet time the same day; never one for an earlier day. Its body holds what `RoutineSummary` answers for each of the rule's instances, the day's wakes by kind and state, the Runtime's epoch and start, and the rule's previous summary with the days after it that had none. No ledger shape, no wire shape, no configuration key, no outcome code and no `runtime-client` revision: the rows, the body schema and the section are AGT-1a's and AGT-1b's.

Summary rows in `host.agent_wake` have the row shape 0.12.37 reads; nothing else persisted changes, and `ledger` does not move.

### 1.264 Slice R-12 (0.12.38): `RoutineSummary`, the routine summary's health statistics, and their CLI and MCP reads (Workflow #429 A.2 R-12, board row 「有界统计、覆盖起点、epoch、取消分类、增量读取」; the shapes are R-0's, §1.213 R0-1, R0-2; coordinator work order `rd-1031/agt/brief-r12.md`)

[runtime-interface.md](runtime-interface.md) ("Workbench request kinds", the row `RoutineSummary`;
the actingctl and MCP tables) and [agent-wake.md](agent-wake.md) ("The daily summary") are the
contract. The number 1.264 is the coordinator's. No wire shape, configuration key or ledger shape
is new; one outcome code is (R12-2).

**What.** The host keeps, in memory only and per owner epoch, the health statistics of each policy
run and direct run of an instance as it settles it: by the task its run record names
(`PackageAdmitted.task_label`), a success, a failure under its terminal's outcome code, or an
interruption for `contained_task_cancelled` (a direct run's client cancel, and a scheduled run's
failure terminal that carries that code), in the hour and the calendar day of the host's local
clock that hold its settle time. Each bucket opens from the host's local offset then; a day bucket
runs from local midnight to the next, so a day across a daylight saving change lasts 23 or 25 hours.
Per instance the last 48 hour buckets and 14 day buckets are kept; an older one is dropped and the
instance's coverage of that width then starts at the oldest kept bucket (before, at the Runtime's
start). One revision counter per epoch, raised by every counted run; a bucket carries the revision
of its last change; `since_revision` answers only the buckets changed after it. `RoutineSummary`
answers from this memory, nothing read from or written to the ledger; the daily summary's function
(AGT-2b, §1.263) now returns the real page and keeps only the buckets that overlap the summary's own
local day.

| # | Shape | Kind | Code slice | First writer | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R12-1 | `RoutineSummary {instance?, granularity, since_revision?}` → `RoutineSummary {summary}` | behaviour of an R-0 kind (no shape change; `runtime-client` stays [3, 5]) | R-12 | the host, as it settles a policy run or a direct run | memory only (`crates/runtime-host/src/routine_summary.rs`, a leaf lock in the host); host runs (a startup package, a ladder's rung) are not counted; a run whose end wrote no terminal (refused before it, or a failure the Runtime does not survive) is not counted; `instance` names a bound instance, an unknown alias is Denied `instance_unknown` at `resolve_runtime_instance`, as `ResourceTargetView` refuses it; without it every bound instance, by alias, each listed with its coverage also when no bucket changed after the cursor; a restart begins the memory, its revisions and every coverage again; UTC for an instant the system cannot convert |
| R12-2 | `request_routine_summary_completed` | new success code (contract, `ReceiptCode`) | R-12 | the host | `since` 0.12.38; Workflow #378 A4's one success code per completing kind (R-0: "each gets its success code with its behaviour") |
| R12-3 | `actingctl routine-summary (--hour \| --day) [--instance <selector>] [--since <revision>]` | new CLI read | R-12 | — | the line is the page's members with `request_routine_summary_completed`, as `perf-preset` and `remedy` print the completed receipt's code; no new actingctl code |
| R12-4 | MCP `ac_routine_summary {granularity, instance?, since?}` | new observer tool (general read until U-3) | R-12 | — | `apps/actingctl/src/mcp/observer.rs`; the CLI's read; an answer past the output budget is exported with `answer_exported`, as `ac_remedy_get` |
| R12-5 | the daily summary's `routine_summary_page` | program state (body file), AGT2B-3 unchanged in shape | R-12 | the worker | only the buckets of the page by day that overlap the rule's local day `[midnight, next midnight)` of its own offset; `owner_epoch`, `revision` and each coverage as the read answered them |

**Decisions within the work order.** (a) The task a run counts under is `PackageAdmitted.task_label`
(the package's entry task id), which every policy run and direct run records; a policy run's
`catalog_task_id` is not on a direct run's record. (b) The code of a failure is the terminal's: the
task failure a cleanup failure replaced keeps its own code. (c) A direct run's cancel carries its
reason's code (`contained_task_cancelled`, `contained_task_deadline_exceeded`,
`contained_task_paused`), so by the decided rule a deadline and a pause's drain timeout count as
failures under their codes, as do a scheduled run's blackout stop and pacing yield
(`blackout_run_stopped`, `perf_run_yielded`, `perf_hold_expired`); only `contained_task_cancelled`
is an interruption. (d) The 48 and 14 are the contract's bounds, not configuration keys. (e) The
CLI and MCP names follow `perf-preset`/`ac_perf_preset` and `schedule`/`ac_schedule`:
`routine-summary`, `ac_routine_summary`; MCP's `granularity` stands for `--hour | --day` and
`since` for `--since`.

**Interface.** `runtime-client` stays [3, 5], `actingd-config` [5, 25] (AGT-2b), `ledger` and
`runtime-outcomes` [1, 1] do not move: the read's shapes are R-0's, and a success code joins the
catalog within its revision. The MCP tool list is not versioned in
[component-interfaces.md](component-interfaces.md); the build's observer tier gains one tool.

**What changes live.** `RoutineSummary` answers its page, from empty at the start; a daily summary
rule's body carries real numbers. Nothing is recorded or persisted; no run is changed.

**Rollback** (to 0.12.37). Nothing persisted changes. 0.12.37 refuses the read `not_implemented`
again, and a daily summary's entries carry that refusal; `actingctl routine-summary` and
`ac_routine_summary` are not in 0.12.37.

**Tests** (gate rows in `host.toml` and `apps.toml`, "R-12"): the nine of the work order, and
`the_summary_body_counts_the_routine_runs_of_its_own_day` (`gate_agt_2b`, the AGT-2b body with real
numbers; added beside `the_summary_body_holds_the_routine_summary_and_the_days_wakes`, which is
unchanged). Adapted, as the requirement changes: `r0_each_workbench_kind_without_behaviour_answers_not_implemented_with_no_effect`
(`gate_429_r0`) no longer sends `RoutineSummary`, which has its behaviour; and
`a4_each_request_kind_that_completes_has_its_own_success_code` (`actingcommand-contract`) no longer
lists `RoutineSummary` among the kinds that never complete.

### 1.266 Slice RA-1 (0.12.38): an artifact resolution is answered by the ledger's reader pool, not the writer thread (#422; the console reads one frame of a watched account at most every 10 s, UI-3c-1, UI PR #114, on production since 11-03; coordinator work order `rd-1031/brief-ra-1.md`)

[ledger-store.md](ledger-store.md) ("Recovery, artifacts and forensic consumers", the RA-1
paragraph) and [material-read.md](material-read.md) ("Verification and lifecycle") are the
contract. The number 1.266 is the coordinator's. No persisted ledger shape, wire shape,
configuration key or outcome code is new or changed.

**What the resolution reads and writes** (found before the change). `GlobalLedger::resolve_artifact`
read, in one read transaction, the keyed meta row and the end of the stored rows (against the
writer's head and head hash), the selected record with its link and artifact rows, each
authenticated, and the artifact's eviction proof from the writer's proof set; it opened no
artifact file (the host's material read opens it afterwards, outside the ledger) and wrote
nothing: no pin, lease, read confirmation or access time, and its read transaction commits
nothing. So it only reads, and needs the writer for nothing but its point.

**What changed.** The writer's reader pool (#422 QR-1) answers it, as it answers a view page: a
reader takes it from the same queue and reads it on its own read-only connection at the point
the writer last published (`sqlite::resolve_artifact_at_point`: `verify_published_extent`, the
point read, the proof from the published proofs, availability through that head). The writer's
own resolution and the reader's share one reader (`ViewReader::resolve`), so their answers and
refusals at one head are the same; the published proofs hold every proven object, as the
writer's index does, and an unproven object's identity was checked at every append that named
it, so no answer moves. A resolution is recorded in the writer's commit statistics as a
`ResolveArtifact`, where the writer recorded its own, and is not one of the pool's pages
(`ledger_read_pages` counts view pages only).

| # | Shape | Kind | Code slice | First writer | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RA1-1 | `resolve_artifact` on the reader pool, at the writer's last published point; the writer resolves only without a pool or once every reader ended | behaviour | RA-1 | ledger | `since` 0.12.38; `an_artifact_resolution_is_answered_by_the_reader_pool`, `a_resolution_does_not_wait_for_a_busy_writer` (`gate_ra1`) |
| RA1-2 | the pool's refusals of a resolution: `writer_response_timeout` (its caller's reply limit passed, or the queue full), `writer_panicked` (its reader ended in it), `writer_unavailable` of `shutdown_writer` (the pool closing), each of `resolve_ledger_artifact` where a page's is of `project_ledger_view_page`, none fatal | behaviour of existing codes | RA-1 | ledger | `without_the_reader_pool_a_resolution_falls_back_to_the_writer`; a ledger whose readers all ended says so as before (`take_reader_pool_findings`) and the writer resolves |
| RA1-3 | a record the published point holds whose file retention removed resolves without an eviction as of that point; the material read then answers `missing` (`material_read_missing`) | behaviour (no new failure kind) | RA-1 | ledger | `a_resolution_racing_retention_answers_missing`; a later resolution sees the eviction |
| RA1-4 | [read-session-resource-close.md](read-session-resource-close.md) "Device session lifetime": a frame captured without a lease is kept by its class (a default frame 1 day after its ingestion time), not until the instance's next disconnect | contract text agrees with the code | RA-1 | — | the UI's question QO2: the two files disagreed; the code is [ledger-store.md](ledger-store.md)'s ("Frame classes", "Frame cleaner", statement L): the owner journal's disposition gates no frame since the cleaner stopped calling eviction admission (Workflow #375 R5d); no behaviour changes |

**Failures.** A reader's own failure is never fatal: a refusal above fails that resolution only,
and a reader that ends leaves the resolutions to the readers left, then to the writer, said as a
warning, as for pages. What a reader finds in the ledger (a medium that does not match the
published point, a record that does not authenticate, an identity conflict, a failed statement)
keeps the code, operation and fatal flag the writer's resolution gave it, as a view page on the
pool does; a writer failure stays as it was.

**Interface.** `ledger` stays [3, 5] ([component-interfaces.md](component-interfaces.md)): nothing
persisted or written changes. `runtime-client`, `runtime-outcomes` and `actingd-config` do not
change either: the material read's request, receipt, codes and keys are the same.

**What changes live.** The console's frame reads, and every other material read, no longer wait
behind the writer's commits, and the writer no longer stops for them.

**Rollback** (to 0.12.37). Nothing persisted changes. 0.12.37 resolves on the writer thread
again.

### 1.267 Slice HS-1 (0.12.39): each instance's touch and capture backends as two rows, read only, their whole-instance check, and `nemu_app_index` relaxed (#402; Alice's words of 2026-11-03 11:4x, 「这个东西必须得被CLI、MCP或者是Lab/UI指定并且可以热更改」; design `rd-1031/backend-switch/model-backend-switch.md` §2, §3.6, §3.8, §4.1, §7 HS-1, with the coordinator's answers to its §9 on board #402; coordinator work order `rd-1031/backend-switch/brief-hs-1.md`)

[runtime-config.md](runtime-config.md) ("Key table", "`ConfigureSettings`", "Restore at start",
"Console tiers"), [device-binding.md](device-binding.md) ("Backends") and
[actingd-check-config.md](actingd-check-config.md) ("Discovery-bound instances") are the contract.
The number 1.267 is the coordinator's. This is the first step of 0.12.39's `actingd-config`
revision 26; later slices of the release join it. **Nothing switches:** the two rows are not
settable until HS-2 brings the switch, and no instance's backends change.

**What.** (1) The per-instance rows `instance.<instance id>.touch_backend` and
`instance.<instance id>.capture_backend`, the `instances[]` entry's existing members, by the device
layer's own names (actingd reports an alias the device layer reads, such as touch `adb`, as
`adb_shell_input`); default `none` (a device instance's entry names both, a fixture's neither), not
settable (read once at assembly), `ui_tier` `advanced`. (2) Their whole-instance check, in the
per-instance section's check at start and after every instruction: a backend the instance's kind of

emulator entry may name `nemu_app_index` whatever its backends (checked whenever named, used only by
Nemu touch), Nemu touch no longer needs it in the file, and Nemu touch beside another capture
backend is refused as `nemu_input_requires_paired_capture` (the registry's own code), which
replaces the retired `nemu_paired_input_configuration_missing`.

### 1.269 Slice RH-1 (0.12.39): an entry recovery package is judged as the configured return-home package is (#433 A2, board comment 6611839697: three manual runs on production refused on 11-03 and 11-04; coordinator work order `rd-1031/brief-rh-1.md`)

[linear-steps.md](linear-steps.md) ("Ladder and page-graph home entry"), [ocr-fields.md](ocr-fields.md)
(the recovery call) and [README.md](README.md) ("Entry page sets", the busy end) are the
contract. The number 1.269 is the coordinator's. No persisted ledger shape, wire shape,
configuration key or outcome code is new or changed.

**What.** The home entry judged one package two ways. The registry's return-home package (the
configured path) passes the checks of a return-home chain layer, which allow and ignore a
`scheduling_outcome` without a designated operation; a request's own recovery package
(`--recovery-package`, the entry recovery path) had to declare no `scheduling_outcome` at all
(`PreparedContainedTask::is_entry_recovery_compatible`). So a standard pack's return-home package,
which declares one for the scheduler, was accepted when the registry named it and refused with
`contained_task_home_recovery_package_incompatible`, before any input, when a manual run named it.
Both paths now read one rule, `PreparedContainedTask::scheduling_outcome_incompatibility`: the
first declaration that admission accepts only together with a `scheduling_outcome` and that keeps
a package from running as a layer (resource readings or adjustments, a select step with
`on_empty`, stage `end_pages`, a keyed `on_max_runs` or `on_guard_refused`, a designated
operation). The chain's check (`prerequisite_incompatibility`) calls it where those checks stood,
so its reasons and their order are unchanged; the entry recovery check calls it in place of "no
`scheduling_outcome`", which had refused all of them, so it stays as strict for each. Its other
conditions are unchanged.

| RH1-2 | a request's own recovery package whose `scheduling_outcome` declares a designated operation or one of the declarations above; one with a stability termination, post-admission OCR or fields, or a prerequisite package | unchanged: refused before it runs with `contained_task_home_recovery_package_incompatible` (the configured path keeps `contained_task_prerequisite_incompatible`) | — | — | `entry_recovery_still_refuses_a_designated_scheduling_outcome`; `explicit_home_entry_runs_one_bound_recovery_then_starts_target` (`home_entry`) adapted: the package it shows refused now declares a designated operation (it declared a `scheduling_outcome` without one, which RH1-1 admits) |

### 1.270 Slice HS-2 (0.12.39): an instance's touch and capture backends switched while the Runtime runs (#402; Alice's words of 2026-11-03 11:4x, 「这个东西必须得被CLI、MCP或者是Lab/UI指定并且可以热更改」; design `rd-1031/backend-switch/model-backend-switch.md` §2.2, §3, §6, §8 and §7 row HS-2, with the coordinator's answers to its §9 on board #402 6609804982; coordinator work order `rd-1031/backend-switch/brief-hs-2.md`)

[runtime-config.md](runtime-config.md) ("Switching an instance's backends", "Restore at start",
"The console's device backends group", "Codes"), [backend-open-observation.md](backend-open-observation.md)
("Backend switch event"), [device-binding.md](device-binding.md) ("Backends") and
[runtime-interface.md](runtime-interface.md) (the `config set` row, `ac_config_set`) are the
contract. The number 1.270 is the coordinator's. It builds on HS-1 (§1.267), whose two rows it
makes settable, and on HS-4 (§1.268).

**What.** A `ConfigureSettings` whose changes name one instance's backend keys and leave its
backends other than they are switches the device first. The switch is an operator claim of its own
kind (`backend_switch`) in the instance's one queue that waits at most
`CONNECTION_PREPARATION_CLAIM_WAIT_MS` (the constant, no key: answer Q2): a run (between its steps
too), a ladder, a lease or a Lab operation that holds the instance longer refuses it, never defers
it; a paused instance switches (pause, drain, switch, resume). A player's hold, a #403 fence and a
pending endpoint or an unbound handset refuse it, before the claim and again under the admission
guard. Then, without the settings' gate: the kept session closes; the registration takes the new
backends with its own checks (one shared function with the registration) and recomputes the
capability table, under the entry's lock, the kernel refusing a switch while a session is open; a
connection preparation on the switch's key opens and self-checks them (purpose "switch": its
failure starts no ladder). Passed, the changes apply again under the gate and commit with
`device.backend_switched` before `command.validated`. Failed, or refused by the ledger: the
candidate closes, the registration takes the previous backends, they are prepared again as a
self-check is, and the request is refused, named. A start writes the restored backends into the
registry before it prepares any instance.

| # | Shape | Kind | Code slice | First writer | Notes |

meets the Runtime at a point waits on a channel, never sleeps), `hs2_client_timeout_covers_switch`
(runtime-client) and `hs2_mcp_backend_key_needs_operator_tier` (actingctl). Adapted: the three named
in HS2-1 and HS2-2.

**Where it differs from the brief's letter.** (a) The player hold is R-7b's and not built yet: the
switch reads its dimension of the control gates (`SchedulingPauseTable::control_gates`, false until
R-7b), and `hs2_player_hold_refuses` sets that dimension through a test-only hook. (b) "Fences only
that instance" (`restore_failed`): the instance is left unavailable by its own failed self-check,
and the restore's ordinary preparation may start a ladder; no #403 fence is entered, since no
resource is unconfirmed (an unconfirmed close still fences, as on every close path). (c) The fence
and the endpoint are read before the claim too, so a switch on such an instance answers at once
instead of after the claim's wait; the reads under the admission guard stay the deciding ones. (d)
`nemu_app_index` is carried as before: the registration has it only beside the Nemu pair in the
file, so until HS-3 resolves a missing index, a switch to Nemu touch of an instance whose file names
another touch backend fails its paired open, named (`open_failed`), and keeps its backends; the
record's `nemu_app_index_source` is `file` until HS-3. (e) The switch shows as the self-check it is
in `RuntimeInstanceStatus.activity` (no new activity kind: no wire change). (f) "Run between steps"
is a direct run held at its own checkpoint inside the run (`PackageAdmitted`), on its own key, as a
run between two steps is.

member changes; an instruction row is no file shape), and `runtime-client`, `package` and
`runtime-outcomes` do not move: the request and receipt shapes are the existing ones, and the new
code and words are additive in revision 1. `ledger` moves to [3, 6] in 0.12.39: the new closed
action `device.backend_switched` and its payload are `ledger` revision 6
([component-interfaces.md](component-interfaces.md)). This paragraph first said that `ledger` did
not move because the record was additive "as `device.self_check` was". That was wrong by the
contract: the `ledger` row of revision 5 makes a word added to a closed vocabulary, or a member
added, a new revision, and a Runtime that declares [3, 5] refuses such a record (0.12.39's release
preparation confirmed it in v0.12.38's code). `device.self_check` is no precedent: it predates the
interface table and is part of revision 1 (§1.274).

**What changes live.** Nothing until someone sets either key: with no instruction row nothing
switches, and a start writes nothing into the registry. A person's change of an instance's backends
switches that instance only, while it is free, and commits only once the new backends opened.

**Rollback** (to 0.12.38; corrected by HS-2b, §1.274). `actingctl install` refuses it whether or
not a switch was ever made: 0.12.38 declares `ledger` [3, 5] and 0.12.39 [3, 6] (Rp.max 6 is not in
[3, 5]), and the update to 0.12.39 needs `--accept-ledger-one-way`. This paragraph first said that
the rows of the two keys in `host.config_overrides` are dropped at 0.12.38's start
(`config_override_dropped`) and nothing else changes, the record being read only by a reader of
this contract. The rows would be dropped, but after one committed switch 0.12.38 cannot decode the
record (`corrupt_ledger_record`): its start fails while the record is among the newest
`open_verify_tail_records` records, the rollback gate toward it fails (`rollback_gate_failed`,
`ledger_readability`), and a console built on its ledger reader cannot read the record either. The
test phase does no compatibility work for old versions (Alice 10-11), so 0.12.38 is not taught to
read it.

### 1.271 Slice HS-3 (0.12.39): the Nemu application index resolved when the paired session opens (#402; Alice's words of 2026-11-03 11:4x, 「这个东西必须得被CLI、MCP或者是Lab/UI指定并且可以热更改」; design `rd-1031/backend-switch/model-backend-switch.md` §4.1, §4.5 and §7 row HS-3, with the coordinator's answer Q3 on board #402 6609804982; coordinator work order `rd-1031/backend-switch/brief-hs-3.md`)

[device-binding.md](device-binding.md) ("Backends"), [emulator-control.md](emulator-control.md)
("Application state read"), [actingd-check-config.md](actingd-check-config.md) ("Discovery-bound
instances"), [runtime-config.md](runtime-config.md) (the `open_failed` cause, "Codes") and
[backend-open-observation.md](backend-open-observation.md) (`nemu_app_index_source`) are the
contract. The number 1.271 is the coordinator's. It builds on HS-1 (§1.267), which relaxed the file,
and HS-2 (§1.270), whose switch it lets open Nemu touch without a configured index.

**What.** A paired Nemu open (touch and capture `nemu_ipc`) takes the configuration's
`nemu_app_index` when it names one and reads nothing. Otherwise it reads
`MuMuManager control -v <MuMu index> app info -pkg <application_id>` once (10 s, inside the
preparation's own time): `running` resolves index 0, the main application; `not_installed`, `stopped`,
a read that gives no answer and one that answers another document refuse the open, named. The MuMu
index and MuMuManager are the discovery binding's, or, for an instance bound by HOST:PORT, those
its capture resolves. The resolution is kept in the registry entry until a rebinding or an open that
finds no display. The registry no longer refuses to build without the index, so check-config and a
start take Nemu touch without one.

### 1.272 Slice R-3 (0.12.39): `start_emulator` changed online, and read in effect by every automatic emulator start (Workflow #429 A.2 R-3, board row 「`start_emulator` 在线修改」, depending on 「配置、监视及有效暂停 / 持有规则」, acceptance 「启动 / 监视 / 唤醒重读与整节校验」; Alice's ruling 117 A of 10-31; for the console's UI-3e1-b, the automatic rules on the rescue bar; coordinator work order `rd-1031/brief-r3.md`)

[runtime-config.md](runtime-config.md) ("Key table", "Starting an instance's emulator",
"ConfigureSettings", "Restore at start", "Console tiers"), [emulator-control.md](emulator-control.md)
("Configured start at daemon start", "Emulator watch") and
[actingd-check-config.md](actingd-check-config.md) (`config_manifest`, "Discovery-bound
instances") are the contract. The number 1.272 is the coordinator's. It builds on S6a and S6c
(§1.36, §1.60), emu-watch, IDLE-1, PAUSE-AUTO (§1.230), R-1 (keys the file does not write) and
HS-1 (the check context the host fills in, §1.267).

**What.** `instance.<instance id>.start_emulator` becomes settable while the Runtime runs
(`ConfigureSettings`: `actingctl config set`, MCP `ac_config_set`, the console). Its
whole-instance check is the file's (S6a): `true` only on an instance bound by discovery, which the
host names in the check context from its registry (a physical instance whose endpoint carries a
discovery binding, pending or bound); a fixture, a handset or an instance bound by its port is
`config_value_invalid` (`discovery_binding_required`). Every automatic emulator start reads the
value in effect at its next decision instead of the start-time list: the configured start at
daemon start, the emulator watch's restart, IDLE-1's wake after `stop_emulator`, and each of their
claims once more on its key, after the pause, up to just before the Start (off: the key released,
nothing started, `emulator_autostart_skipped` with `skip_reason` `start_emulator_off`). Ruling 117
A holds everywhere through the one question `automatic_start_hold` (PAUSE-AUTO), unchanged: a
paused instance is never started automatically, re-checked just before acting. A change starts and
stops nothing by itself. A start restores the value as every instance key, re-checked against this
start's instances.

| R3-2 | `discovery_binding_required` | token of `vocab:config_value_problem` | R-3 | the configuration's whole-instance check | at start over the file layer (a second line: actingd refuses first with `start_emulator_requires_discovery_binding`), after every instruction, and at a start's restore (that value alone dropped, `config_override_dropped`) |
| R3-3 | `CheckContext::with_discovery_bound`, field `discovery_bound` | Runtime-internal interface of `actingcommand-runtime-config` | R-3 | the host (`config_check`) | `None` (a context that does not know the instances: actingd's check of the file) asks no rule; `CheckContext` is no longer `Copy` and `with_backends` no longer `const` |
| R3-4 | `start_emulator_off` | token of `vocab:emulator_autostart_skip_reason` on `emulator_autostart_skipped` | R-3 | the host | a claim that met the value off on its key (the daemon start's, a watch restart's, which gives its place in the bound back, an idle wake's, which is spent), and an IDLE-1 wake that found it off (no claim, nothing queued, the instance active again once free); once per claim or wake; no new code |

**Tests** (gate row in `host.toml`, "#429 R-3"): the nine of the work order, eight in
runtime-host (`gate_r3`; the scripted emulator, a scripted connectivity status, the manual clock
and the pause table, no sleep) and `r3_restore_drops_a_value_that_no_longer_fits`
(runtime-config, `gate_r3`). Adapted: the one named in R3-1.

**Where it differs from the brief's letter.** (a) "A hold": the player hold is R-7b's and has no
state yet; `automatic_start_hold` is the one place it will extend, and every consumer of the value
asks it before and on its key, as before. (b) The value is re-read on each claim's key as well as at
each consumer's decision, so a claim requested while the value was on never starts an emulator
after it was turned off. (c) An instance turned on by an instruction takes its turn after those
the file turned on (the configured ones in configuration order, then the others by alias): the
host has no configuration order of an instance the file does not list. (d) An IDLE-1 wake whose
start is off is spent rather than owed (unlike a paused one): the instance becomes active, its
emulator left as it is, so a person's start or the watch's recognition (EMU-BIND) brings it back.
(e) For a host started without actingd's manifest, the start-time list (`with_emulator_autostart`)
is what the key is for an instance whose configuration does not carry it.

**Interface.** No step for 0.12.39 ([component-interfaces.md](component-interfaces.md)):
`actingd-config` stays [5, 26] (HS-1's step: the entry's existing member is unchanged, and an
instruction row is no file shape), and `runtime-client`, `ledger`, `package` and
`runtime-outcomes` do not move: the request and receipt shapes are the existing ones, and the two
new words are additive in their vocabularies.

**What changes live.** Nothing until someone sets the key: every instance's value in effect is its
file's, as the start-time list was. Turned on for an instance, the watch's next poll restarts its
stopped emulator (and a later daemon start starts it); turned off, no automatic start launches it,
and its running emulator stays as it is.

**Rollback** (to 0.12.38). Rows of the key in `host.config_overrides` are dropped at start
(`config_override_dropped`: a key 0.12.38 may not set) and each instance's file value is in effect
again; nothing else persisted changes.

### 1.274 Slice HS-2b (0.12.39): `ledger` revision 6 for the backend switch's record, and a receipt wait that covers the whole switch (#402; the record found by 0.12.39's release preparation in v0.12.38's code, the wait by the console's UI channel; coordinator work order `rd-1031/backend-switch/brief-hs-2b.md`)

[component-interfaces.md](component-interfaces.md) (the `ledger` row of revision 6),
[runtime-config.md](runtime-config.md) ("Switching an instance's backends", "The wait"),
[runtime-interface.md](runtime-interface.md) (the `config set` row) and
[backend-open-observation.md](backend-open-observation.md) ("Backend switch event") are the
contract. 1.274 was the next free number on the base `9cf1ce5e`; the Lab slice HS-L takes the one
after it. It corrects HS-2 (§1.270: its HS2-4 and HS2-6 rows, its **Interface** and **Rollback**
paragraphs, each saying what changed).

**What.** (a) HS-2 recorded `device.backend_switched` as additive "as `device.self_check` was".
By the `ledger` row of revision 5, a word added to a closed vocabulary or a member added is a new
revision, and a Runtime that declares the older range refuses such a record. v0.12.38 does: it
decodes records with fixed types and refuses unknown values, so after one committed switch its
start fails while the record is among the newest `open_verify_tail_records` records, the rollback
gate toward it fails (`rollback_gate_failed`, `ledger_readability`), and a console built on its
ledger reader cannot read the record. The coordinator's decision: follow the contract. `ledger`
goes to [3, 6] in 0.12.39, the deploy takes `--accept-ledger-one-way`, and going back to 0.12.38 is
refused whether or not a switch was ever made; 0.12.38 is not taught to read the record (Alice
10-11: no compatibility work for old versions). (b) `BACKEND_SWITCH_WAIT_MS` left out the switch's
two session closes and the commit's ledger write, so a client could give up while the Runtime
still switched, and `config_version` moves only at the commit. It is now the switch's worst case,
and a client whose wait runs out re-reads before it sends again.

**Revision 6, from the diff.** Between the tag `v0.12.38` and the base, the ledger-read types
changed only in the contract crate (the ledger crate is unchanged): `EventAction` gained
`DeviceBackendSwitched`, `RuntimePayload` its variant, the new payload file its types, the key
table two keys, `codes.rs` lost one code. Revision 6 is revision 5 plus:

- the closed action `device.backend_switched` (`EventAction::DeviceBackendSwitched`) of the
  existing record type `runtime.lifecycle_observed`;
- its payload `RuntimePayload::DeviceBackendSwitched`, `DeviceBackendSwitchedPayload`
  (`instance_alias`, `touch` and `capture` as `DeviceBackendChange {from, to}`, the optional
  `nemu_app_index` and `nemu_app_index_source`, `session_generation`, `audit`; unknown members
  refused);
- the closed vocabulary `nemu_app_index_source` (`NemuAppIndexSource`: `file`, `resolved`), HS-2's
  (HS-3 first writes `resolved`).

Not in it, each read by the reader only as a spelling or not read at all: the claim kind
`backend_switch` (HS-2, memory only; it reaches a record only as the outcome value `holder_kind`,
vocabulary `claim_kind`); `start_emulator_off` (R-3, the outcome value `skip_reason`, vocabulary
`emulator_autostart_skip_reason`); the outcome vocabularies `backend_switch_problem` (HS-2) and
`nemu_app_index_problem` (HS-3) and their keys; the backend names in `from` and `to` (checked as
tokens, not a vocabulary); the codes HS-1 to HS-4, RH-1, BX-1 and R-3 added, and
`nemu_app_index_requires_paired_input`, which HS-3 removed. Only HS-2 and HS-3 touched the contract
crate; HS-1, HS-4, RH-1, BX-1 and R-3 changed no type the ledger reads. The ledger's own copies of the `Status` and `ScheduleExplanation` types
(revision 5) and their sources are unchanged since v0.12.38, so no guard test of the copies moves;
the record types, the views' type lists and the index keys are unchanged.

**What `device.self_check` was.** It shipped with the first tagged Runtimes (Workflow #317 sc3,
commit `d82e5985`, 2026-09-27), before the interface table existed (#364 RT-1, 2026-10-07).
`ledger` revision 1 is every record that Runtimes v0.11.0 to v0.11.2 write, so `device.self_check`
is part of revision 1: it never needed a revision of its own, and its "additive" in
[backend-open-observation.md](backend-open-observation.md) predates the rule. It is no precedent
for a record added after the table; taking it as one was HS-2's mistake, not a second one of its
own.

**The wait.** `BACKEND_SWITCH_WAIT_MS` is the sum of the bounds of the switch's steps in their
order (the constant's doc comment names each):

| Step | Bound | Term |
|---|---|---|
| the switch claim's wait in the instance's queue | 3 s | `CONNECTION_PREPARATION_CLAIM_WAIT_MS` |
| the kept session's close before the candidate (`close_switch_session`) | no bound at its source: the kernel waits for the session's worker without a deadline (`ExecutionSession::close_with_input_check`, `recv` and `join`), though each backend's own shutdown has its bound; bounded with the contract's existing allowance for a device-session close (R-7a §3.1, until R-7b measures it) | `PLAYER_HOLD_CLOSE_ALLOWANCE_MS`, 30 s |
| the candidate's connection preparation | 30 s | `CONNECTION_PREPARATION_WAIT_MS` |
| the commit's ledger write: its `host.config_overrides` record, whose refusal the restore follows | one writer reply, `ledger_observer.writer_reply_timeout_ms` (10 s by default; the ledger's `GlobalLedger::REPLY_TIMEOUT`) | `LEDGER_WRITER_REPLY_WAIT_MS`, 10 s (new: the contract cannot name the ledger crate's constant, so the ledger's default now takes this one, value unchanged) |
| the candidate's close before the restore | as the first close | `PLAYER_HOLD_CLOSE_ALLOWANCE_MS`, 30 s |
| the preparation that restores the previous backends | 30 s | `CONNECTION_PREPARATION_WAIT_MS` |

133 s, and the client adds its IO timeout. A commit whose `host.config_overrides` is written writes
three more records (`config.parameters.instance`, `device.backend_switched`, `command.validated`;
30 s at most) and restores nothing, which the last two terms (60 s) exceed. The request's own
`command.received` and terminal record are not counted, as for every request. `runtime-client`'s
`configure_settings` keeps computing its wait from the constant. A Runtime whose writer reply limit
is configured above its default, or a close slower than its allowance, can still outlast the wait:
the rule below covers it.

**A lost receipt.** A `runtime_receipt_timeout` on a `ConfigureSettings` that names a backend key is
an unconfirmed result, never "not applied": the client re-reads the settings' `config_version`
(`RuntimeFactSnapshot`) and the instance's `activity` in `Status` (the switch shows as a
`selfcheck` with its `request_id` while it runs) before it sends again.

| # | Shape | Kind | Code slice | First writer | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| HS2B-1 | `device.backend_switched`, `RuntimePayload::DeviceBackendSwitched` and the vocabulary `nemu_app_index_source` | `ledger` revision 6 (HS-2's shapes, §1.270 HS2-4) | HS-2 | the host (HS-2; `resolved`: HS-3) | the revision only: no shape changes |
| HS2B-2 | `ledger` [3, 6] | interface declaration | HS-2b | — | one way, as revisions 4 and 5 |
| HS2B-3 | `LEDGER_WRITER_REPLY_WAIT_MS` (10 000) | contract constant | HS-2b | — | the default of `ledger_observer.writer_reply_timeout_ms`; the ledger's `COMMAND_TIMEOUT` takes it |
| HS2B-4 | `BACKEND_SWITCH_WAIT_MS` (133 000) | contract constant (HS2-6, changed) | HS-2b | the client | the sum of its six named terms |
| HS2B-5 | a lost receipt of a backend switch is unconfirmed | client rule | — | actingctl, MCP, the console, the Lab | re-read `config_version` and the instance's `activity` before sending again |

**Tests** (gate row in `host.toml`, "#402 HS-2b"):
`hs2b_ledger_six_needs_the_one_way_flag_and_refuses_the_rollback_to_five` (actingctl, the INST-1
update gate: the build's own declaration is [3, 6]; from a [3, 5] build the update is refused
`one_way` without the flag and applied with it, and the rollback to it is refused
`previous_max_in_next`, flag or not). Adapted: `hs2_client_timeout_covers_switch` (runtime-client;
it pinned 63 000, now the sum of the named terms, 133 000) and
`the_runtime_declares_each_v0120_interface_revision_once` (actinglab-architecture; its `ledger`
[3, 5] becomes [3, 6]). The INST-1 fixtures' builds keep their [3, 4] default; no guard test of the
ledger's copies moves.

**Where it differs from the brief's letter.** (a) "The contract crate constant the installer
reads": there is none. `actingctl install` embeds `distribution/windows/component-interfaces.json`
(`host.rs`, `OWN_DECLARATION`), and no other `speaks` table holds the build's range. (b) The
commit's bound is named by a new contract constant, `LEDGER_WRITER_REPLY_WAIT_MS`, because the
contract crate cannot depend on the ledger crate; the ledger's default takes it, so the value has
one source. (c) The closes' term is R-7a's allowance; when R-7b measures the close and sets it,
the switch's wait follows.

**Interface.** `ledger` [3, 5] → [3, 6] (HS2B-2). `runtime-client`, `actingd-config`, `package`,
`runtime-outcomes` and the install interfaces do not move: the wait is a client constant, and no
request or receipt shape changes.

**What changes live.** The deploy of 0.12.39 needs `--accept-ledger-one-way`, and the console in
use must declare `ledger` with a maximum of 6 or more. A backend switch's receipt is waited for up
to 133 s plus the IO margin. Nothing else.

**Rollback** (to 0.12.38). Refused by `actingctl install` whether or not a switch was ever made
(§1.270, **Rollback**, corrected).

### 1.275 Slice HS-L (0.12.40): the Lab sets an instance's touch and capture backends through the same `ConfigureSettings` (#402; Alice's words of 2026-11-03 11:4x, 「这个东西必须得被CLI、MCP或者是Lab/UI指定并且可以热更改」; design `rd-1031/backend-switch/model-backend-switch.md` §2.2, §3.1 and §7 row HS-L; coordinator work order `rd-1031/backend-switch/brief-hs-l.md`)

[runtime-config.md](runtime-config.md) ("Switching an instance's backends": the boundary and "The
Lab"), [runtime-interface.md](runtime-interface.md) (actinglab's table, the R-14 note under "The
gate's decision"), [actinglab-dry-run.md](actinglab-dry-run.md) and
[actinglab-capabilities.md](actinglab-capabilities.md) are the contract. The number 1.275 is the
coordinator's (HS-2b takes §1.274). It builds on HS-2 (§1.270), whose request, switch, refusals and
receipt wait it uses unchanged.

**What.** `actinglab --instance <alias> session backend [--touch <name>] [--capture <name>]
[--clear]` reads the instance's id from `Status` and sends one `ConfigureSettings` on the Lab
channel (with `via` when forwarded) through `runtime-client`'s `configure_settings`, whose receipt
wait for a backend key is the client's: the named backend keys, both in the one request when both
are named; `--clear` both without a value, back to the file's values, itself a switch. It prints the
receipt (`settings`, `config_version`); a refusal prints the receipt's top code with its problem
word (`config_value_problem`, `backend_switch_problem`), the key, the receipt's state and the whole
outcome, and exits non-zero. There is no Lab-only backend. The Lab keeps no Runtime frame between
two commands: every online `do` observes first, and a frame of the closed session that a client
still names is refused `input_frame_unavailable` (HS-2's own rule). `session instance list` and
`session instance registry` gain the column `runtime_backends`, read from the Runtime, beside the
file's columns.

| # | Shape | Kind | Code slice | First writer | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| HSL-1 | `session backend [--touch <name>] [--capture <name>] [--clear]` on `--instance <alias>` | actinglab command (dispatch `session backend`; capability `running_runtime`, `device`, `unverified`; dry run `refused`, `dry_run_unsupported`) | HS-L | the person, or a counter forwarding with `--via` | no request kind, member or code is new: Status, then the existing `ConfigureSettings`; an unregistered alias is `instance_not_found`; a bare line, `--clear` beside another option, a repeated option, an unknown option or a word is `validation_failed` before any connection; `ratchet/actinglab_commands.json` gains the command (142) |
| HSL-2 | the success answer `{instance, instance_id, settings, config_version}` | actinglab output (data members) | HS-L | actinglab | `settings` is the receipt's `ConfiguredSetting` list as `config set` prints it; `hsl_session_backend_sends_configure_settings`, `hsl_session_backend_clear_returns_file_values` |
| HSL-3 | a refusal: `code` the receipt's top code (exit 2 for `config_value_invalid`, `config_key_unknown`, `config_key_not_settable`, 4 otherwise), `details` `{instance, outcome, config_key?, config_value_problem?, backend_switch_problem?, receipt_state, runtime_outcome}` | actinglab output (error members) | HS-L | actinglab | a failure without a receipt keeps the Lab's mapping (`runtime_not_running`, `device_error`); `tier_not_enabled` does not arise (no MCP tool forwards the command); `hsl_refusal_printed_with_problem` |
| HSL-4 | `runtime_backends` per listed instance (`{registered: true, instance_id, touch_backend, capture_backend}`, each `{value, source}` or null; `{registered: false}`; null when unread) and `runtime_backends_read` (`{read: true, config_version}` or `{read: false, error: {code, message}}`) on `session instance list` and `session instance registry` | actinglab output (data members) | HS-L | actinglab | read by Status and RuntimeFactSnapshot (`config.parameters.instance`), general reads that record nothing; both commands stay `offline` and `available`; the file's `capture_backend` and the registry's `effective` are unchanged |

**Tests** (gate row in `host.toml`, "#402 HS-L"): the three of the work order and one for `--clear`,

**Interface.** No step for 0.12.40 ([component-interfaces.md](component-interfaces.md)):

### 1.276 Slice HS-5a (0.12.40): a paired Nemu session without its application's display takes the main display, and a failed open releases its own connection (#402; the production failure of 2026-11-04 12:3x, board #402 6621962566; Alice's 「现在就可以换」 of 11-04 12:3x; design `rd-1031/backend-switch/model-hs5.md` §1, §3, §4.1, §4.2, §4.6, §5.1 and §6 row HS-5a, with the coordinator's answers Q1, Q4 and Q5; coordinator work order `rd-1031/backend-switch/brief-hs-5ab.md`)

[device-binding.md](device-binding.md) ("Backends", HS-5), [nemu-owned-resource-close.md](nemu-owned-resource-close.md)
("The opener's own connection"), [application-lifecycle.md](application-lifecycle.md) (its opening
paragraph) and the catalog's `capture_open_cause` `display_missing` are the contract. The number
1.276 is the coordinator's. It builds on HS-4 (§1.268), whose fake device it extends.

**What.** The paired session looks its package's display up before every capture, every resolution
probe and every touch, as before; without one it now takes the main display (the configured

run, as with adb. A display that appears, goes or changes, also only by its source (main 0, then the
package's 0), invalidates every earlier frame's geometry (D3); the rest is unchanged (D4). An open
that fails after `nemu_connect` and before it hands its backend over (its resolution probe, its
first frame, its memory admission, its probe cache) releases the connection it made itself under
`LocalOnly` when nothing was pressed on it, and fails confirmed (R1); a handed-over backend's
`LocalOnly` close stays refused (R2), a failed disconnect stays unconfirmed (R3).

### 1.278 Slice HS-5c (0.12.40): a backend switch passes a fence its instance's own backend open caused, as the remedy (#402; production on 2026-11-04 12:3x, board #402 6621962566: an instance fenced by its own failed Nemu paired open could not be switched back to its file's backends, `backend_switch_refused` `instance_fenced`; design `rd-1031/backend-switch/model-hs5.md` §1.3, §4.5, §4.6, §5.2 and §6 row HS-5c, with the coordinator's answer to its §8 Q3; coordinator work order `rd-1031/backend-switch/brief-hs-5c.md`)

[runtime-config.md](runtime-config.md) ("Switching an instance's backends": the `instance_fenced`
row and "A fence a switch remedies") and [emulator-control.md](emulator-control.md) ("Resource
fence", what lifts a fence) are the contract, with the module note of `host/resource_fence.rs`.
The number 1.278 is the coordinator's (HS-5a and HS-5b, the device layer and the HS-3 read, take
§1.276 and §1.277 in a pull request written beside this one). It builds on HS-2 (§1.270), whose
gates, steps, restore and refusals it keeps, and on #403 and #411 A38, whose fence, lift and wait
for a person it uses unchanged.

**What.** The switch's control gates (at the entry and again under the admission guard) read the
fence's cause. A fence caused by the instance's own backend open that failed,
`input_backend_open_failed`, `capture_backend_open_failed` or `paired_backend_open_failed`, in any
stage, lets the switch through; every other cause refuses it as before (`instance_fenced`): an
unconfirmed contact, an adb child or pipe, the application backend (A46), a session dead twice
(ISO-2b), a failed capture operation, any other contained failure (the coordinator's answer to Q3:
those three only). A ladder that holds the instance still makes the switch's claim wait and refuse
(`instance_busy`). The fence ends on the existing path: the candidate's preparation, whose passing
self-check lifts it in `prepare_connection_attempt` (`instance_resources_fence_lifted`, the lift
record carrying the switch's request and naming that preparation), which ends a wait for a person,
before the commit. A failed candidate restores the previous backends (HS-2 step 5), whose passing
self-check lifts the fence too; when they fail again (`restore_failed`) the fence, its wait for a
person, its rechecks so far and the next one's time stay as they were.

| # | Shape | Kind | Code slice | First writer | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| HS5C-1 | a fence of cause `input_backend_open_failed`, `capture_backend_open_failed` or `paired_backend_open_failed` passes the switch's gates | behaviour of `switch_gate` (`fence_remedied_by_switch`; the fence's cause read by `resource_fence_cause`) | HS-5c | the host | no code, key, vocabulary word, member or record is new; `hs5_switch_passes_open_failure_fence_and_lifts`; HS-2's `hs2_fenced_instance_refuses` (cause `capture_backend_operation_failed`, unchanged) still refuses |
| HS5C-2 | the switch's passing candidate lifts the fence | the existing lift of a passing preparation (`resource_fence_lifted`, `instance_resources_fence_lifted`) on the switch's request | HS-5c | the host | a failing candidate and a failing restore leave the fence and its wait as they were; `hs5_switch_back_failing_keeps_fence` |

**Tests** (gate row in `host.toml`, "#402 HS-5c"): the two of the work order, in
`tests::gate_hs5c`, over HS-2's fake provider (a switch replaces its registered backends; an input
open fails while its touch backend is one a test names) on a manual Runtime clock, the fenced
instance's stuck recovery off; the row also names `hs2_fenced_instance_refuses`, the counter-case.
None adapted. A test helper, `fence_instance_awaiting_person_for_test`, fences an instance for an
instance fault with the open's code (as `fence_instance_for_test` does with a capture operation's)
and hands the fence to a person as the lease sweep does with a fence no ladder may take.

**Where it differs from the design's letter.** (a) The tests are in `gate_hs5c.rs`, not the
design's `gate_hs5.rs`, which HS-5a and HS-5b write in their own pull request. (b)
`hs5_switch_back_failing_keeps_fence`: the design's §5.2 row names `open_failed`, but that receipt
means the previous backends opened again, whose passing self-check lifts the fence (§4.5); a
candidate that fails while the fence stays is `restore_failed`, which the test asserts. Its fence's
cause is `input_backend_open_failed` (an instance on another touch backend by instruction), so the
two tests cover two of the three causes.

**Interface.** No step for 0.12.40 ([component-interfaces.md](component-interfaces.md)):
`runtime-client`, `actingd-config`, `ledger`, `package` and `runtime-outcomes` do not move.

**What changes live.** An instance fenced by its own backend open (on production, a Nemu paired
open) can be switched, by `actingctl config clear`, `ac_config_set` or the console's 恢复为文件值,
without a self-check first; the console may stop telling the person to self-check before such a
switch (#429, the UI channel's). Every other fence refuses as before.

### 1.279 Slice HS-5d (0.12.40): the arrival wait goes on across the display's change, and two HS-5b tests run on a manual Runtime clock (#402; `hs5_ladder_application_rung_opens_after_entry` passed in the CI of #1519 and failed in the CI of #1521 on the same code; coordinator work order `rd-1031/backend-switch/brief-hs-5d-flake.md`)

[application-lifecycle.md](application-lifecycle.md) (the paired session's paragraph) and
[display-adapter.md](display-adapter.md) (the frames of one observation) are the contract. The
number 1.279 is the coordinator's. It builds on HS-5a (§1.276, D3) and changes two tests of HS-5b
(§1.277). No outcome code, key, member or record is new.

**Why the test failed.** The failed run's rungs were return home (`contained_task_page_unknown`),
application restart (`page_confirmation_failed`) and emulator restart (skipped, no emulator
control). The restart rung's startup package, `gate_hs5`'s application entry package, restarts the
application before any capture; its arrival wait is the step's confirmation, whose window is the
package's step timeout (600 ms) on the Runtime clock, the system clock in that test. The fake's
package display comes up on the second capture after the start (`display_delay` 1), counted in
captures, not in time, and the fake's frames keep one geometry. The rung recovers only when that
second frame is taken inside the window. The work around the first frame (the rung run's first
capture, its frame and geometry records, the test thread reading the whole ledger every 20 ms
while it waits for the ladder's end, a loaded runner) can spend the 600 ms; the wait then ends on
the first frame (`after_page=<unrecognized>`), `page_confirmation_failed`. Thread timing decided
it; the code under test was the same in both runs. That failure is the test's own.

**The product's race.** Every capture of a paired Nemu session resolves its display first (HS-5a
D1–D4): while the package has no display it captures the main display; once it has one, the next
capture takes it, and the change of source invalidates the input state (D3: the geometry
generation goes up by one). The capture still returns its frame, with the new generation in its
input geometry. What the confirmation did with it:

- An observation of one frame (a pack without target consensus): nothing. The confirmation judges
  each frame by its page; a frame of the main display is a frame that did not confirm, and the
  wait takes its next frame in its window. The generation is read only by the Nemu input's
  geometry fence, which refuses an input sent on a frame of an earlier generation; an arrival
  wait sends no input. So the switch alone never ended the wait with `page_confirmation_failed`.
- An observation of several frames (a pack with target consensus): its frames must keep one
  geometry (DA-2a C11; the frames' input geometry, generation included, and their map). When the
  switch fell between two of its frames the observation ended `recognition_sample_geometry_changed`,
  which is no sampling timeout and was not retried: the run failed with it. Whether it did
  depended on when the package's display came up against the observation's sampling: a race in
  the product, on Nemu-touch instances whose pack declares target consensus (none of the
  resource repositories' packs read for this slice declares one).

| # | Shape | Kind | Code slice | First writer | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| HS5D-1 | in a page graph's step confirmation (`await_postcondition_after`: every step's, an application effect's arrival included) and in a step plan's wait after an input or an application effect (`linear_wait`, purpose `AfterInput`), an observation that ends `recognition_sample_geometry_changed` is a frame that did not confirm: no page, the wait's window check and the pause before the next observation as after any such frame, the same window (its start and its credit kept) | behaviour | HS-5d | the kernel | `gate_hs5d`; no other wait changes: an entry wait, a retry decision, a run of optional steps (`linear_wait_set`, never after an application effect: `optional_restart_segment_end`), the settled path, an observation window and the Lab's online observations keep failing with the code; a sampling timeout keeps its observe-only retries |
| HS5D-2 | `hs5_ladder_application_rung_opens_after_entry` and `hs5_startup_package_opens_after_entry` on a `ManualRuntimeClock` | test change | HS-5d | — | what they assert is unchanged; their gate row is HS-5b's |

**Tests.** New (exec gate row "#402 HS-5d"), in `contained_task::gate_hs5d` on the scripted runtime
and clock (EXEC-I3): the kernel sees the display's change only as frames of another geometry, so
the main display's frames are 2x1 (the desktop) and the application's 4x2 (home; a pure scale of the
2x1 package), the one geometry a scripted frame carries; home needs two frames 100 ms apart. With
the change before the wait's first frame, inside its first observation, between two observations
and inside a later one, a page graph's application entry run as a host package and a step plan's
application entry arrive on home; when every observation straddles the change, the wait ends where
its 1 000 ms window ends, with `page_confirmation_failed` and `contained_task_linear_application_unconfirmed`
and `limit_ms` 1000. Red first: the cases inside an observation and the straddling one fail on the
commit before the fix with `recognition_sample_geometry_changed`. Adapted (HS5D-2): the two host
tests whose arrival needs a second frame inside the package's window run on a manual Runtime clock
(the ladder's at the policy fixture's time, as the other manual-clock ladder tests do; the startup
package's at 1 000 ms), whose time only the kernel's own waits move, so the window is spent only by
the 10 ms between two frames and the display follows the count of captures. In the ladder's test
each paired open also takes one millisecond (fix 1): its instance is a policy instance on a device
endpoint, whose start's preparation withholds `session.instance.available` and publishes the seed
again once the open's self-check passes, and a clock that stood between the two refused the seed
`fact_observation_not_newer`, so the start failed. Their `wait_until`
polls only bound a hang (120 s) and decide nothing. The other `gate_hs5` tests need no second frame
inside a window: with `display_delay` 0 the arrival's first frame is the destination's, and a frame
that reaches it ends the wait whatever the time.

**Where it differs from the work order's letter.** (a) The work order names the ladder's test; the
startup package's has the same window and second frame, so it changes the same way. (b) The kernel
tests put the change in the frames' size, not in a Nemu generation: a `NemuFrameGeometry` can only
be built inside the device layer, and the kernel reads both through the one check that ends the
observation.

**Interface.** No step for 0.12.40: nothing persisted, requested or configured is new.

**What changes live.** On a Nemu-touch instance whose pack declares target consensus, an
application's start (a startup package, a ladder rung, a run's application entry) or any step's
confirmation no longer fails when the display moves between two frames of one observation; the
wait goes on and its window decides. Everything else is as in 0.12.39.

**Rollback** (to 0.12.39). Nothing persisted; an earlier build ends such a run with
`recognition_sample_geometry_changed`.

Shape rules (`invalid_performance_status`): with `process`, working set within peak and the parts' bytes (frame stores, model loads, queue, packages) within `private_bytes`; no store, all zero; the largest within the sum; bytes only with a run; at most 256 models, each `model_ref` a bounded logical name once per kind |
| PR-2 | `RuntimePerformanceStatus.vision` = `[{model_ref, kind, requests, inferences, lock_wait_total_us, lock_wait_longest_us, inference_total_us, inference_longest_us}]` | wire, read from memory (§3 W23) | PERF-READ | PERF-READ | per model since the start, absent while no model was asked: the requests that waited for the model's lock (a wait that timed out counts until it ended), the engine calls, and the lock wait and inference time summed and longest, in microseconds on the provider's monotonic clock; a load is in neither time. Shape rules: inferences within requests, longest within sum, no time without a request or an inference, at most 256 models, each once per kind |
| PR-3 | `perf_memory_unavailable` (warning, `since` 0.12.41; values `actual_bytes`, `limit_bytes`) | outcome code | PERF-READ | PERF-READ | the status read's warning when `memory.process` is absent, never zero: the sample failed (caused by the sampler's code: `performance_sampler_unsupported` off Windows, `performance_memory_status_failed` or `performance_memory_structure_invalid` on it), or the parts claimed more than the private bytes (`actual_bytes` the parts, `limit_bytes` the private bytes); put first among the warnings so their bound never drops it |

(`provider::tests::vision_timing_separates_lock_wait_from_inference`, a scripted clock: each

as they leave out `ledger_read_pages` or the read's time (each read has its own);

status literal gain the two members, absent; the declaration pins (`component_interfaces` V0120,
`gate_429_r0b_pairing`) read [3, 6].

its client fails `runtime_receipt_decode_failed` and latches the connection. This build fills
