### 1.292 Slice QP-1 (0.12.49): a ledger page stays inside its sequence bounds whatever the planner chooses (#422; the read-only investigation of 2026-11-10, `rd-1110/ledger-window-plan-findings.md`; the console's ledger window will send pages with `from_sequence`, `to_sequence`, a limit and a snapshot and no instance, which the coordinator ruled acceptable once this slice makes the bound independent of the planner; coordinator work order `rd-1110/brief-qp1-page-plan-bounds.md`)

[ledger-observer.md §15](ledger-observer.md#15-configuration-keys-ledger_observer) (the QP-1
note) and [global-ledger-query.md](global-ledger-query.md) (the QP-1 paragraphs) are the
contract. 1.292 is the next free number on main `fa8adc67`, where #1554 added §1.291 (S168-0);
this slice had taken 1.291, then the next free one on `7910349a`. No persisted ledger shape, wire
shape, configuration key, outcome code, index or table is new or changed.

**Why.** A view page reads its selection in segments of the sequence (LN-WS R2:
`e.sequence>c AND e.sequence<=end`), its first of one sequence and run whatever the budget. A
segment bounds a statement only when the index that drives it takes the segment's bounds. For a
statement with a per-run link the link's index drives (DIAG-RUN). For one without, nothing in
the text forced it: SQLite chose. Every view and link index is (column, sequence), so with an
equality on its column the segment enters it as its second term; but the time bounds are a range
on the time index's first column, where the segment cannot enter, and a statement the time
index drove read every record of its time range, however far before the segment (the
investigation measured about 6 500 SQLite steps for a page against about 18 million with the
time index forced, on 400 000 records). With a window, the statement also carried the window's
own sequence terms (`e.sequence>=from`, `e.sequence<=to`), a second range an index could take in
place of the segment's.

**What changed** (`history_statement`). Every time term is written `+e.timestamp_unix_ms`, in
every statement, with a per-run link or without (a per-run statement had them so already), so
no index serves a time bound; the window start's lookup (`TIME_START`, LN-WS R3) is its own
statement and unchanged. A statement without a per-run link writes its window's sequence terms
`+e.sequence>=?` and `+e.sequence<=?`: every caller's segment lies inside the window, so they
select nothing more, and the segment's pair is the only sequence range an index can take. The
link-set page of LN-8d still counts such a term as a sequence condition. A statement with a
per-run link is unchanged: its time terms were already `+`. For a page its read budget does not
cut, the rows, their order, cursors, read scope and continuation are the same; only plans may
differ. Where the budget cuts a page, the place it stops depends on the work its statements'
plans needed, so it may stop at another place than before.

**The first statement** keeps its exemption from the budget: it spans one sequence and every
search it makes stays inside it, so it reads that sequence's rows, and its work no longer grows
with the history before the window.

**Not bounded by the window, unchanged** (ledger-observer.md §15, the QP-1 note): the Lab
relations a page reads (past the pool index's end through the snapshot, with the earlier link
rows of a request or correlation first anchored there; the whole history's without a built
index) and run recovery (each run of the page from sequence 0 through the snapshot through
`ledger_links_run`, at most 1 025 records). The Runtime does not limit the distance between
`from_sequence` and `to_sequence`.

**Interfaces.** None raised ([component-interfaces.md](component-interfaces.md)): `ledger`
stays [3, 7], since nothing persisted or written changes (SQLite format 2, the tables, the
indexes and the views are the same); `runtime-client` stays [3, 6], since no request member and
no answer changes; `actingd-config` gains no key.

**What changes live.** Nothing in answers of a page its read budget does not cut; a page the
budget cuts may stop at another place. A page with a time bound, and a page without a
per-run link with a window, may take a different plan. The console may send time conditions
online only against a Runtime with this slice.

**Rollback** (to 0.12.48). Nothing persisted changes; 0.12.48 builds the statements as before,
and a time bound may again drive a page's statement.

| QP1-2 | the window's sequence terms of a history statement without a per-run link written `+e.sequence` | Runtime-internal behaviour (statement text) | QP-1 | ledger | `page_statements_stay_inside_sequence_bounds`; the segment's pair is the only indexable sequence range; LN-8d's link-set page keeps its form with such a term: the same test asserts that a link-set statement with `to_sequence` (the resident retention's object load, its artifacts and its frames), built by `history_statement`, has the `e.sequence IN (SELECT sequence FROM (` form |

### 1.293 Slice TB-R1 (0.12.50): the table reader does not read the names a replacement in place leaves (#428; on 11-10 production reported `standard_pack_table_invalid` (`table_id_mismatch`, `/table_id`) for a file `tables/<table_id>.json.old-<unix_ms>` that a deploy kit kept beside the table it replaced, and the Lab rescue module's `place` keeps a replaced table there too; the coordinator's ruling, not Alice's words: change the reader, not the placer; coordinator work order `rd-1110/brief-tbr1-table-listing-leftovers.md`)

[package-reference.md](package-reference.md) ("Tables", "When the Runtime reads it") and
[actingd-check-config.md](actingd-check-config.md) (a sound game root's `tables`) are the
contract; this section amends §1.65 TB1 to TB3. 1.293 is the next free number on main
`dfc1d96f` and still is on `2e949752` (#1558 merged), and the name TB-R1 was free. No persisted
ledger shape, wire shape, configuration key, outcome code or vocabulary is new or changed.

**Why.** `read_standard_pack_tables` listed every entry of `tables/`, read each as a table and
took the first 64 by name. A kept copy was reported as an invalid table at every start (one
`standard_pack_read` record), by check-config and by `actingctl packs`, and enough of them would
have pushed real tables past the 64th place (`table_too_large`). The placer's `undo` and its
journal rely on the copy beside the item, and the other readers of a game root read only the
names `bundle.json` and the root files give.

**What.** The contract crate's `replacement_leftover_name` says which names a replacement in
place leaves, matched as the code writes them: a name ending in `.part`, or holding `.old-`,
`.abandoned-` or `.rolledback-`. In `tables/` the rescue module leaves them so (crate
`lab-rescue`, `src/install/`): `<name>.new-<ms>.part`, the part `place` writes before it renames
it in, left by an interrupted step (`place.rs`, `steps`, `item_step`); `<name>.old-<ms>`, the
replaced table kept beside it (`place.rs`, `steps`; `update.rs`, `swap`), as a deploy kit keeps
its `.old-<stamp>`; `<name>.abandoned-<ms>`, a part set aside by a retried step or by `undo`, and
`<name>.rolledback-<ms>`, the placed table `undo` sets aside (`place.rs`, `item_step`,
`reverse_item`; `undo.rs`, `set_aside`). The first two are the two names `reserved_package_id`
reserves (NAV-T); the other two are not, so the rule is its own. `reserved_package_id` is
unchanged: it says what a bundle's pack may be named (the `package` interface), this rule what
the readers of an installed root's `tables/` ignore. Every reader of `tables/` skips such an
entry before it sorts and counts: `read_standard_pack_tables` (the Runtime's startup,
check-config, `actingctl packs` and `ac_packs`), `read_standard_pack_table` (a run's
preparation and the Lab's dry run, which judge a table's place among the same entries) and
`actinglab resource validate` (its count for `table_too_large`; a selected file of such a name
takes no row of the family `standard_pack_tables` and is judged as any path no parser is mapped
to). A table's file name, `<table_id>.json`, never matches.

**Unchanged.** A real table that is invalid is reported as before; a directory or any other name
in `tables/` (`notes.txt`, say) is read and reported as before; a root without such names lists,
reads and records as before. The Runtime deletes and moves nothing.

**Interfaces.** None raised ([component-interfaces.md](component-interfaces.md)); every range
stays as main declares it ([3, 7] for `package` and `ledger`, [3, 6] for `runtime-client` on
`2e949752`). `package`: what a bundle may contain does not change (the bundle index and
`reserved_package_id` are untouched; only what the reader of an installed root ignores).
`ledger`: no record shape changes (an existing `standard_pack_read` record is no longer written
for such a name). `runtime-client` and `runtime-outcomes`: no shape and no code changes;
check-config's `tables` and the `packs` answer lose rows of an unchanged shape.

**At deploy.** A game root with leftover copies in `tables/` stops reporting them; no table that
was read before reads differently. **Rollback** (below 0.12.50): a Runtime before this release
still reports them, so the old reports come back; nothing else changes.

| TBR1-2 | check-config's `standard_packs.games[].tables` (TB3), `actingctl packs` / `ac_packs` (TB4) and the startup's `standard_pack_read` records (TB2) | fewer rows and records, same shapes | TB-R1 | — | an entry of such a name has no row and no record and does not count toward the 64 |
| TBR1-3 | `actinglab resource validate`, family `standard_pack_tables` (TB5) | tool family | TB-R1 | — | such a name takes no row of the family and is not counted for `table_too_large` |

### 1.294 Slice FLK-10 (0.12.51): the Lab's environment-detection lock reads its holder's identity from the operating system, no helper program started (Workflow #71 FLK-10; on 11-10 a loaded CI runner did not get an answer from PowerShell within 30 s, and `detect` answered `validation_failed`, "owner identity unavailable: PowerShell process inspector for PID … timed out after 30000ms", CI run 42793213181, registered as flaky FLK-10 in #71 comment 6764779352; the coordinator's ruling, not Alice's words: read the process start from the system directly; coordinator work order `rd-1110/brief-flk10-native-process-inspector.md`)

This section and the comments of `crates/lab/src/env_detection/lock.rs` are the contract: no
contract and no README described the result lock before. 1.294 is the next free number on main
`126d3f68`. No persisted ledger shape, wire shape, configuration key, outcome code, location or
vocabulary is new or changed.

**The lock.** A writer of an environment-detection result holds `<result>.json.lock` (schema
`env-result-lock.v2`) while it writes. The record names its holder by `host_identity`, `pid`,
`process_start_token` and a 64-hex `owner_token`. A contender takes a lock over only when the host
is the same and the holder process is gone (`owner_pid_absent`) or the pid now belongs to a process
with another start (`owner_pid_reused_with_different_start_time`); a holder whose liveness cannot be
proven keeps the lock. The record's shape and the text of every member are unchanged.

**Why.** On Windows the lock learned these facts by starting programs, each under a 30 s deadline
(`WINDOWS_PROBE_TIMEOUT`): `powershell.exe` with `Get-Process` for a process's start,
`hostname.exe` for the host, and `powershell.exe` with `RandomNumberGenerator` for the 32 bytes
that seed the owner token. Every Lab process that takes the lock started all three, and on a host
under load PowerShell alone can take longer than the deadline to start.

**What changed (Windows only).** The three reads go to the operating system directly, through
`actingcommand-host-metrics`, the workspace's safe Win32 boundary (`crates/lab` forbids unsafe
code, as lab-ops, lab-rescue and runtime-host do, which already read processes there); no program
is started and nothing waits on one:

- **A process's start:** `probe_process_creation`, the query of the existing `probe_process`
  (`OpenProcess` with `PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION`, `GetExitCodeProcess`,
  `GetProcessTimes`), which answers the creation `FILETIME` (100 ns since 1601-01-01T00:00:00Z).
  The start token stays the text PowerShell printed, `$p.StartTime.ToUniversalTime().Ticks` in the
  invariant culture: .NET ticks (100 ns since 0001-01-01T00:00:00Z) in decimal digits. .NET's
  `StartTime` is `DateTime.FromFileTime` of the same `FILETIME`, so the token is the `FILETIME` plus
  504 911 232 000 000 000 (584 388 days of 864 000 000 000 ticks, .NET's
  `DateTime.FileTimeOffset`); a time past .NET's last tick is an error, as PowerShell printed no
  ticks for it. A lock written by an earlier build is therefore judged as before, and the other
  way round.
- **Gone or unreadable:** no process with the id (`OpenProcess` fails with
  `ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER`), or one that has exited, is `Missing`, as the script's exit 3 was. A
  process the system refuses to open (`process_query_refused`), cannot open
  (`process_open_failed`), or whose exit code, times or creation time cannot be read
  (`process_exit_code_unavailable`, `process_times_unavailable`, `process_creation_time_invalid`)
  is an error naming that code, never `Missing`, so its lock is kept ("owner liveness could not be
  proven"). Pid 0 is `process_id_reserved`.
- **The host:** `dns_host_name`, `GetComputerNameExW` with `ComputerNameDnsHostname`: the host-name
  part of the computer's full DNS name, which `hostname.exe` prints. It is trimmed and lowercased
  as before, so `host_identity` keeps its text.
- **The owner token's seed:** `fill_system_random`, `BCryptGenRandom` with the system-preferred
  generator (windows-sys feature `Win32_Security_Cryptography` for host-metrics), 32 bytes as
  before; the owner token is still the SHA-256 of seed, pid, sequence and time, 64 hex digits. The
  seed is not a fact of the system, but it started PowerShell under the same deadline, so leaving
  it would have left the same timeout.

The probe runner and its constants (`WINDOWS_PROBE_TIMEOUT` among them) are gone: no probe is left
for them. `probe_process` keeps its answers; it now converts the creation probe's. Linux and the
other Unix systems are unchanged (`/proc`, `ps`, `hostname`, `/dev/urandom`).

**Interfaces.** None raised ([component-interfaces.md](component-interfaces.md)): the result lock
is no listed interface, its file and every member's text are unchanged, and the new host-metrics
functions are Runtime-internal. `runtime-outcomes`: the codes the process read can name are
host-metrics' existing ones.

**At deploy.** Environment detection no longer starts PowerShell or `hostname.exe` to read the lock
holder's identity, and no longer fails with "process inspector … timed out" on a loaded machine.
Locks written by an earlier build are read as before. The Windows error texts of the three reads
change (for example "process inspector could not read PID <pid>: process_query_refused; …").
**Rollback** (below 0.12.51): the PowerShell readers return with their deadline; the lock file and
its tokens are the same either way.

| # | Shape | Kind | Code slice | First writer | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FLK10-1 | `actingcommand_host_metrics::probe_process_creation`, `ProcessCreationProbe` (`Running { created_at_windows_100ns }`, `NotRunning`, `Unknown(Code)`) | Runtime-internal interface | FLK-10 | — | `since` 0.12.51; `probe_process`'s query and codes; `process_probe_unsupported` off Windows |
| FLK10-2 | `actingcommand_host_metrics::dns_host_name` | Runtime-internal interface | FLK-10 | — | `GetComputerNameExW`, `ComputerNameDnsHostname`; the operating system's error; `Unsupported` off Windows |
| FLK10-3 | `actingcommand_host_metrics::fill_system_random` | Runtime-internal interface | FLK-10 | — | `BCryptGenRandom`, `BCRYPT_USE_SYSTEM_PREFERRED_RNG`; a failure names its NTSTATUS; `Unsupported` off Windows |
| FLK10-4 | the environment-detection lock's holder identity on Windows (`crates/lab/src/env_detection/lock.rs`) | Runtime-internal behaviour | FLK-10 | lab | `env-result-lock.v2` and the text of `host_identity`, `process_start_token` and `owner_token` unchanged; `crates/lab` gains the Windows-only workspace dependency `actingcommand-host-metrics`, no new third-party crate |

Tests (exec gate row "#71 FLK-10"):
`env_detection::lock::tests::flk10_windows_holder_start_is_read_from_the_system_as_dotnet_ticks`.
Removed with the runner it tested: `env_detection::lock::tests::windows_probe_timeout_terminates_helper`
(in no gate row). The other tests of the lock are unchanged; none pinned the PowerShell reader's
text (the Windows fixture `sleeping_child` still starts `powershell.exe`, as a process to kill).

### 1.295 Slice RD-BUDGET-1 (0.12.51): the declaration validator counts a file once per run (#428; on 11-10 a full scan of one resource repository's `main`, 441 pack JSON files, counted 114.25 MiB and was refused with "declaration read budget exceeded", although the distinct files it reads come to 25.76 MiB; the coordinator's ruling of 11-10, not Alice's words: the bound is on what a run reads from disk, so a file counts once; read-only triage `rd-1110/validator-failures-triage.md`, part A; coordinator work order `rd-1110/brief-rd-budget1.md`)

[resource-declarations.md](resource-declarations.md) (the adapter's bounds) and
[package-reference.md](package-reference.md) (the read bounds of `maintenance.json`) are the
contract. 1.295 is the next free number on main `8d9b4f73`, and the name RD-BUDGET-1 was free. No
persisted ledger shape, wire shape, configuration key, outcome code or vocabulary is new or
changed.

**Why.** `actinglab resource validate`, the declarations step of `resource verify` and
`operation` share one reader, `DeclarationReader`, which bounds what one run reads to 64 MiB in
total (`MAX_TOTAL_BYTES`). It counted every read, a repeated read of the same file too, and a
selection-policy document is checked by checking its whole task again: the task, every policy
the task names and the operations' `resources.json`, then the policy once more. The count grew
with the square of the policies in a task, so a full scan was refused long before it had read
64 MiB of distinct files. A run of the Runtime is not affected: it loads a pack through another
reader, with per-pack bounds.

**What.** The reader keeps each file's bytes for the rest of the run, by its repository-relative
path as `read_files` spells it, and counts a path against the total only at its first read. A
later read of the path answers the kept bytes and reads nothing from disk, under that read's own
limit (a document read again under a policy's 512 KiB limit is still held to it, refused as "not
a bounded regular file" as before). The first read of a file that takes the count past the total
is refused as before: `resource_declaration_invalid`, `<file>: declaration read budget exceeded`,
naming that file. The 16 MiB document limit, the policy limit, the 1 MiB path-list bound, the
4096-path bound and the 64 MiB total are unchanged, and so are the files a check reads, the order
of the checks and the count of a relative path list. The total stays a constant of the program;
the reader takes it through a constructor (`DeclarationReader::with_total`) only so that a test
can set a lower one, never from configuration or the command line.

**Answer members.** `read_bytes` keeps its name and its meaning, the bytes the run read from disk,
which is now also what is counted: in the answer of `resource validate`
(`actinglab.resource-declarations.v1`) and of `operation`, and in the `declarations` counts of
`resource verify`'s report. Its value falls for a run that reads a file more than once (such a
file now counts once); a run that reads each file once answers as before. `read_files` and every
other member are unchanged. Checking each task once per run would save the repeated parsing too;
it is not done here.

**Interfaces.** None raised ([component-interfaces.md](component-interfaces.md)): no pack format
changes (`package`), the answers of actinglab's commands are no listed interface, and
`runtime-outcomes` sees the same code and message.

**At deploy.** `actinglab resource validate`, `resource verify` and `operation` count a file once
per run. A full scan that was refused only because the same files were counted again now passes.
No pack, no run and no answer shape changes. **Rollback** (below 0.12.51): the reader counts every
read again, and such a scan is refused again; nothing else changes.

| RDB1-1 | the total read bound of `DeclarationReader` (`apps/actinglab/src/resource_declarations.rs`) | tool behaviour | RD-BUDGET-1 | — | `since` 0.12.51; 64 MiB over the distinct files a run reads, each counted at its first read and kept; a later read reads nothing from disk; the refusal is unchanged |
| RDB1-2 | `read_bytes` of `resource validate`'s and `operation`'s answers and of `resource verify`'s `declarations` counts | answer member, same name and meaning | RD-BUDGET-1 | — | the bytes read from disk, each file once; smaller than before only for a run that reads a file more than once |

existing test changed: none pinned a repeated count (`gate_rc2_a11` and the consumer goldens read
each file once, and `gate_rv1` asks only for a `read_bytes` above zero).

### 1.296 Slice UNSET-2 (0.12.51): a scheduled run cut by a stop after it released its own lease is settled at the next start (#428; production: one scheduled dispatch of 10-26, cut by the 19:12 stop after its failure path wrote the run's own `lease.released` (effect `performed`) and inputs and before its terminal, open ever since and reported by every start, first as `policy_settlement_dispatch_unsettled`, from 0.12.28 as `policy_settlement_dispatch_left_open`, both with `failure_code` `scheduled_execution_recovery_interruption_conflict`; UNSET-1's row: "settling it is UNSET-2, which changes #670's rule"; the coordinator's ruling of 11-10, not Alice's words: the next start settles it, once, and records who closed it and why, with no new request kind and no protocol revision; read-only survey `rd-1110/leftopen-survey.md`; coordinator work order `rd-1110/brief-unset2.md`; fix round 1 after the review `rd-1110/review-1564-findings.md`, the coordinator's rulings L1 to L4 of 11-10, not Alice's words: `rd-1110/brief-unset2-fix1.md`; fix round 2 after the first run of its host tests and the second review `rd-1110/review-1564-fix1-findings.md`: `rd-1110/brief-unset2-fix2.md`)

This section changes #670's rule R4 and its pin, and the order in which the host takes a pair's
latest completed run. [scheduling/README.md](scheduling/README.md) ("Failures (#419)") and the
catalog entries of `policy_settlement_dispatch_closed`, `policy_settlement_dispatch_unsettled`,
`policy_settlement_dispatch_left_open` and `scheduled_execution_recovery_interruption_conflict`
are the contract. 1.296 is the next free number: Runtime PR #1565 takes 1.295 (fix round 1
renumbered this section, first written as 1.295 on main `8d9b4f73`). No persisted ledger shape,
wire shape, configuration key, location or vocabulary is new or changed; one outcome code is new.
LN4-6, LN4-7 and LN4-8 (§1.184) are corrected in place.

**Why.** The ledger's guarded check of a recovered settlement (`append_recovered_policy_execution`)
settled a run with no terminal as interrupted from its one run-linked release only when the run
had no effect or input record, unless the release was the one the start recovered
(`not_performed`) or the lease ended another way: R4 as pinned by
`interrupted_policy_execution_recovery_rejects_effects_and_duplicate_release`, effect half. A run
whose own failure path wrote its release (`performed`) and which a stop cut before its execution
record had no settlement the Runtime could derive but the interrupted one, and the ledger refused
it (`scheduled_execution_recovery_interruption_conflict`) at every start. No operation closes a
dispatch and nothing expires it, so the dispatch stayed open: its (task, instance) pair counted as
in flight (its eligibility age pinned to 0, no aging in rank, a score-deferred candidate never
reaching `defer_aging_cap_ms`, no clock-slot planning records) and every start wrote the Warning
again. Had the stop left no run-linked release, the start would have recovered one and settled the
same run as interrupted, inputs and all.

**The rule (changes R4).** A run with no terminal whose one run-linked release is its own (effect
`performed`) is settled as interrupted (`policy_settlement_interrupted`, Severe, the task paused,
no retry, runtime 0, timed at the release) also when it has effect or input records, the way the
recovered `not_performed` release is accepted; the check no longer reads those records. A run that
has a terminal is still settled only from it (an interrupted settlement of it is refused, here
`scheduled_execution_recovery_failure_conflict`, or `..._interruption_conflict` when its lease end
was recovered or ended otherwise); more than one run-linked release is still refused
(`scheduled_execution_recovery_release_not_unique`); nothing else of the check changes. The replay
of a settlement already recorded takes the same rule, so a start cut between the execution record
and the completion completes it.

**Who closed it and why.** The start's settlement does not change; with the check changed, the
next start closes the dispatch once with the records a settlement writes (`policy.execution_recorded`,
`policy.dispatch_completed`, Scheduler). When an earlier start had refused the run (its first
`policy_settlement_dispatch_unsettled` record, read by the run's link index before the
settlement's write), the start then records one `runtime.failed`
`policy_settlement_dispatch_closed` (Info, new) under the run's links: `operation`
`reconcile_policy_outcomes` (the start's settlement) and `failure_code` the earlier refusal's code
(when that record named an unregistered spelling, the earlier record's outcome is a `note` link
instead). A later start finds the dispatch settled and writes no settlement, no Warning and no
second record for it. Two windows (fix round 1):

- A stop that cuts the settling start between the execution record and the completion leaves the
  completion to the next start (its pending completions, `reconcile_policy_dispatches`). That
  start reads the run's earlier refusal by the completion's run links and records
  `policy_settlement_dispatch_closed` itself, after the completion. Two inexact details stay
  (fix round 2 leaves them, as neither is a one-line change): that record's `operation` is
  `reconcile_policy_outcomes` there too, though the step that completes the dispatch is
  `reconcile_policy_dispatches` (the operation would have to be carried per late settlement);
  and it reads the earlier refusal through the completion's sequence, where every replay reads
  through the execution record's (the journal does not keep that sequence). The two reads differ
  only for a `policy_settlement_dispatch_unsettled` record between the execution record and the
  completion, which only a start that refused the completion writes; the second review found
  that unreachable, since a refused completion stays refused. No test cuts a start there: the
  execution record and the completion are appended by one ledger command
  (`reconcile_scheduled_policy_settlement`), so the cut needs a hook inside the ledger's
  settlement path, not one of the host's `fail_next_…_for_test` hooks.
- A stop that cuts a start between the completion and that record leaves the record unwritten, and
  no later start writes it (none scans the ledger for it). The record can be missing after such a
  cut; the settlement (`policy.execution_recorded`) and the completion
  (`policy.dispatch_completed`) are the lasting records.

**The late settlement is not a failure of its pair.** In ledger order it comes after the later
runs of its (task, instance) pair, when there are any ("R" below; "N" when there are none). Today's
rule for an interruption is `interruption_lifted_by_restart`: the first interruption of a pair in a
row is recorded as its failure (Severe, the task paused) and lifted by the restart that recorded
it; a second one in a row keeps the pair paused until its package changes. Applied to a late
settlement that would make the old run the pair's latest failure in both cases, would end a later
run's backoff or failure streak and owed rerun in R, and would pause the pair when its latest run
before it was also an interruption. So an interrupted settlement of a run an earlier start refused
leaves the decision memory as it was: no failure streak, pause, backoff or retry round, not the
pair's latest failure, no owed rerun ended, its admission's counts as the admission took them. The
record is checked against the settlement it must be as any record. The start decides it by the
run's `policy_settlement_dispatch_unsettled` record before the settlement's write; every replay of
the execution record (the decision memory's re-alignment, a load, a seeding start, a read on
demand, the test replay) reads the same record before the execution's sequence, so the held and
the replayed state agree. Fix round 1 (the review found that wherever the host took a pair's
latest completed run by completion order, a late completion stood for the pair in R, and that
then every start after the settling one failed with `runtime_fact_stale`; the coordinator's
rulings):

- **Admission order (L1).** Wherever the host takes a pair's latest completed dispatch or run, it
  takes the latest in admission order, `(admitted_sequence, intent_sequence)`, the order
  `fold_settlements_by` and the task snapshots already used: the latest completed dispatch a
  pair's value record names (`journal_records_of`, LN4-7) and the previous completed dispatch a
  completion counts its failures from (`failures_through`); the outcome-key snapshot and the runs
  whose authoritative outcomes a start or the online reconciliation recovers
  (`outcome_key_snapshot`, `latest_completed_policy_runs`, which the dispatch's projection checks
  against each other); and `actingd suspended`, which orders a pair's executions by their dispatch
  intents' sequences. A pair runs one dispatch at a time on its instance, so for every other
  completion this is the order it completed in. The other readers of a pair's runs order by
  admission already (the task snapshots, the settlement facts, the remedy journal, the dispatch
  clocks) or hold one run per pair (`recover_authoritative_policy_outcomes`, whose sort by
  completion sequence runs over pairs).
- **Not a failure, anywhere (L2).** A late completion keeps the failure count of its pair's latest
  other completed dispatch in admission order instead of adding one (`failures_through`; the
  journal's flag `settled_late`, set where the execution is committed or replayed, from the same
  record), and the task snapshot of an executed late run not yet completed adds none either
  (`fold_settlements_by`). So neither the task snapshot's `failure_streak` (the journal's
  `failures`, failed runs in a row) nor the decision memory's failure streak (its `count`, the
  same error in a row) counts the late run; they are two different counters, and each stays
  what it was without the late run. The snapshot's validation allows a failed latest run with an
  unchanged count. `actingd suspended` leaves a late settlement out of its pair's executions (an
  interrupted execution whose run has a `policy_settlement_dispatch_unsettled` record before it):
  the pair's failures in a row and its latest failure are those without it.
- **What stays visible (L3).** The run itself reads as interrupted. In N it is the pair's latest
  run in admission order: its task snapshot shows it, failed, with the pair's failures in a row as
  before, and the pair's outcome is missing, as after any interrupted latest run; its settlement
  facts are recorded, newer than the pair's earlier ones. In R the later run stays the pair's
  latest everywhere, and no settlement fact of the pair is recorded again.
- **The cut run's retry round (fix round 2).** A pair's normal admission opens its retry round
  (`commit_admission`; an immediate rerun opens none), so in N the round the cut run's own
  admission opened is part of the pair's failure state before the settlement, and it is the
  same after it, as L2 asks (the first run of the host tests found it there; the test had
  expected none). In R the later run's admission replaced it, and the later run's success ended
  that round or its failure kept it. The round never delays anything: it is read only to offer
  and to admit an immediate rerun (R22, `immediate_retry_pairs`), and only while the pair's
  failure state is a `retry_scheduled` failure with a failure identity, the instant lies in the
  round's own activity window (before its `until_unix_ms`, that window's end) and the round's
  budgets leave room. The late settlement sets no failure state, so the round offers and admits
  exactly what it did before the settlement; the round of a run cut on an earlier day, as
  production's of 10-26, offers nothing, since its window has ended. It ends as any round does:
  at the pair's next success, at its next normal admission (which opens the next round), when a
  later admission or settlement on its instance finds its budget spent, or when an admission
  refuses an immediate rerun (`policy_retry_round_ended`); past its window it stays in the value
  record, inert, until then.
- **The journal keeps a late completion until a value record follows it.** The value record of a
  task of the remedy journal (one that declares a remedy or provides a capability) names every
  admitted run the journal keeps (LN4-7), so a late settlement of such a task after more than 64
  later admitted runs of its pair completes outside the journal's bound (LN4-8), while the
  decision memory's re-alignment still applies its records, which lie after the value records'
  position (LN4-6). For any other task the journal a start loads holds the pair's open
  dispatches, its latest completed one and the records after the value records, so the late
  completion stays inside the bound however many runs the pair had. Once the value records are
  loaded or seeded, the journal keeps a dispatch completed after their position until a value
  record follows it (`prune_journal`), so the re-alignment finds it; the next pruning after that
  record drops it. `journal_answers_at` answers as before: the late run completed after the
  earliest completion the bound keeps.

**Starts after it (L4).** Every start of 0.12.51 after the settling one loads the pair's value
record and takes from it the pair's latest completed run in admission order (in R the later run,
with its own failure count), so the journal it loads, its task snapshots, the settlement facts it
derives again (`record_policy_settlement_facts_on_start`) and its outcome-key snapshot read that
run: it starts, records no settlement fact for the pair, and a rule on the task's outcome decides
as before the settlement.

**A rollback (corrected in fix round 2, after the second review).** No shape changed and no
member was added, so a start of an earlier version (v0.12.50, v0.12.49) loads the same value
records and facts, reads the closed record as a code it does not act on, and starts and schedules
in every case; no interface is raised ([component-interfaces.md](component-interfaces.md): a
revision rises when an older peer can no longer work with the change). What it reads:

- In N, and in R for a task outside the remedy journal, the value record names the pair's latest
  run in admission order (in R the later run alone), and v0.12.50 reads it as the pair's latest,
  as 0.12.51 does.
- In R for a task of the remedy journal (one that declares a remedy or provides a capability),
  the value record also names the late completion (LN4-7). v0.12.50 takes a pair's latest
  completed run by completion order (`outcome_key_snapshot`, `latest_completed_policy_runs`), so
  it reads the late run as the pair's latest: the pair's outcome key is missing until the pair's
  next completion, and a rule on that outcome decides as after an interrupted latest run until
  then. Its failure count stays right (the late completion kept the later run's count). This is
  v0.12.50's own completion-order rule meeting an out-of-order completion in the ledger, not a
  changed shape.
- A late completion's `failures` leaves the late run out (LN4-7); v0.12.50 reads it as the pair's
  count through that dispatch, which is the pair's count without the late run.

The edge: a settling start of 0.12.51 cut after the settlement records and before its value
records, followed by a start of v0.12.50. That start's re-alignment commits the late execution
under its older rule, as the pair's latest failure, and its value record then names the late
dispatch as the pair's latest completed one (by completion order; alone, for a task outside the
remedy journal). That start starts. In R the start after it fails with `runtime_fact_stale`,
which is fatal, on either version: it loads only the late run and records that run's settlement
facts over the later run's newer ones; only a run the pair completes in between avoids it. In N
it does not fail. Hence the operating rule: after a deploy of 0.12.51, do not go back to v0.12.50
before one start of 0.12.51 has completed after the settlement.

**The online path.** The changed check also serves the online settlement of abandoned and inactive
runs (`reconcile_scheduled_policy_outcomes_for` with no start, #427-A). A run with its own
`performed` release and no terminal reaches it only through `inactive_policy_settlements`, and only
when the run has no effect or input record and its release carries its dispatch intent's links;
the ledger accepted that shape before this slice too, and the run is settled there as an ordinary,
fresh interruption. With an effect or input record no online path takes it
(`policy_run_effect_started`; the abandoned-lane path waits on a run-linked release that does not
record `not_performed`), and the next start settles it as a fresh interruption. A run a start
refused to settle stays quarantined, out of the pending settlements, for the life of that host, so
the online path never meets a late settlement. Nothing changes there.

**After it.** The dispatch is completed: the pair is no longer in flight, its eligibility age runs
again and its clock-slot planning records are written again, and later starts record nothing for
it. The other writer of `policy_settlement_dispatch_left_open` (a pending scheduled dispatch whose
instance is no longer configured, or whose lease ended in more than one way) is unchanged, and a
run the check still refuses is reported as before (UNSET-1).

**Interfaces.** None raised ([component-interfaces.md](component-interfaces.md)), every range as
main declares it: `ledger`: the check's rule is not a record shape, and a new code is not a shape
change (its row: a new code "raises no revision"); the value records (register L7, LN4-7) keep
their shape, and the latest completed dispatch they name is the pair's latest run in admission
order, as every other completion's is (a remedy-journal pair's record in R also names the late
completion, which v0.12.50 reads by its own completion order: "A rollback" above; an older peer
still starts and schedules, so no revision rises); `runtime-outcomes`: one new code in the
catalog only; `runtime-client` and the protocol: no request kind, no member. No configuration key.

**At deploy.** At the first start of 0.12.51 a dispatch left open by a run cut after its own
release is settled once (`policy.execution_recorded`, `policy.dispatch_completed`) and recorded as
closed (`policy_settlement_dispatch_closed`, with `failure_code`
`scheduled_execution_recovery_interruption_conflict`); the Warning of every start stops.
Production has one such dispatch, of 10-26; the pair's failure state stays as it was. Later
starts of 0.12.51 read the pair's latest run in admission order (the later run when the pair ran
since) and start as before. A **rollback** to v0.12.50 keeps the settlement, reports nothing for
the closed dispatch and starts; it reads the pair's latest run in admission order too, except for
a task that declares a remedy or provides a capability when the pair ran since: v0.12.50 then
reads the late run as the pair's latest, and the pair's outcome key is missing until the pair's
next completion. The edge: a settling start of 0.12.51 cut after the settlement and before its
value records, followed by a start of v0.12.50: that start starts, and when the pair ran since,
the start after it fails with `runtime_fact_stale`, on either version, unless the pair completed
a run in between. Operating rule: after a deploy of 0.12.51, do not go back to v0.12.50 before
one start of 0.12.51 has completed after the settlement.

### 1.297 Slice CI-OCR-1 (0.12.52): a script fills or verifies a CPU vision root from the tool registry (#428; the coordinator's ruling of 2026-11-10 on board #428, not Alice's words: CI runs real OCR on the CPU, under six conditions, and its logic lives once, in the Runtime; coordinator work order `rd-1110/brief-ci-ocr-1.md`; fix round 1, the license files get pins so that a complete root is verified without a fetch: `rd-1110/brief-ci-ocr-1-fix1.md`)

[vision-model-folders.md](vision-model-folders.md) (section "Vision root") is the contract, and
`scripts/windows-tools/README.md` (section "CPU vision root") describes the script. 1.297 is the
next free number: Runtime PR #1564 took 1.296 (on main `af7e2557`), and the name CI-OCR-1 was
free. No persisted ledger shape,
wire shape, configuration key, outcome code or vocabulary is new or changed, and no Rust code
changes.

**Why.** A resource repository's frame regression runs `actinglab` on GitHub's hosted Windows
runners. A runner has no vision root, so every check that needs OCR answered
`lab_ocr_unavailable` and checked nothing. The coordinator ruled (board #428, 2026-11-10) that CI
runs real OCR on the CPU under six conditions:

1. addresses and hashes come only from the Runtime's registry
   `scripts/windows-tools/windows-tool-sources.v1.json`;
2. files go only into the runner's temporary directory and `actions/cache`;
3. the CPU execution provider;
4. the folder layout of [vision-model-folders.md](vision-model-folders.md);
5. a failed download fails the job after at most three attempts;
6. one repository's branch first.

That trial passed (1989 checks in 78 cases, twice, with and without a restored cache). It could
not use `Materialize-TaskToolCache.ps1`, which refuses to finish while a selected component is
`PendingVerification` (the registry said so of `ppocrv6-medium-onnx`), does not retry and refuses
a target directory that exists, which a restored cache always is; so it carried about 470 lines of
its own in a workflow file, which four repositories would have had to copy. **The coordinator's
ruling:** the logic lives in the Runtime, once, as a small script of its own that the resource
repositories fetch at their Tools pin's commit and call. The existing materializer keeps its
behaviour.

**What.** `scripts/windows-tools/Materialize-VisionRoot.ps1` (PowerShell 7) takes `-Destination`
(the vision root, created when missing), `-Registry` (default: the registry beside it),
`-ExecutionProvider` (only `cpu`; any other value is refused by name, before anything is read or
written) and `-Attempts` (per fetched file, default 3, at least 1). It places
`ort/onnxruntime.dll` and `ort/onnxruntime_providers_shared.dll` (the `pinned_files` of
`onnxruntime-directml-1.24.4` at their `vision_root_path`, extracted from the pinned package), that
package's `LICENSE` and `ThirdPartyNotices.txt` in `ort/licenses/onnxruntime/` (its
`placement_note`; the entry's `pinned_license_files` at their `vision_root_path`), and
`models/PP-OCRv6_medium/det.onnx`, `rec.onnx` and `keys.txt` (the three artifacts of
`ppocrv6-medium-onnx`, flat layout; the trial built the same folder). Every file has a pin. A file
with its pinned size and SHA-256 is kept and reported `verified`; any other is removed if present,
fetched to a temporary name beside it, checked and moved into place (`downloaded`); a file that
fails its check is never left in place. The package is fetched only when a file it pins (runtime or
license) did not verify, and only those files are extracted from it, so a run on a complete root
fetches nothing; a registry without `pinned_license_files` is refused by name. A failed fetch is
tried again up to `-Attempts` times, then the run fails. The script holds no address, size or hash, writes nothing
outside the destination, writes no configuration file and starts no program. Its stdout is one JSON
line, `{execution_provider, destination, registry {path, sha256}, files [{path, size, sha256, state,
component}]}`; diagnostics go to stderr; it exits 0 only when every file is in place and verified,
otherwise 1 with `Materialize-VisionRoot: FAILED: <file>: <reason>`. A hidden test-only parameter
reads the addresses from a local directory and is refused unless every address the entries name
is on the reserved host `example.invalid`.

**The registry.** `ppocrv6-medium-onnx`'s `compatibility.state` goes from `PendingVerification`
to `Ready`, with the evidence as its `reason`: the Runtime's vision pipeline runs exactly these
files in production (the coordinator compared the three SHA-256 of a production vision root with
the pins on 2026-11-10: equal), and a hosted runner's frame regression passed on them.
`ppocrv6-medium-source` keeps `PendingVerification`. `Ready` is the value of the materializer's
own vocabulary. Of the registry's readers only the new script reads this state (it requires
`Ready`): `Materialize-TaskToolCache.ps1` decides by the component's id, so a selection with
`ppocrv6-medium-onnx` is still published as `pending-verification` and fails as before, its
`pending_verification` now quoting the new reason; `Test-WindowsRemoteBuildTools.ps1` checks only
`ppocrv6-medium-source`'s state; the Rust readers (`crates/vision-ffi`, `crates/device/build.rs`,
actingd's adb pin) read other components.

**License pins (fix round 1).** Without a pin of their own the license files were compared with the
package, so every run fetched the package (12.5 MB), also on a restored cache where every pinned
file verified, and failed when that one fetch failed. `onnxruntime-directml-1.24.4` now pins them
in a new member `pinned_license_files`, in the shape of `pinned_files` (`path` in the package,
`vision_root_path`, `size`, `sha256`, and a `hash_provenance`): `LICENSE` 1094 bytes, SHA-256
`c250d6278f0b47a6439fb7592b08b58a55eb9f535aa49a1db63211c3f982b674`, and `ThirdPartyNotices.txt`
331175 bytes, SHA-256 `fb0af774b4d7cffc5b9d046f2aaeade2f37df2f80abf8033c95dfffcc77a8866`, read
from the pinned package by this script on a GitHub-hosted Windows runner on 2026-11-11 (two runs,
identical). A member of its own keeps `pinned_files` the runtime pin of
`crates/vision-ffi/src/runtime_pin.rs`: its logic test (`gate_407_gpu1a`) holds the three pinned
runtime files equal to the `pinned_files` of the two components, both ways, and stays true
unchanged; `Test-WindowsRemoteBuildTools.ps1`, which freezes two `pinned_files` of the entry, too.

**Interfaces.** None raised ([component-interfaces.md](component-interfaces.md)): the registry is
a tool source, the script's output line is no listed interface, and no Runtime program changes.

**At deploy.** Nothing changes in a deployed Runtime: the script and the registry are repository
files that a resource repository's CI reads at its Tools pin's commit. 0.12.52 is the first release
that carries them. **Rollback** (a Tools pin below 0.12.52): the pin has no such script, and a
resource repository's CI that calls it fails.

| # | Shape | Kind | Code slice | First writer | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CIO-1 | `scripts/windows-tools/Materialize-VisionRoot.ps1` (`-Destination`, `-Registry`, `-ExecutionProvider cpu`, `-Attempts`) and its stdout line | tool script | CI-OCR-1 | — | `since` 0.12.52; the one implementation a resource repository's CI calls; seven files, each `verified` or `downloaded`, each with a pin; the package fetched only for a file of it that did not verify, so a complete root is verified without a fetch (fix round 1) |
| CIO-2 | `windows-tool-sources.v1.json` `ppocrv6-medium-onnx` `compatibility` `{state: Ready, reason}` | tool source | CI-OCR-1 | — | was `PendingVerification`; `ppocrv6-medium-source` unchanged; `Materialize-TaskToolCache.ps1` unchanged and still pending for this component |
| CIO-3 | `scripts/windows-tools/Test-MaterializeVisionRoot.ps1`, run by the step `Test Windows artifact tooling` of the Windows exact-SHA build | test | CI-OCR-1 | — | no network: a made-up registry on `example.invalid`, made-up files in a local directory, the script as a child process |
| CIO-4 | `windows-tool-sources.v1.json` `onnxruntime-directml-1.24.4` `pinned_license_files[]` `{path, vision_root_path, size, sha256, hash_provenance}` | new member of a tool source | CI-OCR-1 (fix round 1) | — | `LICENSE` and `ThirdPartyNotices.txt` at `ort/licenses/onnxruntime/`; `Materialize-VisionRoot.ps1` requires it and refuses a registry without it by name; `pinned_files` and the runtime pin unchanged; no other reader |

Tests (`Test-MaterializeVisionRoot.ps1`, not a Rust gate): `fresh-fill`,
`second-run-fetches-nothing` (fix round 1: its test source is an empty directory, so any fetch,
of the package or of a model file, would fail the run; it exits 0 with every file `verified` and
none written again, and says the package was not fetched), `one-license-file-fetched` (fix round
1: `LICENSE` missing, then `ThirdPartyNotices.txt` changed; the package is fetched from a source
that holds only the package and only that file is placed, `downloaded`, the others `verified` and
unwritten), `license-differs-from-pin-fails` (fix round 1: a package whose `LICENSE` has the
pinned length and other bytes fails the run, naming the file and its pin, and the file is not left
in place), `wrong-hash-fails-after-attempts`, `missing-registry-entry`,
`provider-other-than-cpu`. `second-run-fetches-nothing` replaces the first round's
`second-run-only-verifies`, which still served the package to the license files' comparison. No
test outside this slice changed: `Test-WindowsRemoteBuildTools.ps1` pins only
`ppocrv6-medium-source`'s state and the entry's two `pinned_files`, and `gate_407_gpu1a` reads
only `pinned_files`.

## 2 Removals and changes of option 丙 (M-PKG §4.3, §4.4)

Deleted outright, no old-version reader (M-PKG §7). The slice named deletes the field and its
readers in one PR.

| PKG-S2 | `PackageAdmitted.package_sha256` (keep `package_label`, `task_label`); `EntryRecoveryPackageAdmitted/Completed/Failed.package_sha256` → `package_label`; effective configuration `EntryRecovery.package_sha256` → `package_label`; `TaskSelectionPolicy.package_sha256`; Lab declared refusal `declared_package`, `verified_package` → optional `package_label`; Lab evidence `expected_package_sha256` / `actual_package_sha256` → `package_label`; `EvidencePackage.sha256`; OCR comparison report `truth_set_sha256` and its runtime-client reader; run status `package_ref` / `recovery_packages` → `package_label` / `recovery_package_labels`; run summary digest checks; reading facts' `resource_bundle_hash` = SHA-256(`"package:" + package_id`) (shape unchanged). **Done (PKG-S2):** all of them, §1.31 P2-1 to P2-11; also the run summary's `package_digest` (now `package_label`), the in-package `sha256` keys made optional and ignored (D5), and request replay by `package_label` (a recorded label must be the request's package's, or a configured prerequisite package's or the recovery binding's `package_id`, each admitted again) |
| PKG-S3 | `DispatchIntent.package_digest` (payload and storage equality); `ProcedureBinding.package_digest`; `binding_digest` tuple v3 = (`procedure_ref`, `operation_id`, `yield_points`); `PausedOn.package_digest` → content hashes parsed from the failure identity; suspension report members `paused_hash_prefix`, `current_hash_prefix`, `lifts_when: content_hash_changes`, `lifted_by: main_hash \| layer:<n> \| restart`. **Done (PKG-S3):** all of them, §1.47 P3-1 to P3-6; also the run identity check by path (the request's path against the binding's location) and `lifted[].effective` `next_evaluation` in place of `pending_restart` |
| PKG-S4 | IPC `expected_sha256` of `PackageDebugRequest`, `ContainedTaskRecoveryBinding`, `ContainedTaskRequest`, the Lab operation, online observation and saved-artifact OCR requests; `PackageDebugSummary.verified_sha256`; configuration `startup_package.expected_sha256`, `prerequisite_packages[].package_digest`, `policy.procedure_manifest[].package_digest`, the resource declaration's `package_digest`. **Done (PKG-S4):** all of them, §1.55 P4-1 to P4-6; also the actingctl, MCP and actinglab digest flags and arguments, the `takeover` hint's `--package-ref`, the `package validate` / `lab validate` digest outputs, the dry-run record's `package_label` and the identity check of a configured prerequisite package (D7) |
| PKG-S5 | bundle v4 `packs[] {package_id, server, entry_task_id, path = "packs/<package_id>", file_count, byte_count}` (the bundle-level maintenance declaration stays, coordinator 10-12); `RecordingArtifact.digest` / `.sha256` → `package_id`; `PackageRef`, `ContentDirectory` and the `sha256:` serializers. **Done (PKG-S5):** all of them, §1.64 P5-1 to P5-8; also bundle v4's optional `tables` (M-357a TB12) and its reserved `package_id` `tables`, the Lab output named `<package_id>.<ext>` and replaced in place (D9), `actinglab package digest` and the authoring receipt's `package_sha256` |

**Failure identity, format v2** (PKG-S3, M-PKG §3.4):
`<base>~v2~k<K>~m<I><H>[~p<I><H>]…[~r<Kh><I><H>]~f<F>`. `I` = the first 8 hex digits of the
SHA-256 of `package_id`; `H` = the first 12 hex digits of the package's content hash measured at
suspension (`x` when it could not be measured, D18); the `pre:<digest>` scope becomes `pre:<I>`.
A v1 string is not read. The content hash is measured only at suspension and at lift checks
(never on admission) and is stored only inside this string (the failure record's
`failure_identity`, §1.15 Q1) and in SR-3's suspension event key
`actual_digest`. A lift check of one package runs at most once per
`scheduling.suspension.lift_check_min_interval_ms` (§5).

### 1.243 Slice R-0b2 (0.12.36): `activity` on the instance rows of `actingctl overview` and `ac_overview` (R-0b, §1.238, fills `Status.activity`, and `actingctl status` prints it, but the overview's rows are built member by member and did not carry it, so the agents that run the devices could not see what an instance does now; coordinator work order `rd-1031/brief-r0b2.md`)

[runtime-interface.md](runtime-interface.md) (the `overview` command row, the `ac_overview` tool row
and the output budget's "never cut" list) is the contract. The number 1.243 is the coordinator's;
§1.241 and §1.242 are in flight in the same release. Nothing persisted, no wire shape of the
Runtime, no configuration key, no outcome code and no interface revision changes.

**What.** (1) Each instance row carries the optional member `activity`, `{kind, request_id?,
package_id?, since_unix_ms}`, the `RuntimeInstanceStatus.activity` of the overview's one Status read
as the Runtime answered it, and no member while the instance has none. No Runtime request is added
and nothing is read from the ledger for it. A row has it whichever other reads fail, since the
Status read is the one the overview cannot do without. (2) MCP's output budget never cuts it; the
members cut and their order are unchanged. (3) The tool's description and result schema say so.

**What changes live.** The rows of a busy instance grow by the member (about 150 bytes for a run), so
an overview near the budget starts cutting a little earlier, in the order it already has.

**Rollback** (to 0.12.35). Nothing persisted: the member disappears from the rows.

| # | Shape | Kind | Code slice | First writer | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R0B2-1 | `instances[].activity?` | `actingctl overview` / `ac_overview` answer | R-0b2 | R-0b2 | `since` 0.12.36; from the one Status read; never cut |

### 5.1 Capacity of `config.parameters`

`config.parameters` is one runtime fact whose `record_list` holds at most 256 rows (M387 §5.9,
`runtime_fact.rs`). One row per key; list, object and decimal keys are one row each.

| Rows | Count |
|---|---|
| today (`apps/actingd/src/config/manifest.rs` at 706ead94) | about 55, plus 2 per instance |
| `ledger_observer.*` | 35 (21, #411 A51's two, P0-LO's two, one each of #422 LN-5, LN-TUNE and LN-8, #422 LN-9's three, #422 LN-WS's two and #422 LN-7c Q's two) |
| `recovery_ladder.*`, `host_claims.*` | 16 (and #411 A38's two, #411 B37's four, #411 A35's seven) |
| `performance.*`, `execution.defaults.*` | about 100 (some replace today's `performance_monitor.*` / `performance_control.*` rows) |
| `scheduling.*` (recognition, rerun, cost_commit, blackout, feature_lock, not_run, pack_admission, fact_refresh, suspension, random_delay) | 32 |
| Lab options | 2 |
| per instance: `recognition_package`, `start_emulator`, `scheduling.random_delay.*` (#405) | 5 per instance |
| **total** | **about 226 + 7 per instance** (three instances ≈ 247; five ≈ 261) |

The total stayed under 256 for up to eight instances (255 rows) before #405's three per-instance
keys (SR-1, §1.23); with them it passes 256 at five instances. So D1b implements the split (coordinator ruling, 2026-10-12): `config.parameters`
becomes one `config.parameters.<section>` fact per section (M387 §5.9), written and read that way
from D1b on, and each section fact holds at most 256 rows.
